rules.title: Rare Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
rules.description: Detects uncommon processes creating remote threads.
falsepositives: This rule is best put in testing first in order to create a baseline that reflects the data in your environment.

rules.title: HackTool - CACTUSTORCH Remote Thread Creation
rules.description: Detects remote thread creation from CACTUSTORCH as described in references.

rules.title: HackTool - Potential CobaltStrike Process Injection
rules.description: Detects a potential remote threat creation with certain characteristics which are typical for Cobalt Strike beacons
authors: Olaf Hartong, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Aleksey Potapov, oscd.community

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation By Uncommon Source Image
rules.description: Detects uncommon processes creating remote threads.
falsepositives: This rule is best put in testing first in order to create a baseline that reflects the data in your environment.

rules.title: Remote Thread Created In KeePass.EXE
rules.description: Detects remote thread creation in "KeePass.exe" which could indicates potential password dumping activity

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation Via PowerShell In Uncommon Target
rules.description: Detects the creation of a remote thread from a Powershell process in an uncommon target process

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation In Uncommon Target Image
rules.description: Detects uncommon target processes for remote thread creation

rules.title: Remote Thread Creation Ttdinject.exe Proxy
rules.description: Detects a remote thread creation of Ttdinject.exe used as proxy

rules.title: Password Dumper Remote Thread in LSASS
rules.description:
Detects password dumper activity by monitoring remote thread creation EventID 8 in combination with the lsass.exe process as TargetImage.
The process in field Process is the malicious program. A single execution can lead to hundreds of events.

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Via PowerShell Remote Thread
rules.description: Detects remote thread creation by PowerShell processes into "lsass.exe"

rules.title: DNS Query for Anonfiles.com Domain - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for "anonfiles.com", which is an anonymous file upload platform often used for malicious purposes

rules.title: DNS Query To Devtunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects DNS query requests to Devtunnels domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Devtunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: DNS Query To Ufile.io
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to "ufile.io", which was seen abused by malware and threat actors as a method for data exfiltration
falsepositives: DNS queries for "ufile" are not malicious by nature necessarily. Investigate the source to determine the necessary actions to take

rules.title: Notepad++ Updater DNS Query to Uncommon Domains
rules.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) makes DNS queries to domains that are not part of the known legitimate update infrastructure.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater mechanism or suspicious network activity that warrants further investigation.
falsepositives: Some legitimate network misconfigurations or proxy issues causing unexpected DNS queries.
Other legitimate query to official domains not listed in the filter, needing tuning.

rules.title: DNS Query Request By Regsvr32.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries initiated by "Regsvr32.exe"

rules.title: DNS Query To Remote Access Software Domain From Non-Browser App
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
falsepositives: Likely with other browser software. Apply additional filters for any other browsers you might use.

rules.title: DNS Query To MEGA Hosting Website
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for subdomains related to MEGA sharing website
falsepositives: Legitimate DNS queries and usage of Mega

rules.title: TeamViewer Domain Query By Non-TeamViewer Application
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to a TeamViewer domain only resolved by a TeamViewer client by an image that isn't named TeamViewer (sometimes used by threat actors for obfuscation)
falsepositives: Depending on the environment the rule might require some initial tuning before usage to avoid FP with third party applications

rules.title: DNS HybridConnectionManager Service Bus
rules.description: Detects Azure Hybrid Connection Manager services querying the Azure service bus service
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Azure Hybrid Connection Manager and the Azure Service Bus service

rules.title: AppX Package Installation Attempts Via AppInstaller.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries made by "AppInstaller.EXE". The AppInstaller is the default handler for the "ms-appinstaller" URI. It attempts to load/install a package from the referenced URL

rules.title: DNS Query Request By QuickAssist.EXE
rules.description: Detects DNS queries initiated by "QuickAssist.exe" to Microsoft Quick Assist primary endpoint that is used to establish a session.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Quick Assist in the environment.

rules.title: Cloudflared Tunnels Related DNS Requests
rules.description:
Detects DNS requests to Cloudflared tunnels domains.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of cloudflare tunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: DNS Server Discovery Via LDAP Query
rules.description: Detects DNS server discovery via LDAP query requests from uncommon applications

rules.title: DNS Query To Visual Studio Code Tunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects DNS query requests to Visual Studio Code tunnel domains. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Visual Studio Code tunnel will also trigger this.

rules.title: DNS Query Tor .Onion Address - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects DNS queries to an ".onion" address related to Tor routing networks

rules.title: DNS Query by Finger Utility
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries made by the finger utility, which can be abused by threat actors to retrieve remote commands for execution on Windows devices.
In one ClickFix malware campaign, adversaries leveraged the finger protocol to fetch commands from a remote server.
Since the finger utility is not commonly used in modern Windows environments, its presence already raises suspicion.
Investigating such DNS queries can also help identify potential malicious infrastructure used by threat actors for command and control (C2) communication.

rules.title: DNS Query Request To OneLaunch Update Service
rules.description:
Detects DNS query requests to "update.onelaunch.com". This domain is associated with the OneLaunch adware application.
When the OneLaunch application is installed it will attempt to get updates from this domain.

rules.title: DNS Query To AzureWebsites.NET By Non-Browser Process
rules.description: Detects a DNS query by a non browser process on the system to "azurewebsites.net". The latter was often used by threat actors as a malware hosting and exfiltration site.
falsepositives: Likely with other browser software. Apply additional filters for any other browsers you might use.

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query Indicating Kerberos Coercion via DNS Object SPN Spoofing
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries containing patterns associated with Kerberos coercion attacks via DNS object spoofing.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication from victim systems to attacker-controlled hosts.
It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack, where adversaries manipulate DNS records
to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) and redirect authentication requests like CVE-2025-33073.

rules.title: Suspicious DNS Query for IP Lookup Service APIs
rules.description: Detects DNS queries for IP lookup services such as "api.ipify.org" originating from a non browser process.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of IP lookup services such as ipify API

rules.title: Suspicious Cobalt Strike DNS Beaconing - Sysmon
rules.description: Detects a program that invoked suspicious DNS queries known from Cobalt Strike beacons

rules.title: DNS Query To Common Malware Hosting and Shortener Services
rules.description:
Detects DNS queries to domains commonly used by threat actors to host malware payloads or redirect through URL shorteners.
These include platforms like Cloudflare Workers, TryCloudflare, InfinityFree, and URL shorteners such as tinyurl and lihi.cc.
Such DNS activity can indicate potential delivery or command-and-control communication attempts.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of these services is possible but rare in enterprise environments

rules.title: Credential Manager Access By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects suspicious processes based on name and location that access the windows credential manager and vault.
Which can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::cred" function
falsepositives: Legitimate software installed by the users for example in the "AppData" directory may access these files (for any reason).

rules.title: Access To Windows DPAPI Master Keys By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects file access requests to the the Windows Data Protection API Master keys by an uncommon application.
This can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::masterkey" function

rules.title: Microsoft Teams Sensitive File Access By Uncommon Applications
rules.description: Detects file access attempts to sensitive Microsoft teams files (leveldb, cookies) by an uncommon process.

rules.title: Access To Windows Credential History File By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects file access requests to the Windows Credential History File by an uncommon application.
This can be a sign of credential stealing. Example case would be usage of mimikatz "dpapi::credhist" function

rules.title: Suspicious File Access to Browser Credential Storage
rules.description:
Detects file access to browser credential storage paths by non-browser processes, which may indicate credential access attempts.
Adversaries may attempt to access browser credential storage to extract sensitive information such as usernames and passwords or cookies.
This behavior is often commonly observed in credential stealing malware.
authors: frack113, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems), Parth-FourCore
falsepositives: Legitimate software accessing browser data for synchronization or backup purposes.
Legitimate software installed on partitions other than "C:\"

rules.title: Access To Potentially Sensitive Sysvol Files By Uncommon Applications
rules.description: Detects file access requests to potentially sensitive files hosted on the Windows Sysvol share.

rules.title: Access To Crypto Currency Wallets By Uncommon Applications
rules.description:
Detects file access requests to crypto currency files by uncommon processes.
Could indicate potential attempt of crypto currency wallet stealing.
falsepositives: Legitimate software installed on partitions other than "C:\"

rules.title: Unusual File Modification by dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being modified by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)

rules.title: Backup Files Deleted
rules.description: Detects deletion of files with extensions often used for backup files. Adversaries may delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.

rules.title: Prefetch File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of a prefetch file which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence

rules.title: Tomcat WebServer Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of tomcat WebServer logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
falsepositives: During uninstallation of the tomcat server

rules.title: ADS Zone.Identifier Deleted By Uncommon Application
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the "Zone.Identifier" ADS by an uncommon process. Attackers can leverage this in order to bypass security restrictions that make use of the ADS such as Microsoft Office apps.
falsepositives: Other third party applications not listed.

rules.title: IIS WebServer Access Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of IIS WebServer access logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
authors: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: During uninstallation of the IIS service

rules.title: EventLog EVTX File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the event log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence

rules.title: File Deleted Via Sysinternals SDelete
rules.description: Detects the deletion of files by the Sysinternals SDelete utility. It looks for the common name pattern used to rename files.

rules.title: Unusual File Deletion by Dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected file being deleted by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)

rules.title: Exchange PowerShell Cmdlet History Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the Exchange PowerShell cmdlet History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence

rules.title: TeamViewer Log File Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the TeamViewer log files which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence

rules.title: PowerShell Console History Logs Deleted
rules.description: Detects the deletion of the PowerShell console History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence

rules.title: WScript or CScript Dropper - File
rules.description: Detects a file ending in jse, vbe, js, vba, vbs, wsf, wsh written by cscript.exe or wscript.exe

rules.title: BloodHound Collection Files
rules.description: Detects default file names outputted by the BloodHound collection tool SharpHound
falsepositives: Some false positives may arise in some environment and this may require some tuning. Add additional filters or reduce level depending on the level of noise

rules.title: HackTool - Impacket File Indicators
rules.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by Impacket.

rules.title: ADExplorer Writing Complete AD Snapshot Into .dat File
rules.description: Detects the dual use tool ADExplorer writing a complete AD snapshot into a .dat file. This can be used by attackers to extract data for Bloodhound, usernames for password spraying or use the meta data for social engineering. The snapshot doesn't contain password hashes but there have been cases, where administrators put passwords in the comment field.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of ADExplorer by administrators creating .dat snapshots

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Temporary File
rules.description:
Detects the creation of files in a specific location by ScreenConnect RMM.
ScreenConnect has feature to remotely execute binaries on a target machine. These binaries will be dropped to ":\Users\<username>\Documents\ConnectWiseControl\Temp\" before execution.

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Created
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database)

rules.title: Anydesk Temporary Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Adwind RAT / JRAT File Artifact
rules.description: Detects javaw.exe in AppData folder as used by Adwind / JRAT
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tom Ueltschi, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Get-Variable.exe Creation
rules.description:
Get-Variable is a valid PowerShell cmdlet
WindowsApps is by default in the path where PowerShell is executed.
So when the Get-Variable command is issued on PowerShell execution, the system first looks for the Get-Variable executable in the path and executes the malicious binary instead of looking for the PowerShell cmdlet.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Office Startup Folder
rules.description: Detects creation of Microsoft Office files inside of one of the default startup folders in order to achieve persistence.
authors: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Loading a user environment from a backup or a domain controller

rules.title: Office Macro File Download
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the system via an application (browser, mail client).
This can help identify potential malicious activity, such as the download of macro-enabled documents that could be used for exploitation.
falsepositives: Legitimate macro files downloaded from the internet
Legitimate macro files sent as attachments via emails

rules.title: Suspicious Outlook Macro Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a macro file for Outlook.

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon process or a process located in a suspicious directory
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Shell/Scripting Application File Write to Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detects Windows shells and scripting applications that write files to suspicious folders

rules.title: Potential Winnti Dropper Activity
rules.description: Detects files dropped by Winnti as described in RedMimicry Winnti playbook

rules.title: Files With System DLL Name In Unsuspected Locations
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a file with the ".dll" extension that has the name of a System DLL in uncommon or unsuspected locations. (Outisde of "System32", "SysWOW64", etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
falsepositives: Third party software might bundle specific versions of system DLLs.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Abusing Winsat Path Parsing - File
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using a path parsing issue in winsat.exe (UACMe 52)

rules.title: TeamViewer Remote Session
rules.description: Detects the creation of log files during a TeamViewer remote session
falsepositives: Legitimate uses of TeamViewer in an organisation

rules.title: Malicious DLL File Dropped in the Teams or OneDrive Folder
rules.description:
Detects creation of a malicious DLL file in the location where the OneDrive or Team applications
Upon execution of the Teams or OneDrive application, the dropped malicious DLL file ("iphlpapi.dll") is sideloaded

rules.title: Legitimate Application Writing Files In Uncommon Location
rules.description:
Detects legitimate applications writing any type of file to uncommon or suspicious locations that are not typical for application data storage or execution.
Adversaries may leverage legitimate applications (Living off the Land Binaries - LOLBins) to drop or download malicious files to uncommon locations on the system to evade detection by security solutions.

rules.title: Suspicious File Write to SharePoint Layouts Directory
rules.description:
Detects suspicious file writes to SharePoint layouts directory which could indicate webshell activity or post-exploitation.
This behavior has been observed in the exploitation of SharePoint vulnerabilities such as CVE-2025-49704, CVE-2025-49706 or CVE-2025-53770.

rules.title: PsExec Service File Creation
rules.description: Detects default PsExec service filename which indicates PsExec service installation and execution

rules.title: Suspicious Startup Folder Persistence
rules.description:
Detects the creation of potentially malicious script and executable files in Windows startup folders, which is a common persistence technique used by threat actors.
These files (.ps1, .vbs, .js, .bat, etc.) are automatically executed when a user logs in, making the Startup folder an attractive target for attackers.
This technique is frequently observed in malvertising campaigns and malware distribution where attackers attempt to maintain long-term access to compromised systems.
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare legitimate usage of some of the extensions mentioned in the rule

rules.title: Creation of WerFault.exe/Wer.dll in Unusual Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file named "WerFault.exe" or "wer.dll" in an uncommon folder, which could be a sign of WerFault DLL hijacking.

rules.title: Startup Folder File Write
rules.description: A General detection for files being created in the Windows startup directory. This could be an indicator of persistence.
falsepositives: FP could be caused by legitimate application writing shortcuts for example. This folder should always be inspected to make sure that all the files in there are legitimate

rules.title: Suspicious Binary Writes Via AnyDesk
rules.description:
Detects AnyDesk writing binary files to disk other than "gcapi.dll".
According to RedCanary research it is highly abnormal for AnyDesk to write executable files to disk besides gcapi.dll,
which is a legitimate DLL that is part of the Google Chrome web browser used to interact with the Google Cloud API. (See reference section for more details)

rules.title: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack
rules.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class over the network
authors: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR), wagga

rules.title: ISO File Created Within Temp Folders
rules.description: Detects the creation of a ISO file in the Outlook temp folder or in the Appdata temp folder. Typical of Qakbot TTP from end-July 2022.
falsepositives: Potential FP by sysadmin opening a zip file containing a legitimate ISO file

rules.title: PSEXEC Remote Execution File Artefact
rules.description: Detects creation of the PSEXEC key file. Which is created anytime a PsExec command is executed. It gets written to the file system and will be recorded in the USN Journal on the target system

rules.title: File Creation In Suspicious Directory By Msdt.EXE
rules.description: Detects msdt.exe creating files in suspicious directories which could be a sign of exploitation of either Follina or Dogwalk vulnerabilities

rules.title: Suspicious LNK Double Extension File Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of files with an "LNK" as a second extension. This is sometimes used by malware as a method to abuse the fact that Windows hides the "LNK" extension by default.
falsepositives: Some tuning is required for other general purpose directories of third party apps

rules.title: WMI Persistence - Script Event Consumer File Write
rules.description: Detects file writes of WMI script event consumer

rules.title: Rclone Config File Creation
rules.description: Detects Rclone config files being created

rules.title: Potential Webshell Creation On Static Website
rules.description: Detects the creation of files with certain extensions on a static web site. This can be indicative of potential uploads of a web shell.
authors: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, Thurein Oo
references: PT ESC rule and personal experience
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or developer creating legitimate executable files in a web application folder

rules.title: NTDS Exfiltration Filename Patterns
rules.description: Detects creation of files with specific name patterns seen used in various tools that export the NTDS.DIT for exfiltration.

rules.title: VsCode Powershell Profile Modification
rules.description: Detects the creation or modification of a vscode related powershell profile which could indicate suspicious activity as the profile can be used as a mean of persistence
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the profile by developers or administrators

rules.title: HackTool - RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay Secrets Dump Module Indicators
rules.description: Detects the creation of file with specific names used by RemoteKrbRelay SMB Relay attack module.

rules.title: Uncommon File Created by Notepad++ Updater Gup.EXE
rules.description:
Detects when the Notepad++ updater (gup.exe) creates files in suspicious or uncommon locations.
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater component to deliver unwanted malware or unwarranted files.
falsepositives: Custom or portable Notepad++ installations in non-standard directories.
Legitimate update processes creating temporary files in unexpected locations.

rules.title: Suspicious PROCEXP152.sys File Created In TMP
rules.description:
Detects the creation of the PROCEXP152.sys file in the application-data local temporary folder.
This driver is used by Sysinternals Process Explorer but also by KDU (https://github.com/hfiref0x/KDU) or Ghost-In-The-Logs (https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-The-Logs), which uses KDU.
falsepositives: Other legimate tools using this driver and filename (like Sysinternals). Note - Clever attackers may easily bypass this detection by just renaming the driver filename. Therefore just Medium-level and don't rely on it.

rules.title: Created Files by Microsoft Sync Center
rules.description: This rule detects suspicious files created by Microsoft Sync Center (mobsync)

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using MSConfig Token Modification - File
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using a msconfig GUI hack (UACMe 55)

rules.title: ISO or Image Mount Indicator in Recent Files
rules.description:
Detects the creation of recent element file that points to an .ISO, .IMG, .VHD or .VHDX file as often used in phishing attacks.
This can be a false positive on server systems but on workstations users should rarely mount .iso or .img files.
falsepositives: Cases in which a user mounts an image file for legitimate reasons

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using IDiagnostic Profile - File
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file by "dllhost.exe" in System32 directory part of "IDiagnosticProfileUAC" UAC bypass technique

rules.title: Writing Local Admin Share
rules.description:
Aversaries may use to interact with a remote network share using Server Message Block (SMB).
This technique is used by post-exploitation frameworks.

rules.title: NTDS.DIT Creation By Uncommon Parent Process
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "ntds.dit" (Active Directory Database) by an uncommon parent process or directory

rules.title: Potential SAM Database Dump
rules.description: Detects the creation of files that look like exports of the local SAM (Security Account Manager)

rules.title: Potential Homoglyph Attack Using Lookalike Characters in Filename
rules.description:
Detects the presence of unicode characters which are homoglyphs, or identical in appearance, to ASCII letter characters.
This is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques. Only "perfect" homoglyphs are included; these are characters that
are indistinguishable from ASCII characters and thus may make excellent candidates for homoglyph attack characters.
falsepositives: File names with legitimate Cyrillic text. Will likely require tuning (or not be usable) in countries where these alphabets are in use.

rules.title: Hijack Legit RDP Session to Move Laterally
rules.description: Detects the usage of tsclient share to place a backdoor on the RDP source machine's startup folder

rules.title: Suspicious Interactive PowerShell as SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects the creation of files that indicator an interactive use of PowerShell in the SYSTEM user context
falsepositives: PowerShell scripts running as SYSTEM user

rules.title: GoToAssist Temporary Installation Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Suspicious Files in Default GPO Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of copy of suspicious files (EXE/DLL) to the default GPO storage folder

rules.title: HackTool - Powerup Write Hijack DLL
rules.description:
Powerup tool's Write Hijack DLL exploits DLL hijacking for privilege escalation.
In it's default mode, it builds a self deleting .bat file which executes malicious command.
The detection rule relies on creation of the malicious bat file (debug.bat by default).
falsepositives: Any powershell script that creates bat files

rules.title: Wmiprvse Wbemcomn DLL Hijack - File
rules.description: Detects a threat actor creating a file named `wbemcomn.dll` in the `C:\Windows\System32\wbem\` directory over the network and loading it for a WMI DLL Hijack scenario.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Consent and Comctl32 - File
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using consent.exe and comctl32.dll (UACMe 22)

rules.title: EVTX Created In Uncommon Location
rules.description:
Detects the creation of new files with the ".evtx" extension in non-common or non-standard location.
This could indicate tampering with default EVTX locations in order to evade security controls or simply exfiltration of event log to search for sensitive information within.
Note that backup software and legitimate administrator might perform similar actions during troubleshooting.
falsepositives: An unknown bug seems to trigger the Windows "svchost" process to drop EVTX files in the "C:\Windows\Temp" directory in the form "<log_name">_<uuid>.evtx". See https://superuser.com/questions/1371229/low-disk-space-after-filling-up-c-windows-temp-with-evtx-and-txt-files

rules.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Archive
rules.description: Detects programs on a Windows system that should not write an archive to disk

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Windows Media Player - File
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using Windows Media Player osksupport.dll (UACMe 32)

rules.title: LSASS Process Dump Artefact In CrashDumps Folder
rules.description: Detects the presence of an LSASS dump file in the "CrashDumps" folder. This could be a sign of LSASS credential dumping. Techniques such as the LSASS Shtinkering have been seen abusing the Windows Error Reporting to dump said process.
falsepositives: Rare legitimate dump of the process by the operating system due to a crash of lsass

rules.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Creation Via Taskmgr.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of an "lsass.dmp" file by the taskmgr process. This indicates a manual dumping of the LSASS.exe process memory using Windows Task Manager.
falsepositives: Rare case of troubleshooting by an administrator or support that has to be investigated regardless

rules.title: Suspicious File Drop by Exchange
rules.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS

rules.title: Suspicious Deno File Written from Remote Source
rules.description:
Detects Deno writing a file from a direct HTTP(s) call and writing to the appdata folder or bringing it's own malicious DLL.
This behavior may indicate an attempt to execute remotely hosted, potentially malicious files through deno.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of deno to request a file or bring a DLL to a host

rules.title: HackTool - Potential Remote Credential Dumping Activity Via CrackMapExec Or Impacket-Secretsdump
rules.description: Detects default filenames output from the execution of CrackMapExec and Impacket-secretsdump against an endpoint.

rules.title: PCRE.NET Package Temp Files
rules.description: Detects processes creating temp files related to PCRE.NET package

rules.title: HackTool - Typical HiveNightmare SAM File Export
rules.description: Detects files written by the different tools that exploit HiveNightmare
falsepositives: Files that accidentally contain these strings

rules.title: Suspicious MSExchangeMailboxReplication ASPX Write
rules.description: Detects suspicious activity in which the MSExchangeMailboxReplication process writes .asp and .apsx files to disk, which could be a sign of ProxyShell exploitation

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec File Indicators
rules.description: Detects file creation events with filename patterns used by CrackMapExec.

rules.title: WinRAR Creating Files in Startup Locations
rules.description:
Detects WinRAR creating files in Windows startup locations, which may indicate an attempt to establish persistence by adding malicious files to the Startup folder.
This kind of behaviour has been associated with exploitation of WinRAR path traversal vulnerability CVE-2025-6218 or CVE-2025-8088.

rules.title: Suspicious Executable File Creation
rules.description:
Detect creation of suspicious executable file names.
Some strings look for suspicious file extensions, others look for filenames that exploit unquoted service paths.

rules.title: ADSI-Cache File Creation By Uncommon Tool
rules.description: Detects the creation of an "Active Directory Schema Cache File" (.sch) file by an uncommon tool.
falsepositives: Other legimate tools, which do ADSI (LDAP) operations, e.g. any remoting activity by MMC, Powershell, Windows etc.

rules.title: Self Extraction Directive File Created In Potentially Suspicious Location
rules.description:
Detects the creation of Self Extraction Directive files (.sed) in a potentially suspicious location.
These files are used by the "iexpress.exe" utility in order to create self extracting packages.
Attackers were seen abusing this utility and creating PE files with embedded ".sed" entries.

rules.title: DPAPI Backup Keys And Certificate Export Activity IOC
rules.description: Detects file names with specific patterns seen generated and used by tools such as Mimikatz and DSInternals related to exported or stolen DPAPI backup keys and certificates.

rules.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Script
rules.description:
Detects LOLBINs and applications that should not legitimately drop script files to disk.
This may indicate malware staging or abuse of a trusted binary for script-based code execution.

rules.title: RemCom Service File Creation
rules.description: Detects default RemCom service filename which indicates RemCom service installation and execution

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using NTFS Reparse Point - File
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using NTFS reparse point and wusa.exe DLL hijacking (UACMe 36)

rules.title: Octopus Scanner Malware
rules.description: Detects Octopus Scanner Malware.

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Write to System32 Tasks
rules.description: Detects the creation of tasks from processes executed from suspicious locations

rules.title: Desktop.INI Created by Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects unusual processes accessing desktop.ini, which can be leveraged to alter how Explorer displays a folder's content (i.e. renaming files) without changing them on disk.
falsepositives: Operations performed through Windows SCCM or equivalent

rules.title: VHD Image Download Via Browser
rules.description:
Detects creation of ".vhd"/".vhdx" files by browser processes.
Malware can use mountable Virtual Hard Disk ".vhd" files to encapsulate payloads and evade security controls.
falsepositives: Legitimate downloads of ".vhd" files would also trigger this

rules.title: HackTool - QuarksPwDump Dump File
rules.description: Detects a dump file written by QuarksPwDump password dumper

rules.title: Suspicious File Write to Webapps Root Directory
rules.description:
Detects suspicious file writes to the root directory of web applications, particularly Apache web servers or Tomcat servers.
This may indicate an attempt to deploy malicious files such as web shells or other unauthorized scripts.

rules.title: New Outlook Macro Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a macro file for Outlook.
falsepositives: User genuinely creates a VB Macro for their email

rules.title: Creation Exe for Service with Unquoted Path
rules.description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking vulnerable file path references.
Adversaries can take advantage of paths that lack surrounding quotations by placing an executable in a higher level directory within the path, so that Windows will choose the adversary's executable to launch.

rules.title: Wmiexec Default Output File
rules.description: Detects the creation of the default output filename used by the wmiexec tool

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Office Add-In
rules.description: Detects potential persistence activity via startup add-ins that load when Microsoft Office starts (.wll/.xll are simply .dll fit for Word or Excel).

rules.title: Cred Dump Tools Dropped Files
rules.description: Files with well-known filenames (parts of credential dump software or files produced by them) creation
falsepositives: Legitimate Administrator using tool for password recovery

rules.title: Office Macro File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new office macro files on the systems
falsepositives: Very common in environments that rely heavily on macro documents

rules.title: Potential Startup Shortcut Persistence Via PowerShell.EXE
rules.description:
Detects PowerShell writing startup shortcuts.
This procedure was highlighted in Red Canary Intel Insights Oct. 2021, "We frequently observe adversaries using PowerShell to write malicious .lnk files into the startup directory to establish persistence.
Accordingly, this detection opportunity is likely to identify persistence mechanisms in multiple threats.
In the context of Yellow Cockatoo, this persistence mechanism eventually launches the command-line script that leads to the installation of a malicious DLL"
falsepositives: Depending on your environment accepted applications may leverage this at times. It is recommended to search for anomalies inidicative of malware.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using .NET Code Profiler on MMC
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using .NET Code Profiler and mmc.exe DLL hijacking (UACMe 39)

rules.title: HackTool - Dumpert Process Dumper Default File
rules.description: Detects the creation of the default dump file used by Outflank Dumpert tool. A process dumper, which dumps the lsass process memory

rules.title: Installation of TeamViewer Desktop
rules.description: TeamViewer_Desktop.exe is create during install

rules.title: Potential File Extension Spoofing Using Right-to-Left Override
rules.description: Detects suspicious filenames that contain a right-to-left override character and a potentially spoofed file extensions.
authors: Jonathan Peters (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Filenames that contains scriptures such as arabic or hebrew might make use of this character

rules.title: Suspicious Screensaver Binary File Creation
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension

rules.title: Windows Terminal Profile Settings Modification By Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects the creation or modification of the Windows Terminal Profile settings file "settings.json" by an uncommon process.
falsepositives: Some false positives may occur with admin scripts that set WT settings.

rules.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Kirbi File Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of files created by mimikatz such as ".kirbi", "mimilsa.log", etc.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious File Creation by OpenEDR's ITSMService
rules.description:
Detects the creation of potentially suspicious files by OpenEDR's ITSMService process.
The ITSMService is responsible for remote management operations and can create files on the system through the Process Explorer or file management features.
While legitimate for IT operations, creation of executable or script files could indicate unauthorized file uploads, data staging, or malicious file deployment.
falsepositives: Authorized remote file uploads by IT administrators

rules.title: Process Monitor Driver Creation By Non-Sysinternals Binary
rules.description: Detects creation of the Process Monitor driver by processes other than Process Monitor (procmon) itself.
falsepositives: Some false positives may occur with legitimate renamed process monitor binaries

rules.title: Uncommon File Created In Office Startup Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file with an uncommon extension in an Office application startup folder
falsepositives: False positive might stem from rare extensions used by other Office utilities.

rules.title: LSASS Process Memory Dump Files
rules.description: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.

rules.title: Potential RipZip Attack on Startup Folder
rules.description:
Detects a phishing attack which expands a ZIP file containing a malicious shortcut.
If the victim expands the ZIP file via the explorer process, then the explorer process expands the malicious ZIP file and drops a malicious shortcut redirected to a backdoor into the Startup folder.
Additionally, the file name of the malicious shortcut in Startup folder contains {0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D} meaning the folder shortcut operation.

rules.title: Registry Hive File Staged Outside Standard User Profile Path
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a registry hive file (UsrClass.dat or NTUSER.DAT) outside of the standard user profile path.
These files generally contain various user-specific registry settings and are typically located in the user's profile directory.
Staging these files outside of the standard path can be indicative of an attacker attempting to manipulate user registry settings
for persistence, privilege escalation, or dump user registry hives for credential harvesting.

rules.title: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream
rules.description: Detects the creation of hidden file/folder with the "::$index_allocation" stream. Which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folder and files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" and "powershell.exe"

rules.title: Office Macro File Creation From Suspicious Process
rules.description: Detects the creation of a office macro file from a a suspicious process

rules.title: Suspicious Binaries and Scripts in Public Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a file with a suspicious extension in the public folder, which could indicate potential malicious activity.
falsepositives: Administrators deploying legitimate binaries to public folders.

rules.title: Suspicious Double Extension Files
rules.description: Detects dropped files with double extensions, which is often used by malware as a method to abuse the fact that Windows hide default extensions by default.

rules.title: PowerShell Profile Modification
rules.description: Detects the creation or modification of a powershell profile which could indicate suspicious activity as the profile can be used as a mean of persistence
falsepositives: System administrator creating Powershell profile manually

rules.title: DLL Search Order Hijackig Via Additional Space in Path
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker create a similar folder structure to windows system folders such as (Windows, Program Files...)
but with a space in order to trick DLL load search order and perform a "DLL Search Order Hijacking" attack

rules.title: Windows Binaries Write Suspicious Extensions
rules.description: Detects Windows executables that write files with suspicious extensions

rules.title: HackTool - Inveigh Execution Artefacts
rules.description: Detects the presence and execution of Inveigh via dropped artefacts

rules.title: Suspicious File Created In PerfLogs
rules.description: Detects suspicious file based on their extension being created in "C:\PerfLogs\". Note that this directory mostly contains ".etl" files

rules.title: Suspicious ASPX File Drop by Exchange
rules.description: Detects suspicious file type dropped by an Exchange component in IIS into a suspicious folder

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using IEInstal - File
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using IEInstal.exe (UACMe 64)

rules.title: SCR File Write Event
rules.description: Detects the creation of screensaver files (.scr) outside of system folders. Attackers may execute an application as an ".SCR" file using "rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver" for example.
falsepositives: The installation of new screen savers by third party software

rules.title: WerFault LSASS Process Memory Dump
rules.description: Detects WerFault creating a dump file with a name that indicates that the dump file could be an LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Form
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new Outlook form which can contain malicious code

rules.title: File With Uncommon Extension Created By An Office Application
rules.description: Detects the creation of files with an executable or script extension by an Office application.
authors: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng (Rule), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: AWL Bypass with Winrm.vbs and Malicious WsmPty.xsl/WsmTxt.xsl - File
rules.description: Detects execution of attacker-controlled WsmPty.xsl or WsmTxt.xsl via winrm.vbs and copied cscript.exe (can be renamed)

rules.title: Files With System Process Name In Unsuspected Locations
rules.description:
Detects the creation of an executable with a system process name in folders other than the system ones (System32, SysWOW64, etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
authors: Sander Wiebing, Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: System processes copied outside their default folders for testing purposes
Third party software naming their software with the same names as the processes mentioned here

rules.title: Potential Initial Access via DLL Search Order Hijacking
rules.description: Detects attempts to create a DLL file to a known desktop application dependencies folder such as Slack, Teams or OneDrive and by an unusual process. This may indicate an attempt to load a malicious module via DLL search order hijacking.

rules.title: Process Explorer Driver Creation By Non-Sysinternals Binary
rules.description:
Detects creation of the Process Explorer drivers by processes other than Process Explorer (procexp) itself.
Hack tools or malware may use the Process Explorer driver to elevate privileges, drops it to disk for a few moments, runs a service using that driver and removes it afterwards.
falsepositives: Some false positives may occur with legitimate renamed process explorer binaries

rules.title: Creation Of Non-Existent System DLL
rules.description:
Detects creation of specific system DLL files that are  usually not present on the system (or at least not in system directories) but may be loaded by legitimate processes.
Phantom DLL hijacking involves placing malicious DLLs with names of non-existent system binaries in locations where legitimate applications may search for them, leading to execution of the malicious DLLs.
Thus, the creation of such DLLs may indicate preparation for phantom DLL hijacking attacks.

rules.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Dump Indicator
rules.description: Detects default lsass dump filename generated by SafetyKatz.
falsepositives: Rare legitimate files with similar filename structure

rules.title: Suspicious DotNET CLR Usage Log Artifact
rules.description: Detects the creation of Usage Log files by the CLR (clr.dll). These files are named after the executing process once the assembly is finished executing for the first time in the (user) session context.
falsepositives: Rundll32.exe with zzzzInvokeManagedCustomActionOutOfProc in command line and msiexec.exe as parent process - https://twitter.com/SBousseaden/status/1388064061087260675

rules.title: Suspicious Creation with Colorcpl
rules.description: Once executed, colorcpl.exe will copy the arbitrary file to c:\windows\system32\spool\drivers\color\

rules.title: Dynamic CSharp Compile Artefact
rules.description:
When C# is compiled dynamically, a .cmdline file will be created as a part of the process.
Certain processes are not typically observed compiling C# code, but can do so without touching disk.
This can be used to unpack a payload for execution

rules.title: Suspicious File Created by ArcSOC.exe
rules.description:
Detects instances where the ArcGIS Server process ArcSOC.exe, which hosts REST services running on an ArcGIS
server, creates a file with suspicious file type, indicating that it may be an executable, script file,
or otherwise unusual.

rules.title: UEFI Persistence Via Wpbbin - FileCreation
rules.description: Detects creation of a file named "wpbbin" in the "%systemroot%\system32\" directory. Which could be indicative of UEFI based persistence method
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the file by hardware manufacturer such as lenovo (Thanks @0gtweet for the tip)

rules.title: New Custom Shim Database Created
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.
The Microsoft Windows Application Compatibility Infrastructure/Framework (Application Shim) was created to allow for backward compatibility of software as the operating system codebase changes over time.
falsepositives: Legitimate custom SHIM installations will also trigger this rule

rules.title: HackTool - NetExec File Indicators
rules.description:
Detects file creation events indicating NetExec (nxc.exe) execution on the local machine.
NetExec is a PyInstaller-bundled binary that extracts its embedded data files to a "_MEI<random>" directory
under the Temp folder upon execution. Files dropped under the "\nxc\" sub-directory of that
extraction path are unique to NetExec and serve as reliable on-disk indicators of execution.
NetExec (formerly CrackMapExec) is a widely used post-exploitation and lateral movement tool used for
Active Directory enumeration, credential harvesting, and remote code execution.

rules.title: Legitimate Application Dropped Executable
rules.description:
Detects LOLBINs and applications that should not legitimately drop executable or executable-equivalent files to disk.
This may indicate malware staging, process injection, or abuse of a trusted binary for payload delivery.

rules.title: CSExec Service File Creation
rules.description: Detects default CSExec service filename which indicates CSExec service installation and execution

rules.title: Malicious PowerShell Scripts - FileCreation
rules.description: Detects the creation of known offensive powershell scripts used for exploitation
authors: Markus Neis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Mustafa Kaan Demir, Georg Lauenstein

rules.title: Suspicious File Created in Outlook Temporary Directory
rules.description:
Detects the creation of files with suspicious file extensions in the temporary directory that Outlook uses when opening attachments.
This can be used to detect spear-phishing campaigns that use suspicious files as attachments, which may contain malicious code.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Opening of headers or footers in email signatures that include SVG images or legitimate SVG attachments

rules.title: Suspicious Desktopimgdownldr Target File
rules.description: Detects a suspicious Microsoft desktopimgdownldr file creation that stores a file to a suspicious location or contains a file with a suspicious extension
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: ScreenConnect Temporary Installation Artefact
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Advanced IP Scanner - File Event
rules.description: Detects the use of Advanced IP Scanner. Seems to be a popular tool for ransomware groups.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Self Extraction Directive File Created
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a binary file with the ".sed" extension. The ".sed" extension stand for Self Extraction Directive files.
These files are used by the "iexpress.exe" utility in order to create self extracting packages.
Attackers were seen abusing this utility and creating PE files with embedded ".sed" entries.
Usually ".sed" files are simple ini files and not PE binaries.

rules.title: Suspicious Appended Extension
rules.description: Detects file renames where the target filename uses an uncommon double extension. Could indicate potential ransomware activity renaming files and adding a custom extension to the encrypted files, such as ".jpg.crypted", ".docx.locky", etc.

rules.title: WMI Persistence - Command Line Event Consumer
rules.description: Detects WMI command line event consumers
falsepositives: Unknown (data set is too small; further testing needed)

rules.title: Unsigned Module Loaded by ClickOnce Application
rules.description: Detects unsigned module load by ClickOnce application.

rules.title: WMIC Loading Scripting Libraries
rules.description:
Detects threat actors proxy executing code and bypassing application controls by leveraging wmic and the `/FORMAT` argument switch to download and execute an XSL file (i.e js, vbs, etc).
It could be an indicator of SquiblyTwo technique, which uses Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute malicious code.
falsepositives: The command wmic os get lastbootuptime loads vbscript.dll
The command wmic os get locale loads vbscript.dll

Since the ImageLoad event doesn't have enough information in this case. It's better to look at the recent process creation events that spawned the WMIC process and investigate the command line and parent/child processes to get more insights

rules.title: PowerShell Core DLL Loaded By Non PowerShell Process
rules.description:
Detects loading of essential DLLs used by PowerShell by non-PowerShell process.
Detects behavior similar to meterpreter's "load powershell" extension.
authors: Tom Kern, oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova, Tim Shelton, Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)
falsepositives: Used by some .NET binaries, minimal on user workstation.
Used by Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio

rules.title: Trusted Path Bypass via Windows Directory Spoofing
rules.description:
Detects DLLs loading from a spoofed Windows directory path with an extra space (e.g "C:\Windows \System32") which can bypass Windows trusted path verification.
This technique tricks Windows into treating the path as trusted, allowing malicious DLLs to load with high integrity privileges bypassing UAC.

rules.title: Potential RjvPlatform.DLL Sideloading From Non-Default Location
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "RjvPlatform.dll" by "SystemResetPlatform.exe" located in a non-default location.

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Using Coregen.exe
rules.description: Detect usage of the "coregen.exe" (Microsoft CoreCLR Native Image Generator) binary to sideload arbitrary DLLs.

rules.title: Potential CCleanerDU.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "CCleanerDU.dll"
falsepositives: False positives could occur from other custom installation paths. Apply additional filters accordingly.

rules.title: Potential Vivaldi_elf.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "vivaldi_elf.dll"

rules.title: Potential SmadHook.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "SmadHook.dll", a DLL used by SmadAV antivirus

rules.title: Potential RjvPlatform.DLL Sideloading From Default Location
rules.description: Detects loading of "RjvPlatform.dll" by the "SystemResetPlatform.exe" binary which can be abused as a method of DLL side loading since the "$SysReset" directory isn't created by default.

rules.title: VMMap Unsigned Dbghelp.DLL Potential Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of an unsigned dbghelp.dll by the Sysinternals VMMap.

rules.title: System Control Panel Item Loaded From Uncommon Location
rules.description: Detects image load events of system control panel items (.cpl) from uncommon or non-system locations that may indicate DLL sideloading or other abuse techniques.

rules.title: Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy VSS_PS.dll Load
rules.description:
Detects the image load of vss_ps.dll by uncommon executables. This DLL is used by the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) to manage shadow copies of files and volumes.
It is often abused by attackers to delete or manipulate shadow copies, which can hinder forensic investigations and data recovery efforts.
The fact that it is loaded by processes that are not typically associated with VSS operations can indicate suspicious activity.

rules.title: Load Of RstrtMgr.DLL By An Uncommon Process
rules.description:
Detects the load of RstrtMgr DLL (Restart Manager) by an uncommon process.
This library has been used during ransomware campaigns to kill processes that would prevent file encryption by locking them (e.g. Conti ransomware, Cactus ransomware). It has also recently been seen used by the BiBi wiper for Windows.
It could also be used for anti-analysis purposes by shut downing specific processes.
falsepositives: Other legitimate Windows processes not currently listed

rules.title: Potential CCleanerReactivator.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "CCleanerReactivator.dll"
falsepositives: False positives could occur from other custom installation paths. Apply additional filters accordingly.

rules.title: Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy Vssapi.dll Load
rules.description: Detects the image load of VSS DLL by uncommon executables

rules.title: Suspicious Loading of Dbgcore/Dbghelp DLLs from Uncommon Location
rules.description:
Detects loading of dbgcore.dll or dbghelp.dll from uncommon locations such as user directories.
These DLLs contain the MiniDumpWriteDump function, which can be abused for credential dumping purposes or in some cases for evading EDR/AV detection by suspending processes.

rules.title: Potential Mpclient.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential sideloading of "mpclient.dll" by Windows Defender processes ("MpCmdRun" and "NisSrv") from their non-default directory.

rules.title: DotNet CLR DLL Loaded By Scripting Applications
rules.description: Detects .NET CLR DLLs being loaded by scripting applications such as wscript or cscript. This could be an indication of potential suspicious execution.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy Vsstrace.dll Load
rules.description: Detects the image load of VSS DLL by uncommon executables

rules.title: HackTool - SharpEvtMute DLL Load
rules.description: Detects the load of EvtMuteHook.dll, a key component of SharpEvtHook, a tool that tampers with the Windows event logs
falsepositives: Other DLLs with the same Imphash

rules.title: Potential Iviewers.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "iviewers.dll" (OLE/COM Object Interface Viewer)

rules.title: Potential 7za.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "7za.dll"
falsepositives: Legitimate third party application located in "AppData" may leverage this DLL to offer 7z compression functionality and may generate false positives. Apply additional filters as needed.

rules.title: Potential System DLL Sideloading From Non System Locations
rules.description: Detects DLL sideloading of DLLs usually located in system locations (System32, SysWOW64, etc.).
falsepositives: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLLs mentioned in this rule

rules.title: Potential Azure Browser SSO Abuse
rules.description:
Detects abusing Azure Browser SSO by requesting OAuth 2.0 refresh tokens for an Azure-AD-authenticated Windows user (i.e. the machine is joined to Azure AD and a user logs in with their Azure AD account) wanting to perform SSO authentication in the browser.
An attacker can use this to authenticate to Azure AD in a browser as that user.
falsepositives: False positives are expected since this rules is only looking for the DLL load event. This rule is better used in correlation with related activity

rules.title: Potential Antivirus Software DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of DLLs that are part of antivirus software suchas McAfee, Symantec...etc
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)
falsepositives: Applications that load the same dlls mentioned in the detection section. Investigate them and filter them out if a lot FPs are caused.
Dell SARemediation plugin folder (C:\Program Files\Dell\SARemediation\plugin\log.dll) is known to contain the 'log.dll' file.
The Canon MyPrinter folder 'C:\Program Files\Canon\MyPrinter\' is known to contain the 'log.dll' file

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of MpSvc.DLL
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "MpSvc.dll".
falsepositives: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule.

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via comctl32.dll
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading using comctl32.dll to obtain system privileges

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of DBGHELP.DLL
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "dbghelp.dll"
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)
falsepositives: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via JsSchHlp
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading using JUSTSYSTEMS Japanese word processor

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of Non-Existent DLLs From System Folders
rules.description:
Detects loading of specific system DLL files that are usually not present on the system (or at least not in system directories) but may be loaded by legitimate processes, potentially indicating phantom DLL hijacking attempts.
Phantom DLL hijacking involves placing malicious DLLs with names of non-existent system binaries in locations where legitimate applications may search for them, leading to execution of the malicious DLLs.

rules.title: Potential Rcdll.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of rcdll.dll

rules.title: BaaUpdate.exe Suspicious DLL Load
rules.description:
Detects BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility (baaupdate.exe) loading DLLs from suspicious locations that are publicly writable which could indicate an attempt to lateral movement via BitLocker DCOM & COM Hijacking.
This technique abuses COM Classes configured as INTERACTIVE USER to spawn processes in the context of the logged-on user's session. Specifically, it targets the BDEUILauncher Class (CLSID ab93b6f1-be76-4185-a488-a9001b105b94)
which can launch BaaUpdate.exe, which is vulnerable to COM Hijacking when started with input parameters. This allows attackers to execute code in the user's context without needing to steal credentials or use additional techniques to compromise the account.

rules.title: VMGuestLib DLL Sideload
rules.description: Detects DLL sideloading of VMGuestLib.dll by the WmiApSrv service.
falsepositives: FP could occur if the legitimate version of vmGuestLib already exists on the system

rules.title: Potential Waveedit.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "waveedit.dll", which is part of the Nero WaveEditor audio editing software.

rules.title: Potential Chrome Frame Helper DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "chrome_frame_helper.dll"
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)

rules.title: HackTool - SILENTTRINITY Stager DLL Load
rules.description: Detects SILENTTRINITY stager dll loading activity

rules.title: DLL Loaded From Suspicious Location Via Cmspt.EXE
rules.description: Detects cmstp loading "dll" or "ocx" files from suspicious locations

rules.title: Wmiprvse Wbemcomn DLL Hijack
rules.description: Detects a threat actor creating a file named `wbemcomn.dll` in the `C:\Windows\System32\wbem\` directory over the network and loading it for a WMI DLL Hijack scenario.

rules.title: Abusable DLL Potential Sideloading From Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of DLLs that are known to be abused from suspicious locations

rules.title: Potential JLI.dll Side-Loading
rules.description:
Detects potential DLL side-loading of jli.dll.
JLI.dll has been observed being side-loaded by Java processes by various threat actors, including APT41, XWorm,
and others in order to load malicious payloads in context of legitimate Java processes.

rules.title: Fax Service DLL Search Order Hijack
rules.description: The Fax service attempts to load ualapi.dll, which is non-existent. An attacker can then (side)load their own malicious DLL using this service.

rules.title: Microsoft Office DLL Sideload
rules.description: Detects DLL sideloading of DLLs that are part of Microsoft Office from non standard location
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)

rules.title: Potential ShellDispatch.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "ShellDispatch.dll"
falsepositives: Some installers may trigger some false positives

rules.title: PCRE.NET Package Image Load
rules.description: Detects processes loading modules related to PCRE.NET package

rules.title: Unsigned Image Loaded Into LSASS Process
rules.description: Loading unsigned image (DLL, EXE) into LSASS process

rules.title: Suspicious Renamed Comsvcs DLL Loaded By Rundll32
rules.description: Detects rundll32 loading a renamed comsvcs.dll to dump process memory

rules.title: GAC DLL Loaded Via Office Applications
rules.description: Detects any GAC DLL being loaded by an Office Product
falsepositives: Legitimate macro usage. Add the appropriate filter according to your environment

rules.title: Aruba Network Service Potential DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading activity via the Aruba Networks Virtual Intranet Access "arubanetsvc.exe" process using DLL Search Order Hijacking

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via VMware Xfer
rules.description: Detects loading of a DLL by the VMware Xfer utility from the non-default directory which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL

rules.title: Unsigned Mfdetours.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects DLL sideloading of unsigned "mfdetours.dll". Executing "mftrace.exe" can be abused to attach to an arbitrary process and force load any DLL named "mfdetours.dll" from the current directory of execution.

rules.title: Potential AVKkid.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "AVKkid.dll"

rules.title: VMMap Signed Dbghelp.DLL Potential Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of a signed dbghelp.dll by the Sysinternals VMMap.

rules.title: Microsoft VBA For Outlook Addin Loaded Via Outlook
rules.description: Detects outlvba (Microsoft VBA for Outlook Addin) DLL being loaded by the outlook process
falsepositives: Legitimate macro usage. Add the appropriate filter according to your environment

rules.title: CredUI.DLL Loaded By Uncommon Process
rules.description: Detects loading of "credui.dll" and related DLLs by an uncommon process. Attackers might leverage this DLL for potential use of "CredUIPromptForCredentials" or "CredUnPackAuthenticationBufferW".
falsepositives: Other legitimate processes loading those DLLs in your environment.

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of DBGCORE.DLL
rules.description: Detects DLL sideloading of "dbgcore.dll"
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)
falsepositives: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule

rules.title: DLL Load By System Process From Suspicious Locations
rules.description: Detects when a system process (i.e. located in system32, syswow64, etc.) loads a DLL from a suspicious location or a location with permissive permissions such as "C:\Users\Public"

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Iscsicpl - ImageLoad
rules.description: Detects the "iscsicpl.exe" UAC bypass technique that leverages a DLL Search Order hijacking technique to load a custom DLL's from temp or a any user controlled location in the users %PATH%

rules.title: Potential SolidPDFCreator.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "SolidPDFCreator.dll"

rules.title: UAC Bypass With Fake DLL
rules.description: Attempts to load dismcore.dll after dropping it
falsepositives: Actions of a legitimate telnet client

rules.title: MMC Loading Script Engines DLLs
rules.description:
Detects when the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) loads the DLL libraries like vbscript, jscript etc which might indicate an attempt
to execute malicious scripts within a trusted system process for bypassing application whitelisting or defense evasion.
falsepositives: Legitimate MMC operations or extensions loading these libraries

rules.title: Suspicious WSMAN Provider Image Loads
rules.description: Detects signs of potential use of the WSMAN provider from uncommon processes locally and remote execution.

rules.title: Microsoft Excel Add-In Loaded From Uncommon Location
rules.description: Detects Microsoft Excel loading an Add-In (.xll) file from an uncommon location
falsepositives: Some tuning might be required to allow or remove certain locations used by the rule if you consider them as safe locations

rules.title: WMI ActiveScriptEventConsumers Activity Via Scrcons.EXE DLL Load
rules.description: Detects signs of the WMI script host process "scrcons.exe" loading scripting DLLs which could indicates WMI ActiveScriptEventConsumers EventConsumers activity.
falsepositives: Dell computers on some versions register an event consumer that is known to cause false positives when brightness is changed by the corresponding keyboard button

rules.title: Load Of RstrtMgr.DLL By A Suspicious Process
rules.description:
Detects the load of RstrtMgr DLL (Restart Manager) by a suspicious process.
This library has been used during ransomware campaigns to kill processes that would prevent file encryption by locking them (e.g. Conti ransomware, Cactus ransomware). It has also recently been seen used by the BiBi wiper for Windows.
It could also be used for anti-analysis purposes by shut downing specific processes.

rules.title: Unsigned DLL Loaded by Windows Utility
rules.description:
Detects windows utilities loading an unsigned or untrusted DLL.
Adversaries often abuse those programs to proxy execution of malicious code.

rules.title: Potential Goopdate.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "goopdate.dll", a DLL used by googleupdate.exe
falsepositives: False positives are expected from Google Chrome installations running from user locations (AppData) and other custom locations. Apply additional filters accordingly.
Other third party chromium browsers located in AppData

rules.title: Suspicious Unsigned Dbghelp/Dbgcore DLL Loaded
rules.description:
Detects the load of dbghelp/dbgcore DLL (used to make memory dumps) by suspicious processes.
Tools like ProcessHacker and some attacker tradecract use MiniDumpWriteDump API found in dbghelp.dll or dbgcore.dll.
As an example, SilentTrynity C2 Framework has a module that leverages this API to dump the contents of Lsass.exe and transfer it over the network back to the attacker's machine.

rules.title: Potential Libvlc.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "libvlc.dll", a DLL that is legitimately used by "VLC.exe"
falsepositives: False positives are expected if VLC is installed in non-default locations

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Image Load of Offreg.dll
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious loading of the Offline Registry Library (offreg.dll).
Offreg.dll enables direct read/write access to offline registry hives without invoking the Windows Registry API,
bypassing its associated audit logging and telemetry. Attackers may abuse this to stealthily modify registry hives
while evading detection mechanisms that rely on standard registry event logs.
falsepositives: Third-party backup or forensic software that performs offline registry parsing
Windows deployment tools (DISM, ADK) run from non-standard paths

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via ClassicExplorer32.dll
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading using ClassicExplorer32.dll from the Classic Shell software

rules.title: Python Image Load By Non-Python Process
rules.description:
Detects the image load of "Python Core" by a non-Python process. This might be indicative of a execution of executable that has been bundled from Python code.
Various tools like Py2Exe, PyInstaller, and cx_Freeze are used to bundle Python code into standalone executables.
Threat actors often use these tools to bundle malicious Python scripts into executables, sometimes to obfuscate the code or to bypass security measures.
authors: Patrick St. John, OTR (Open Threat Research)
falsepositives: Known false positive caused with Python Anaconda
Various legitimate software is bundled from Python code into executables

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of MsCorSvc.DLL
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "mscorsvc.dll".
falsepositives: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule.

rules.title: CLR DLL Loaded Via Office Applications
rules.description: Detects CLR DLL being loaded by an Office Product

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of KeyScramblerIE.DLL Via KeyScrambler.EXE
rules.description:
Detects potential DLL side loading of "KeyScramblerIE.dll" by "KeyScrambler.exe".
Various threat actors and malware have been found side loading a masqueraded "KeyScramblerIE.dll" through "KeyScrambler.exe".

rules.title: Potential Mfdetours.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "mfdetours.dll". While using "mftrace.exe" it can be abused to attach to an arbitrary process and force load any DLL named "mfdetours.dll" from the current directory of execution.

rules.title: Potential Python DLL SideLoading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of Python DLL files.

rules.title: Potential Vcruntime140 DLL Sideloading
rules.description:
Detects potential DLL sideloading of vcruntime140.dll, a common C++ runtime library.
Threat actors have been observed using DLL sideloading techniques to load malicious payloads under the guise of legitimate applications such as SqlWriter, SqlDumper etc.
Notably, APT29 has been documented leveraging WinELOADER to sideload vcruntime140.dll for executing malicious code.

rules.title: Potential Wazuh Security Platform DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL side loading of DLLs that are part of the Wazuh security platform
falsepositives: Many legitimate applications leverage this DLL. (Visual Studio, JetBrains, Ruby, Anaconda, GithubDesktop, etc.)

rules.title: Potential WWlib.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "wwlib.dll"

rules.title: Potential Edputil.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "edputil.dll"

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of Libcurl.DLL Via GUP.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "libcurl.dll" by the "gup.exe" process from an uncommon location

rules.title: Unsigned .node File Loaded
rules.description:
Detects the loading of unsigned .node files.
Adversaries may abuse a lack of .node integrity checking to execute arbitrary code inside of trusted applications such as Slack.
.node files are native add-ons for Electron-based applications, which are commonly used for desktop applications like Slack, Discord, and Visual Studio Code.
This technique has been observed in the DripLoader malware, which uses unsigned .node files to load malicious native code into Electron applications.
falsepositives: VsCode extensions or similar legitimate tools might use unsigned .node files. These should be investigated on a case-by-case basis, and whitelisted if determined to be benign.

rules.title: VBA DLL Loaded Via Office Application
rules.description: Detects VB DLL's loaded by an office application. Which could indicate the presence of VBA Macros.
falsepositives: Legitimate macro usage. Add the appropriate filter according to your environment

rules.title: Time Travel Debugging Utility Usage - Image
rules.description: Detects usage of Time Travel Debugging Utility. Adversaries can execute malicious processes and dump processes, such as lsass.exe, via tttracer.exe.

rules.title: Suspicious Unsigned Thor Scanner Execution
rules.description: Detects loading and execution of an unsigned thor scanner binary.
