falsepositives: Other legitimate binaries named "thor.exe" that aren't published by Nextron Systems

rules.title: Diagnostic Library Sdiageng.DLL Loaded By Msdt.EXE
rules.description: Detects both of CVE-2022-30190 (Follina) and DogWalk vulnerabilities exploiting msdt.exe binary to load the "sdiageng.dll" library

rules.title: Potential EACore.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "EACore.dll"

rules.title: DLL Sideloading Of ShellChromeAPI.DLL
rules.description:
Detects processes loading the non-existent DLL "ShellChromeAPI". One known example is the "DeviceEnroller" binary in combination with the "PhoneDeepLink" flag tries to load this DLL.
Adversaries can drop their own renamed DLL and execute it via DeviceEnroller.exe using this parameter

rules.title: Potential appverifUI.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "appverifUI.dll"

rules.title: Potential DCOM InternetExplorer.Application DLL Hijack - Image Load
rules.description: Detects potential DLL hijack of "iertutil.dll" found in the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application Class
authors: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR), wagga

rules.title: Remote DLL Load Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description: Detects a remote DLL load event via "rundll32.exe".

rules.title: Potential RoboForm.DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "roboform.dll", a DLL used by RoboForm Password Manager
falsepositives: If installed on a per-user level, the path would be located in "AppData\Local". Add additional filters to reflect this mode of installation

rules.title: Third Party Software DLL Sideloading
rules.description: Detects DLL sideloading of DLLs that are part of third party software (zoom, discord....etc)
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)

rules.title: Clfs.SYS Loaded By Process Located In a Potential Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects Clfs.sys being loaded by a process running from a potentially suspicious location. Clfs.sys is loaded as part of many CVEs exploits that targets Common Log File.

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Of DbgModel.DLL
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "DbgModel.dll"
falsepositives: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule

rules.title: DotNET Assembly DLL Loaded Via Office Application
rules.description: Detects any assembly DLL being loaded by an Office Product

rules.title: RegAsm.EXE Initiating Network Connection To Public IP
rules.description: Detects "RegAsm.exe" initiating a network connection to public IP adresses

rules.title: Network Communication Initiated To Portmap.IO Domain
rules.description: Detects an executable accessing the portmap.io domain, which could be a sign of forbidden C2 traffic or data exfiltration by malicious actors

rules.title: Local Network Connection Initiated By Script Interpreter
rules.description: Detects a script interpreter (Wscript/Cscript) initiating a local network connection to download or execute a script hosted on a shared folder.

rules.title: Uncommon Network Connection Initiated By Certutil.EXE
rules.description:
Detects a network connection initiated by the certutil.exe utility.
Attackers can abuse the utility in order to download malware or additional payloads.

rules.title: Process Initiated Network Connection To Ngrok Domain
rules.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" domains.
Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware.
While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is a sign of either data exfiltration by malicious actors or additional download.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the ngrok service.

rules.title: Communication To Ngrok Tunneling Service Initiated
rules.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" tunneling domains.
Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware.
While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is a sign of either data exfiltration by malicious actors or additional download.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the ngrok service.

rules.title: Suspicious Dropbox API Usage
rules.description: Detects an executable that isn't dropbox but communicates with the Dropbox API
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the API with a tool that the author wasn't aware of

rules.title: New Connection Initiated To Potential Dead Drop Resolver Domain
rules.description:
Detects an executable, which is not an internet browser or known application, initiating network connections to legit popular websites, which were seen to be used as dead drop resolvers in previous attacks.
In this context attackers leverage known websites such as "facebook", "youtube", etc. In order to pass through undetected.
falsepositives: One might need to exclude other internet browsers found in it's network or other applications like ones mentioned above from Microsoft Defender.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated via Finger.EXE
rules.description:
Detects network connections via finger.exe, which can be abused by threat actors to retrieve remote commands for execution on Windows devices.
In one ClickFix malware campaign, adversaries leveraged the finger protocol to fetch commands from a remote server.
Since the finger utility is not commonly used in modern Windows environments, its presence already raises suspicion.
Investigating such network connections can also help identify potential malicious infrastructure used by threat actors

rules.title: Outbound Network Connection Initiated By Microsoft Dialer
rules.description:
Detects outbound network connection initiated by Microsoft Dialer.
The Microsoft Dialer, also known as Phone Dialer, is a built-in utility application included in various versions of the Microsoft Windows operating system. Its primary function is to provide users with a graphical interface for managing phone calls via a modem or a phone line connected to the computer.
This is an outdated process in the current conext of it's usage and is a common target for info stealers for process injection, and is used to make C2 connections, common example is "Rhadamanthys"
falsepositives: In Modern Windows systems, unable to see legitimate usage of this process, However, if an organization has legitimate purpose for this there can be false positives.

rules.title: Communication To LocaltoNet Tunneling Service Initiated
rules.description:
Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "LocaltoNet" tunneling sub-domains.
LocaltoNet is a reverse proxy that enables localhost services to be exposed to the Internet.
Attackers have been seen to use this service for command-and-control activities to bypass MFA and perimeter controls.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the LocaltoNet service.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated To Visual Studio Code Tunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects network connections to Visual Studio Code tunnel domains initiated by a process on a system. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Visual Studio Code tunnel will also trigger this.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Malware Callback Communication
rules.description: Detects programs that connect to known malware callback ports based on statistical analysis from two different sandbox system databases

rules.title: Silenttrinity Stager Msbuild Activity
rules.description: Detects a possible remote connections to Silenttrinity c2

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated By AddinUtil.EXE
rules.description:
Detects a network connection initiated by the Add-In deployment cache updating utility "AddInutil.exe".
This could indicate a potential command and control communication as this tool doesn't usually initiate network activity.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated To AzureWebsites.NET By Non-Browser Process
rules.description: Detects an initiated network connection by a non browser process on the system to "azurewebsites.net". The latter was often used by threat actors as a malware hosting and exfiltration site.

rules.title: RDP Over Reverse SSH Tunnel
rules.description: Detects svchost hosting RDP termsvcs communicating with the loopback address and on TCP port 3389

rules.title: Communication To Uncommon Destination Ports
rules.description: Detects programs that connect to uncommon destination ports

rules.title: Office Application Initiated Network Connection To Non-Local IP
rules.description:
Detects an office application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)  that initiate a network connection to a non-private IP addresses.
This rule aims to detect traffic similar to one seen exploited in CVE-2021-42292.
This rule will require an initial baseline and tuning that is specific to your organization.
authors: Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io', Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: You may have to tune certain domains out that Excel may call out to, such as microsoft or other business use case domains.
Office documents commonly have templates that refer to external addresses, like "sharepoint.ourcompany.com" may have to be tuned.
It is highly recommended to baseline your activity and tune out common business use cases.

rules.title: Outbound Network Connection To Public IP Via Winlogon
rules.description: Detects a "winlogon.exe" process that initiate network communications with public IP addresses
falsepositives: Communication to other corporate systems that use IP addresses from public address spaces

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated From Process Located In Potentially Suspicious Or Uncommon Location
rules.description: Detects a network connection initiated by programs or processes running from suspicious or uncommon files system locations.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated To Cloudflared Tunnels Domains
rules.description:
Detects network connections to Cloudflared tunnels domains initiated by a process on the system.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of cloudflare tunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: Suspicious Non-Browser Network Communication With Google API
rules.description: Detects a non-browser process interacting with the Google API which could indicate the use of a covert C2 such as Google Sheet C2 (GC2-sheet)
falsepositives: Legitimate applications communicating with the "googleapis.com" endpoints that are not already in the exclusion list. This is environmental dependent and requires further testing and tuning.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Network Connection To Notion API
rules.description: Detects a non-browser process communicating with the Notion API. This could indicate potential use of a covert C2 channel such as "OffensiveNotion C2"
falsepositives: Legitimate applications communicating with the "api.notion.com" endpoint that are not already in the exclusion list. The desktop and browser applications do not appear to be using the API by default unless integrations are configured.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated By IMEWDBLD.EXE
rules.description: Detects a network connection initiated by IMEWDBLD.EXE. This might indicate potential abuse of the utility as a LOLBIN in order to download arbitrary files or additional payloads.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated To DevTunnels Domain
rules.description: Detects network connections to Devtunnels domains initiated by a process on a system. Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Devtunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: Outbound Network Connection Initiated By Script Interpreter
rules.description: Detects a script interpreter wscript/cscript opening a network connection to a non-local network. Adversaries may use script to download malicious payloads.

rules.title: Suspicious Outbound SMTP Connections
rules.description:
Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an un-encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing command and control channel.
The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main command and control server.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated To BTunnels Domains
rules.description:
Detects network connections to BTunnels domains initiated by a process on the system.
Attackers can abuse that feature to establish a reverse shell or persistence on a machine.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of BTunnels will also trigger this.

rules.title: Microsoft Sync Center Suspicious Network Connections
rules.description: Detects suspicious connections from Microsoft Sync Center to non-private IPs.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated By Eqnedt32.EXE
rules.description: Detects network connections from the Equation Editor process "eqnedt32.exe".

rules.title: RDP to HTTP or HTTPS Target Ports
rules.description: Detects svchost hosting RDP termsvcs communicating to target systems on TCP port 80 or 443

rules.title: Uncommon Connection to Active Directory Web Services
rules.description: Detects uncommon network connections to the Active Directory Web Services (ADWS) from processes not typically associated with ADWS management.
falsepositives: ADWS is used by a number of legitimate applications that need to interact with Active Directory. These applications should be added to the allow-listing to avoid false positives.

rules.title: Python Initiated Connection
rules.description: Detects a Python process initiating a network connection. While this often relates to package installation, it can also indicate a potential malicious script communicating with a C&C server.
falsepositives: Legitimate python scripts using the socket library or similar will trigger this. Apply additional filters and perform an initial baseline before deploying.

rules.title: Suspicious Non-Browser Network Communication With Telegram API
rules.description: Detects an a non-browser process interacting with the Telegram API which could indicate use of a covert C2
falsepositives: Legitimate applications communicating with the Telegram API e.g. web browsers not in the exclusion list, app with an RSS  etc.

rules.title: Potential Remote PowerShell Session Initiated
rules.description:
Detects a process that initiated a network connection over ports 5985 or 5986 from a non-network service account.
This could potentially indicates a remote PowerShell connection.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of remote PowerShell, e.g. remote administration and monitoring.
Network Service user name of a not-covered localization

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Wuauclt Network Connection
rules.description:
Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) to proxy execute code and making network connections.
One could easily make the DLL spawn a new process and inject to it to proxy the network connection and bypass this rule.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated By Regsvr32.EXE
rules.description: Detects a network connection initiated by "Regsvr32.exe"

rules.title: Rundll32 Internet Connection
rules.description: Detects a rundll32 that communicates with public IP addresses
falsepositives: Communication to other corporate systems that use IP addresses from public address spaces

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Incoming Connection
rules.description: Detects incoming connections to AnyDesk. This could indicate a potential remote attacker trying to connect to a listening instance of AnyDesk and use it as potential command and control channel.
falsepositives: Legitimate incoming connections (e.g. sysadmin activity). Most of the time I would expect outgoing connections (initiated locally).

rules.title: Network Communication Initiated To File Sharing Domains From Process Located In Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detects executables located in potentially suspicious directories initiating network connections towards file sharing domains.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some installers located in the temp directory might communicate with the Github domains in order to download additional software. Baseline these cases or move the github domain to a lower level hunting rule.

rules.title: Uncommon Outbound Kerberos Connection
rules.description: Detects uncommon outbound network activity via Kerberos default port indicating possible lateral movement or first stage PrivEsc via delegation.
falsepositives: Web Browsers and third party application might generate similar activity. An initial baseline is required.

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated Via Notepad.EXE
rules.description:
Detects a network connection that is initiated by the "notepad.exe" process.
This might be a sign of process injection from a beacon process or something similar.
Notepad rarely initiates a network communication except when printing documents for example.
falsepositives: Printing documents via notepad might cause communication with the printer via port 9100 or similar.

rules.title: Outbound RDP Connections Over Non-Standard Tools
rules.description:
Detects Non-Standard tools initiating a connection over port 3389 indicating possible lateral movement.
An initial baseline is required before using this utility to exclude third party RDP tooling that you might use.

rules.title: Suspicious Network Connection to IP Lookup Service APIs
rules.description: Detects external IP address lookups by non-browser processes via services such as "api.ipify.org". This could be indicative of potential post compromise internet test activity.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the external websites for troubleshooting or network monitoring

rules.title: Outbound Network Connection Initiated By Cmstp.EXE
rules.description:
Detects a network connection initiated by Cmstp.EXE
Its uncommon for "cmstp.exe" to initiate an outbound network connection. Investigate the source of such requests to determine if they are malicious.

rules.title: Network Communication With Crypto Mining Pool
rules.description:
Detects initiated network connections to crypto mining pools.
It indicates that the system is likely infected with a crypto miner malware or is being used for crypto mining.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Network Connection Initiated To Mega.nz
rules.description:
Detects a network connection initiated by a binary to "api.mega.co.nz".
Attackers were seen abusing file sharing websites similar to "mega.nz" in order to upload/download additional payloads.
falsepositives: Legitimate MEGA installers and utilities are expected to communicate with this domain. Exclude hosts that are known to be allowed to use this tool.

rules.title: HackTool - Koh Default Named Pipe
rules.description: Detects creation of default named pipes used by the Koh tool

rules.title: CobaltStrike Named Pipe Pattern Regex
rules.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe matching a pattern used by CobaltStrike Malleable C2 profiles

rules.title: ADFS Database Named Pipe Connection By Uncommon Tool
rules.description:
Detects suspicious local connections via a named pipe to the AD FS configuration database (Windows Internal Database).
Used to access information such as the AD FS configuration settings which contains sensitive information used to sign SAML tokens.

rules.title: PsExec Tool Execution From Suspicious Locations - PipeName
rules.description: Detects PsExec default pipe creation where the image executed is located in a suspicious location. Which could indicate that the tool is being used in an attack
falsepositives: Rare legitimate use of psexec from the locations mentioned above. This will require initial tuning based on your environment.

rules.title: WMI Event Consumer Created Named Pipe
rules.description: Detects the WMI Event Consumer service scrcons.exe creating a named pipe

rules.title: HackTool - CoercedPotato Named Pipe Creation
rules.description: Detects the pattern of a pipe name as used by the hack tool CoercedPotato

rules.title: Alternate PowerShell Hosts Pipe
rules.description: Detects alternate PowerShell hosts potentially bypassing detections looking for powershell.exe
falsepositives: Programs using PowerShell directly without invocation of a dedicated interpreter.

rules.title: HackTool - EfsPotato Named Pipe Creation
rules.description: Detects the pattern of a pipe name as used by the hack tool EfsPotato

rules.title: CobaltStrike Named Pipe Patterns
rules.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe with a pattern found in CobaltStrike malleable C2 profiles
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Chrome instances using the exact same pipe name "mojo.xxx"
Websense Endpoint using the pipe name "DserNamePipe(R|W)\d{1,5}"
Some applications may just coincidentally use the pipe names which contain the same prefix as the ones used by CobaltStrike, e.g. "f4c3"

rules.title: HackTool - Credential Dumping Tools Named Pipe Created
rules.description: Detects well-known credential dumping tools execution via specific named pipe creation
falsepositives: Legitimate Administrator using tool for password recovery

rules.title: New PowerShell Instance Created
rules.description: Detects the execution of PowerShell via the creation of a named pipe starting with PSHost

rules.title: PUA - RemCom Default Named Pipe
rules.description: Detects default RemCom pipe creation
authors: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: CobaltStrike Named Pipe
rules.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe as used by CobaltStrike

rules.title: PUA - CSExec Default Named Pipe
rules.description: Detects default CSExec pipe creation
authors: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - PAExec Default Named Pipe
rules.description: Detects PAExec default named pipe

rules.title: Malicious Named Pipe Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of a named pipe seen used by known APTs or malware.

rules.title: HackTool - CobaltStrike BOF Injection Pattern
rules.description: Detects a typical pattern of a CobaltStrike BOF which inject into other processes

rules.title: Suspicious Svchost Process Access
rules.description: Detects suspicious access to the "svchost" process such as that used by Invoke-Phantom to kill the thread of the Windows event logging service.

rules.title: Credential Dumping Attempt Via Svchost
rules.description: Detects when a process tries to access the memory of svchost to potentially dump credentials.

rules.title: Suspicious Process Access of MsMpEng by WerFaultSecure - EDR-Freeze
rules.description:
Detects process access events where WerFaultSecure accesses MsMpEng.exe with dbgcore.dll or dbghelp.dll in the call trace, indicating potential EDR freeze techniques.
This technique leverages WerFaultSecure.exe running as a Protected Process Light (PPL) with WinTCB protection level to call MiniDumpWriteDump and suspend EDR/AV processes, allowing malicious activity to execute undetected during the suspension period.

rules.title: CMSTP Execution Process Access
rules.description: Detects various indicators of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer execution
falsepositives: Legitimate CMSTP use (unlikely in modern enterprise environments)

rules.title: Potential Direct Syscall of NtOpenProcess
rules.description: Detects potential calls to NtOpenProcess directly from NTDLL.

rules.title: Suspicious LSASS Access Via MalSecLogon
rules.description: Detects suspicious access to LSASS handle via a call trace to "seclogon.dll" with a suspicious access right.
authors: Samir Bousseaden (original elastic rule), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: LSASS Access From Potentially White-Listed Processes
rules.description: Detects a possible process memory dump that uses a white-listed filename like TrolleyExpress.exe as a way to dump the LSASS process memory without Microsoft Defender interference

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using WOW64 Logger DLL Hijack
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using a WoW64 logger DLL hijack (UACMe 30)

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Activity Via LSASS
rules.description:
Detects process access requests to the LSASS process with specific call trace calls and access masks.
This behaviour is expressed by many credential dumping tools such as Mimikatz, NanoDump, Invoke-Mimikatz, Procdump and even the Taskmgr dumping feature.

rules.title: HackTool - LittleCorporal Generated Maldoc Injection
rules.description: Detects the process injection of a LittleCorporal generated Maldoc.

rules.title: LSASS Memory Access by Tool With Dump Keyword In Name
rules.description: Detects LSASS process access requests from a source process with the "dump" keyword in its image name.
falsepositives: Rare programs that contain the word dump in their name and access lsass

rules.title: Suspicious Process Access to LSASS with Dbgcore/Dbghelp DLLs
rules.description:
Detects suspicious process access to LSASS.exe from processes located in uncommon locations with dbgcore.dll or dbghelp.dll in the call trace.
These DLLs contain functions like MiniDumpWriteDump that can be abused for credential dumping purposes. While modern tools like Mimikatz have moved to using ntdll.dll,
dbgcore.dll and dbghelp.dll are still used by basic credential dumping utilities and legacy tools for LSASS memory access and process suspension techniques.
falsepositives: Possibly during software installation or update processes

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious GrantedAccess Flags On LSASS
rules.description: Detects process access requests to LSASS process with potentially suspicious access flags
authors: Florian Roth, Roberto Rodriguez, Dimitrios Slamaris, Mark Russinovich, Thomas Patzke, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Sherif Eldeeb, James Dickenson, Aleksey Potapov, oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate software such as AV and EDR

rules.title: Uncommon Process Access Rights For Target Image
rules.description: Detects process access request to uncommon target images with a "PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS" access mask.

rules.title: Lsass Memory Dump via Comsvcs DLL
rules.description: Detects adversaries leveraging the MiniDump export function from comsvcs.dll via rundll32 to perform a memory dump from lsass.

rules.title: Remote LSASS Process Access Through Windows Remote Management
rules.description: Detects remote access to the LSASS process via WinRM. This could be a sign of credential dumping from tools like mimikatz.

rules.title: HackTool - HandleKatz Duplicating LSASS Handle
rules.description: Detects HandleKatz opening LSASS to duplicate its handle to later dump the memory without opening any new handles

rules.title: HackTool - Generic Process Access
rules.description: Detects process access requests from hacktool processes based on their default image name
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: HackTool - SysmonEnte Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of SysmonEnte, a tool to attack the integrity of Sysmon

rules.title: Credential Dumping Attempt Via WerFault
rules.description: Detects process LSASS memory dump using Mimikatz, NanoDump, Invoke-Mimikatz, Procdump or Taskmgr based on the CallTrace pointing to ntdll.dll, dbghelp.dll or dbgcore.dll for win10, server2016 and up.
falsepositives: Actual failures in lsass.exe that trigger a crash dump (unlikely)
Unknown cases in which WerFault accesses lsass.exe

rules.title: Credential Dumping Activity By Python Based Tool
rules.description: Detects LSASS process access for potential credential dumping by a Python-like tool such as LaZagne or Pypykatz.

rules.title: Function Call From Undocumented COM Interface EditionUpgradeManager
rules.description: Detects function calls from the EditionUpgradeManager COM interface. Which is an interface that is not used by standard executables.

rules.title: System Information Discovery via Registry Queries
rules.description: Detects attempts to query system information directly from the Windows Registry.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Windows Media Player - Process
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using Windows Media Player osksupport.dll (UACMe 32)

rules.title: Suspicious Download from Office Domain
rules.description: Detects suspicious ways to download files from Microsoft domains that are used to store attachments in Emails or OneNote documents
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Scripts or tools that download attachments from these domains (OneNote, Outlook 365)

rules.title: Detection of PowerShell Execution via Sqlps.exe
rules.description:
This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqlps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the MSSQL Server.
Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on the analysis of these logs.
falsepositives: Direct PS command execution through SQLPS.exe is uncommon, childprocess sqlps.exe spawned by sqlagent.exe is a legitimate action.

rules.title: RDP Connection Allowed Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of the netsh command to open and allow connections to port 3389 (RDP). As seen used by Sarwent Malware

rules.title: Potentially Over Permissive Permissions Granted Using Dsacls.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of Dsacls to grant over permissive permissions
falsepositives: Legitimate administrators granting over permissive permissions to users

rules.title: Uncommon Svchost Parent Process
rules.description: Detects an uncommon svchost parent process

rules.title: Malicious PowerShell Commandlets - ProcessCreation
rules.description: Detects Commandlet names from well-known PowerShell exploitation frameworks

rules.title: Suspicious HWP Sub Processes
rules.description: Detects suspicious Hangul Word Processor (Hanword) sub processes that could indicate an exploitation

rules.title: Python Function Execution Security Warning Disabled In Excel
rules.description:
Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.
Threat actors could run malicious code through the new Microsoft Excel feature that allows Python to run within the spreadsheet.

rules.title: Potential Mpclient.DLL Sideloading Via OfflineScannerShell.EXE Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of Windows Defender "OfflineScannerShell.exe" from its non standard directory.
The "OfflineScannerShell.exe" binary is vulnerable to DLL side loading and will load any DLL named "mpclient.dll" from the current working directory.

rules.title: Potential COM Objects Download Cradles Usage - Process Creation
rules.description: Detects usage of COM objects that can be abused to download files in PowerShell by CLSID

rules.title: HackTool - SILENTTRINITY Stager Execution
rules.description: Detects SILENTTRINITY stager use via PE metadata

rules.title: Suspicious MSHTA Child Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process spawning from an "mshta.exe" process, which could be indicative of a malicious HTA script execution

rules.title: UtilityFunctions.ps1 Proxy Dll
rules.description: Detects the use of a Microsoft signed script executing a managed DLL with PowerShell.

rules.title: Suspicious IIS Module Registration
rules.description: Detects a suspicious IIS module registration as described in Microsoft threat report on IIS backdoors

rules.title: Insensitive Subfolder Search Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of findstr with the "s" and "i" flags for a "subfolder" and "insensitive" search respectively. Attackers sometimes leverage this built-in utility to search the system for interesting files or filter through results of commands.

rules.title: HackTool - SharpMove Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of SharpMove, a .NET utility performing multiple tasks such as "Task Creation", "SCM" query, VBScript execution using WMI via its PE metadata and command line options.

rules.title: Powershell Executed From Headless ConHost Process
rules.description:
Detects the use of powershell commands from headless ConHost window.
The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Execution Patterns
rules.description: Detects various execution patterns of the CrackMapExec pentesting framework

rules.title: MMC Spawning Windows Shell
rules.description: Detects a Windows command line executable started from MMC

rules.title: Service Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on services registry key. Often used by attacker to remove AV software services

rules.title: XSL Script Execution Via WMIC.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of WMIC with the "format" flag to potentially load local XSL files.
Adversaries abuse this functionality to execute arbitrary files while potentially bypassing application whitelisting defenses.
Extensible Stylesheet Language (XSL) files are commonly used to describe the processing and rendering of data within XML files.
authors: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
falsepositives: WMIC.exe FP depend on scripts and administrative methods used in the monitored environment.

rules.title: Add New Download Source To Winget
rules.description: Detects usage of winget to add new additional download sources
falsepositives: False positive are expected with legitimate sources

rules.title: Suspicious SYSVOL Domain Group Policy Access
rules.description: Detects Access to Domain Group Policies stored in SYSVOL

rules.title: IIS WebServer Log Deletion via CommandLine Utilities
rules.description:
Detects attempts to delete Internet Information Services (IIS) log files via command line utilities, which is a common defense evasion technique used by attackers to cover their tracks.
Threat actors often abuse vulnerabilities in web applications hosted on IIS servers to gain initial access and later delete IIS logs to evade detection.
falsepositives: Deletion of IIS logs that are older than a certain retention period as part of regular maintenance activities.
Legitimate schedule tasks or scripts that clean up log files regularly.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Anydesk Execution From Suspicious Folder
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of AnyDesk from a non-standard folder

rules.title: HackTool - Quarks PwDump Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of the Quarks PwDump tool via commandline arguments

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Via FTP.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "ftp.exe" script with the "-s" or "/s" flag and any child processes ran by "ftp.exe".

rules.title: AWL Bypass with Winrm.vbs and Malicious WsmPty.xsl/WsmTxt.xsl
rules.description: Detects execution of attacker-controlled WsmPty.xsl or WsmTxt.xsl via winrm.vbs and copied cscript.exe (can be renamed)

rules.title: Suspicious Reconnaissance Activity Via GatherNetworkInfo.VBS
rules.description: Detects execution of the built-in script located in "C:\Windows\System32\gatherNetworkInfo.vbs". Which can be used to gather information about the target machine

rules.title: Tamper Windows Defender Remove-MpPreference
rules.description: Detects attempts to remove Windows Defender configurations using the 'MpPreference' cmdlet

rules.title: Potential Reconnaissance For Cached Credentials Via Cmdkey.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of cmdkey to look for cached credentials on the system
authors: jmallette, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential CommandLine Path Traversal Via Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential path traversal attempt via cmd.exe. Could indicate possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
falsepositives: Java tools are known to produce false-positive when loading libraries

rules.title: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Suspicious File Extension
rules.description: Detects the execution of REGSVR32.exe with DLL files masquerading as other files

rules.title: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream - CLI
rules.description: Detects command line containing reference to the "::$index_allocation" stream, which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folders or files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" or "powershell.exe"

rules.title: Use of Pcalua For Execution
rules.description: Detects execition of commands and binaries from the context of The program compatibility assistant (Pcalua.exe). This can be used as a LOLBIN in order to bypass application whitelisting.
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate use by a via a batch script or by an administrator.

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell IEX Execution Patterns
rules.description: Detects suspicious ways to run Invoke-Execution using IEX alias
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Audit Policy Tampering Via Auditpol
rules.description:
Threat actors can use auditpol binary to change audit policy configuration to impair detection capability.
This can be carried out by selectively disabling/removing certain audit policies as well as restoring a custom policy owned by the threat actor.
falsepositives: Administrator or administrator scripts might leverage the flags mentioned in the detection section. Either way, it should always be monitored

rules.title: Suspicious GUP Usage
rules.description: Detects execution of the Notepad++ updater in a suspicious directory, which is often used in DLL side-loading attacks
falsepositives: Execution of tools named GUP.exe and located in folders different than Notepad++\updater

rules.title: Uncommon Userinit Child Process
rules.description: Detects uncommon "userinit.exe" child processes, which could be a sign of uncommon shells or login scripts used for persistence.
falsepositives: Legitimate logon scripts or custom shells may trigger false positives. Apply additional filters accordingly.

rules.title: HackTool - Jlaive In-Memory Assembly Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Jlaive to execute assemblies in a copied PowerShell

rules.title: Renamed Office Binary Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed office binary

rules.title: Time Travel Debugging Utility Usage
rules.description: Detects usage of Time Travel Debugging Utility. Adversaries can execute malicious processes and dump processes, such as lsass.exe, via tttracer.exe.

rules.title: Service Started/Stopped Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of wmic to start or stop a service

rules.title: Imports Registry Key From an ADS
rules.description: Detects the import of a alternate datastream to the registry with regedit.exe.

rules.title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Rename Of Highly Relevant Binaries
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed binary often used by attackers or malware leveraging new Sysmon OriginalFileName datapoint.
authors: Matthew Green - @mgreen27, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113
falsepositives: Custom applications use renamed binaries adding slight change to binary name. Typically this is easy to spot and add to whitelist
PsExec installed via Windows Store doesn't contain original filename field (False negative)

rules.title: Control Panel Items
rules.description: Detects the malicious use of a control panel item

rules.title: Execution via WorkFolders.exe
rules.description: Detects using WorkFolders.exe to execute an arbitrary control.exe
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the uncommon Windows Work Folders feature.

rules.title: PUA - Potential PE Metadata Tamper Using Rcedit
rules.description: Detects the use of rcedit to potentially alter executable PE metadata properties, which could conceal efforts to rename system utilities for defense evasion.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the tool by administrators or users to update metadata of a binary

rules.title: Potential Tampering With RDP Related Registry Keys Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "reg.exe" for enabling/disabling the RDP service on the host by tampering with the 'CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' values

rules.title: Suspicious Reg Add BitLocker
rules.description: Detects suspicious addition to BitLocker related registry keys via the reg.exe utility

rules.title: Firewall Configuration Discovery Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems

rules.title: File Download with Headless Browser
rules.description: Detects execution of chromium based browser in headless mode using the "dump-dom" command line to download files

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32.EXE Execution of UDL File
rules.description:
Detects the execution of rundll32.exe with the oledb32.dll library to open a UDL file.
Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.
falsepositives: UDL files serve as a convenient and flexible tool for managing and testing database connections in various development and administrative scenarios.

rules.title: New DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a dMSASvc account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the Cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server 2025.
On top of that, if the user that is creating the dMSASvc account is not a legitimate administrator or does not have the necessary permissions,
it is a strong signal of an attempted or successful abuse of the BaDSuccessor vulnerability for privilege escalation within the Windows Server 2025 Active Directory environment.

rules.title: Attempts of Kerberos Coercion Via DNS SPN Spoofing
rules.description:
Detects the presence of "UWhRC....AAYBAAAA" pattern in command line.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication from victim systems to attacker-controlled hosts.
It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack, where adversaries manipulate DNS records
to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) and redirect authentication requests like in CVE-2025-33073.
If you see this pattern in the command line, it is likely an attempt to add spoofed Service Principal Names (SPNs) to DNS records,
or checking for the presence of such records through the `nslookup` command.

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Systeminfo
rules.description: Detects usage of the "systeminfo" command to retrieve information

rules.title: Potential DLL File Download Via PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest
rules.description: Detects potential DLL files being downloaded using the PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest or Invoke-RestMethod cmdlets.

rules.title: Script Interpreter Spawning Credential Scanner - Windows
rules.description:
Detects a script interpreter process (like node.js or bun) spawning a known credential scanning tool (e.g., trufflehog, gitleaks).
This behavior is indicative of an attempt to find and steal secrets, as seen in the "Shai-Hulud: The Second Coming" campaign.
falsepositives: Legitimate pre-commit hooks or CI/CD pipeline jobs that use a script to run a credential scanner as part of a security check.

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation via Service Permissions Weakness
rules.description: Detect modification of services configuration (ImagePath, FailureCommand and ServiceDLL) in registry by processes with Medium integrity level

rules.title: Suspicious ScreenSave Change by Reg.exe
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension

rules.title: Terminal Service Process Spawn
rules.description: Detects a process spawned by the terminal service server process (this could be an indicator for an exploitation of CVE-2019-0708)

rules.title: File Download Using ProtocolHandler.exe
rules.description: Detects usage of "ProtocolHandler" to download files. Downloaded files will be located in the cache folder (for example - %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\IE)

rules.title: Persistence Via Sticky Key Backdoor
rules.description:
By replacing the sticky keys executable with the local admins CMD executable, an attacker is able to access a privileged windows console session without authenticating to the system.
When the sticky keys are "activated" the privilleged shell is launched.

rules.title: HackTool - Potential Impacket Lateral Movement Activity
rules.description: Detects wmiexec/dcomexec/atexec/smbexec from Impacket framework
authors: Ecco, oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Tim Rauch

rules.title: User Added To Highly Privileged Group
rules.description: Detects addition of users to highly privileged groups via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
falsepositives: Administrative activity that must be investigated

rules.title: User Discovery And Export Via Get-ADUser Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects usage of the Get-ADUser cmdlet to collect user information and output it to a file
falsepositives: Legitimate admin scripts may use the same technique, it's better to exclude specific computers or users who execute these commands or scripts often

rules.title: Suspicious X509Enrollment - Process Creation
rules.description: Detect use of X509Enrollment

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Silent Installation
rules.description: Detects AnyDesk Remote Desktop silent installation. Which can be used by attackers to gain remote access.

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Browser Launch From Document Reader Process
rules.description: Detects when a browser process or browser tab is launched from an application that handles document files such as Adobe, Microsoft Office, etc. And connects to a web application over http(s), this could indicate a possible phishing attempt.
falsepositives: Unlikely in most cases, further investigation should be done in the commandline of the browser process to determine the context of the URL accessed.

rules.title: Script Interpreter Execution From Suspicious Folder
rules.description:
Detects suspicious script execution from suspicious directories or folders accessible by environment variables that may indicate malware activity.
Script interpreters (cscript, wscript, mshta, powershell) executing from folders like Temp, Public, or user profile directories may suggest attempts to evade detection or execute malicious scripts.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Various legitimate software have been observed to use similar techniques for installation or update purposes;thus, it is recommended to review and tune filters for your environment to reduce false positives before deploying to production.

rules.title: HackTool - KrbRelayUp Execution
rules.description: Detects KrbRelayUp used to perform a universal no-fix local privilege escalation in Windows domain environments where LDAP signing is not enforced

rules.title: Potential Windows Defender AV Bypass Via Dump64.EXE Rename
rules.description:
Detects when a user is potentially trying to bypass the Windows Defender AV by renaming a tool to dump64.exe and placing it in the Visual Studio folder.
Currently the rule is covering only usage of procdump but other utilities can be added in order to increase coverage.
authors: Austin Songer @austinsonger, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Windows Firewall Disabled via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects attempts to disable the Windows Firewall using PowerShell

rules.title: CodePage Modification Via MODE.COM To Russian Language
rules.description:
Detects a CodePage modification using the "mode.com" utility to Russian language.
This behavior has been used by threat actors behind Dharma ransomware.
falsepositives: Russian speaking people changing the CodePage

rules.title: Potential Command Line Path Traversal Evasion Attempt
rules.description: Detects potential evasion or obfuscation attempts using bogus path traversal via the commandline

rules.title: Suspicious Service Path Modification
rules.description: Detects service path modification via the "sc" binary to a suspicious command or path
authors: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Downloaded From Direct IP Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with certain flags that allow the utility to download files from direct IPs.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious WebDAV LNK Execution
rules.description: Detects possible execution via LNK file accessed on a WebDAV server.

rules.title: Boot Configuration Tampering Via Bcdedit.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of the bcdedit command to tamper with the boot configuration data. This technique is often times used by malware or attackers as a destructive way before launching ransomware.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

rules.title: Use of UltraVNC Remote Access Software
rules.description: An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software,to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of WinRAR.EXE
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of WinRAR.exe.

rules.title: Potential DLL Injection Or Execution Using Tracker.exe
rules.description: Detects potential DLL injection and execution using "Tracker.exe"

rules.title: Potential Product Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of WMIC in order to get a list of firewall and antivirus products

rules.title: Potential Meterpreter/CobaltStrike Activity
rules.description: Detects the use of getsystem Meterpreter/Cobalt Strike command by detecting a specific service starting
falsepositives: Commandlines containing components like cmd accidentally
Jobs and services started with cmd

rules.title: Suspicious Process Start Locations
rules.description: Detects suspicious process run from unusual locations
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Rundll32 InstallScreenSaver Execution
rules.description: An attacker may execute an application as a SCR File using rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver
falsepositives: Legitimate installation of a new screensaver

rules.title: Malicious PE Execution by Microsoft Visual Studio Debugger
rules.description:
There is an option for a MS VS Just-In-Time Debugger "vsjitdebugger.exe" to launch specified executable and attach a debugger.
This option may be used adversaries to execute malicious code by signed verified binary.
The debugger is installed alongside with Microsoft Visual Studio package.
falsepositives: The process spawned by vsjitdebugger.exe is uncommon.

rules.title: Local Groups Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "wmic" with the "group" flag.
Adversaries may attempt to find local system groups and permission settings.
The knowledge of local system permission groups can help adversaries determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group.
Adversaries may use this information to determine which users have elevated permissions, such as the users found within the local administrators group.

rules.title: Suspect Svchost Activity
rules.description: It is extremely abnormal for svchost.exe to spawn without any CLI arguments and is normally observed when a malicious process spawns the process and injects code into the process memory space.
falsepositives: Rpcnet.exe / rpcnetp.exe which is a lojack style software. https://www.blackhat.com/docs/us-14/materials/us-14-Kamlyuk-Kamluk-Computrace-Backdoor-Revisited.pdf

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution Without CommandLine Parameters
rules.description: Detects suspicious start of rundll32.exe without any parameters as found in CobaltStrike beacon activity

rules.title: Powershell Defender Exclusion
rules.description: Detects requests to exclude files, folders or processes from Antivirus scanning using PowerShell cmdlets
falsepositives: Other Cmdlets that may use the same parameters

rules.title: Elevated System Shell Spawned From Uncommon Parent Location
rules.description: Detects when a shell program such as the Windows command prompt or PowerShell is launched with system privileges from a uncommon parent location.
falsepositives: Some legitimate applications may spawn shells from uncommon parent locations. Apply additional filters and perform an initial baseline before deploying.

rules.title: Suspicious New Service Creation
rules.description: Detects creation of a new service via "sc" command or the powershell "new-service" cmdlet with suspicious binary paths

rules.title: Potential File Download Via MS-AppInstaller Protocol Handler
rules.description:
Detects usage of the "ms-appinstaller" protocol handler via command line to potentially download arbitrary files via AppInstaller.EXE
The downloaded files are temporarly stored in ":\Users\%username%\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_8wekyb3d8bbwe\AC\INetCache\<RANDOM-8-CHAR-DIRECTORY>"
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: PowerShell Base64 Encoded WMI Classes
rules.description: Detects calls to base64 encoded WMI class such as "Win32_ShadowCopy", "Win32_ScheduledJob", etc.
authors: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Diantz Download and Compress Into a CAB File
rules.description: Download and compress a remote file and store it in a cab file on local machine.

rules.title: Use of VSIISExeLauncher.exe
rules.description: The "VSIISExeLauncher.exe" binary part of the Visual Studio/VS Code can be used to execute arbitrary binaries

rules.title: Execute Code with Pester.bat as Parent
rules.description: Detects code execution via Pester.bat (Pester - Powershell Modulte for testing)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Pester for writing tests for Powershell scripts and modules

rules.title: Uncommon Extension Shim Database Installation Via Sdbinst.EXE
rules.description:
Detects installation of a potentially suspicious new shim with an uncommon extension using sdbinst.exe.
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims

rules.title: Xwizard.EXE Execution From Non-Default Location
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Xwizard tool from a non-default directory.
When executed from a non-default directory, this utility can be abused in order to side load a custom version of "xwizards.dll".

rules.title: Run Once Task Execution as Configured in Registry
rules.description: This rule detects the execution of Run Once task as configured in the registry

rules.title: Suspicious Download Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with certain flags that allow the utility to download files.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Ping Hex IP
rules.description: Detects a ping command that uses a hex encoded IP address
falsepositives: Unlikely, because no sane admin pings IP addresses in a hexadecimal form

rules.title: Renamed CreateDump Utility Execution
rules.description: Detects uses of a renamed legitimate createdump.exe LOLOBIN utility to dump process memory
falsepositives: Command lines that use the same flags

rules.title: Security Event Logging Disabled via MiniNt Registry Key - Process
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable security event logging by adding the `MiniNt` registry key.
This key is used to disable the Windows Event Log service, which collects and stores event logs from the operating system and applications.
Adversaries may want to disable this service to prevent logging of security events that could be used to detect their activities.

rules.title: Firewall Rule Deleted Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects the removal of a port or application rule in the Windows Firewall configuration using netsh

value.pattern: ^.*advfirewall\ firewall\ delete\ rule\ name="Avast\ Antivirus\ Admin\ Client".*$

rules.title: Winrar Compressing Dump Files
rules.description: Detects execution of WinRAR in order to compress a file with a ".dmp"/".dump" extension, which could be a step in a process of dump file exfiltration.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of WinRAR with a command line in which ".dmp" or ".dump" appears accidentally
Legitimate use of WinRAR to compress WER ".dmp" files for troubleshooting

rules.title: Command Line Execution with Suspicious URL and AppData Strings
rules.description: Detects a suspicious command line execution that includes an URL and AppData string in the command line parameters as used by several droppers (js/vbs > powershell)
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: PowerShell SAM Copy
rules.description: Detects suspicious PowerShell scripts accessing SAM hives
falsepositives: PowerShell scripts fixing HiveNightmare / SeriousSAM ACLs

rules.title: Suspicious Modification Of Scheduled Tasks
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker tries to modify an already existing scheduled tasks to run from a suspicious location
Attackers can create a simple looking task in order to avoid detection on creation as it's often the most focused on
Instead they modify the task after creation to include their malicious payload

rules.title: Renamed Plink Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed version of the Plink binary

rules.title: System Network Connections Discovery Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system they are currently accessing or from remote systems by querying for information over the network.

rules.title: REGISTER_APP.VBS Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of a Microsoft signed script 'REGISTER_APP.VBS' to register a VSS/VDS Provider as a COM+ application.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the script. Always investigate what's being registered to confirm if it's benign

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Consent and Comctl32 - Process
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using consent.exe and comctl32.dll (UACMe 22)

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Invoking Inline VBScript
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that invokes inline VBScript as seen being used by UNC2452

rules.title: Suspicious Double Extension File Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious use of an .exe extension after a non-executable file extension like .pdf.exe, a set of spaces or underlines to cloak the executable file in spear phishing campaigns
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @blu3_team (idea), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Curl and PowerShell Execution Combo
rules.description:
Detects the creation of a scheduled task using schtasks.exe, potentially in combination with curl for downloading payloads and PowerShell for executing them.
This facilitates executing malicious payloads or connecting with C&C server persistently without dropping the malware sample on the host.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of schtasks for administrative purposes.
Automation scripts combining curl and PowerShell in controlled environments.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Mofcomp Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the "mofcomp" utility as a child of a suspicious shell or script running utility or by having a suspicious path in the commandline.
The "mofcomp" utility parses a file containing MOF statements and adds the classes and class instances defined in the file to the WMI repository.
Attackers abuse this utility to install malicious MOF scripts

rules.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Uncommon Script Extension Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode to execute an script with a potentially uncommon extension.
Initial baselining of the allowed extension list is required.
falsepositives: False postitve might occur with legitimate or uncommon extensions used internally. Initial baseline is required.

rules.title: Potential Script Proxy Execution Via CL_Mutexverifiers.ps1
rules.description: Detects the use of the Microsoft signed script "CL_mutexverifiers" to proxy the execution of additional PowerShell script commands
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova, frack113

rules.title: Always Install Elevated MSI Spawned Cmd And Powershell
rules.description: Detects Windows Installer service (msiexec.exe) spawning "cmd" or "powershell"

rules.title: Gpscript Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the LOLBIN gpscript, which executes logon or startup scripts configured in Group Policy
falsepositives: Legitimate uses of logon scripts distributed via group policy

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via Squirrel.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" to download arbitrary files. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
falsepositives: Expected FP with some Electron based applications such as (1Clipboard, Beaker Browser, Caret, Discord, GitHub Desktop, etc.)

rules.title: PowerShell Defender Threat Severity Default Action Set to 'Allow' or 'NoAction'
rules.description:
Detects the use of PowerShell to execute the 'Set-MpPreference' cmdlet to configure Windows Defender's threat severity default action to 'Allow' (value '6') or 'NoAction' (value '9').
This is a highly suspicious configuration change that effectively disables Defender's ability to automatically mitigate threats of a certain severity level.
An attacker might use this technique via the command line to bypass defenses before executing payloads.

rules.title: Powershell Defender Disable Scan Feature
rules.description: Detects requests to disable Microsoft Defender features using PowerShell commands
falsepositives: Other Cmdlets that may use the same parameters

rules.title: Suspicious Invoke-WebRequest Execution With DirectIP
rules.description: Detects calls to PowerShell with Invoke-WebRequest cmdlet using direct IP access

rules.title: Potential SPN Enumeration Via Setspn.EXE
rules.description: Detects service principal name (SPN) enumeration used for Kerberoasting

rules.title: PPL Tampering Via WerFaultSecure
rules.description:
Detects potential abuse of WerFaultSecure.exe to dump Protected Process Light (PPL) processes like LSASS or to freeze security solutions (EDR/antivirus).
This technique is used by tools such as EDR-Freeze and WSASS to bypass PPL protections and access sensitive information or disable security software.
Distinct command line patterns help identify the specific tool:
- WSASS usage typically shows: "WSASS.exe WerFaultSecure.exe [PID]" in ParentCommandLine
- EDR-Freeze usage typically shows: "EDR-Freeze_[version].exe [PID] [timeout]" in ParentCommandLine
Legitimate debugging operations using WerFaultSecure are rare in production environments and should be investigated.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of WerFaultSecure for debugging purposes

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via ConfigSecurityPolicy.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "ConfigSecurityPolicy.EXE", a binary part of Windows Defender used to manage settings in Windows Defender.
Users can configure different pilot collections for each of the co-management workloads.
It can be abused by attackers in order to upload or download files.

rules.title: Suspicious Splwow64 Without Params
rules.description: Detects suspicious Splwow64.exe process without any command line parameters

rules.title: Pubprn.vbs Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of the 'Pubprn.vbs' Microsoft signed script to execute commands.

rules.title: Greedy File Deletion Using Del
rules.description: Detects execution of the "del" builtin command to remove files using greedy/wildcard expression. This is often used by malware to delete content of folders that perhaps contains the initial malware infection or to delete evidence.

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation To LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects unknown program using commandline flags usually used by tools such as PsExec and PAExec to start programs with SYSTEM Privileges
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Weird admins that rename their tools
Software companies that bundle PsExec/PAExec with their software and rename it, so that it is less embarrassing

rules.title: Suspicious Outlook Child Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process spawning from an Outlook process.
authors: Michael Haag, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Elastic, FPT.EagleEye Team

rules.title: Ruby Inline Command Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of ruby using the "-e" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live ruby code.

rules.title: Private Keys Reconnaissance Via CommandLine Tools
rules.description: Adversaries may search for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credential

rules.title: Remote File Download Via Desktopimgdownldr Utility
rules.description: Detects the desktopimgdownldr utility being used to download a remote file. An adversary may use desktopimgdownldr to download arbitrary files as an alternative to certutil.

rules.title: Screen Capture Activity Via Psr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of Windows Problem Steps Recorder (psr.exe), a utility used to record the user screen and clicks.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Logon Scripts - CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new LogonScript to the registry value "UserInitMprLogonScript" for potential persistence
falsepositives: Legitimate addition of Logon Scripts via the command line by administrators or third party tools

rules.title: Curl Download And Execute Combination
rules.description: Adversaries can use curl to download payloads remotely and execute them. Curl is included by default in Windows 10 build 17063 and later.

rules.title: Deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via WMI with PowerShell
rules.description: Detects deletion of Windows Volume Shadow Copies with PowerShell code and Get-WMIObject. This technique is used by numerous ransomware families such as Sodinokibi/REvil

rules.title: Delete All Scheduled Tasks
rules.description: Detects the usage of schtasks with the delete flag and the asterisk symbol to delete all tasks from the schedule of the local computer, including tasks scheduled by other users.

rules.title: Vulnerable Driver Blocklist Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects tampering of the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist registry via command line tools such as PowerShell or REG.EXE.
The Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is a security feature that helps prevent the loading of known vulnerable drivers.
Disabling this feature may indicate an attempt to bypass security controls, often targeted by threat actors
to facilitate the installation of malicious or vulnerable drivers, particularly in scenarios involving Endpoint Detection and Response
falsepositives: It is very unlikely for legitimate activities to disable the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist via command line tools; thus it is recommended to investigate promptly.

rules.title: Potential Process Reconnaissance via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "wmic" with the "process" flag, which might indicate an attempt to perform reconnaissance on running processes.
Adversaries may use wmic to query for running processes and their details as part of their reconnaissance efforts.

rules.title: Cloudflared Quick Tunnel Execution
rules.description:
Detects creation of an ad-hoc Cloudflare Quick Tunnel, which can be used to tunnel local services such as HTTP, RDP, SSH and SMB.
The free TryCloudflare Quick Tunnel will generate a random subdomain on trycloudflare[.]com, following a call to api[.]trycloudflare[.]com.
The tool has been observed in use by threat groups including Akira ransomware.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of Cloudflare Quick Tunnel

rules.title: PowerShell MSI Install via WindowsInstaller COM From Remote Location
rules.description:
Detects the execution of PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the
Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`) hosted remotely.
This could be indication of malicious software deployment or lateral movement attempts using Windows Installer functionality.
And the usage of WindowsInstaller COM object rather than msiexec could be an attempt to bypass the detection.

rules.title: WSL Child Process Anomaly
rules.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes spawning from a WSL process. This could indicate an attempt to evade parent/child relationship detections or persistence attempts via cron using WSL

rules.title: Suspicious Persistence Via VMwareToolBoxCmd.EXE VM State Change Script
rules.description: Detects execution of the "VMwareToolBoxCmd.exe" with the "script" and "set" flag to setup a specific script that's located in a potentially suspicious location to run for a specific VM state

rules.title: Dumping Process via Sqldumper.exe
rules.description: Detects process dump via legitimate sqldumper.exe binary

rules.title: Read Contents From Stdin Via Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detect the use of "<" to read and potentially execute a file via cmd.exe

rules.title: DLL Loaded via CertOC.EXE
rules.description: Detects when a user installs certificates by using CertOC.exe to loads the target DLL file.

rules.title: Renamed PingCastle Binary Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "PingCastle" binary based on the PE metadata fields.

rules.title: Direct Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects direct modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry using reg.exe.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: SQLite Chromium Profile Data DB Access
rules.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Chromium-based browsers for potential data stealing.

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Types
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification on a suspicious schedule type
falsepositives: Legitimate processes that run at logon. Filter according to your environment

rules.title: Arbitrary Shell Command Execution Via Settingcontent-Ms
rules.description: The .SettingContent-ms file type was introduced in Windows 10 and allows a user to create "shortcuts" to various Windows 10 setting pages. These files are simply XML and contain paths to various Windows 10 settings binaries.

rules.title: Hacktool Execution - Imphash
rules.description: Detects the execution of different Windows based hacktools via their import hash (imphash) even if the files have been renamed
falsepositives: Legitimate use of one of these tools

rules.title: Exchange PowerShell Snap-Ins Usage
rules.description: Detects adding and using Exchange PowerShell snap-ins to export mailbox data. As seen used by HAFNIUM and APT27

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Using Msdt.EXE
rules.description: Detects processes leveraging the "ms-msdt" handler or the "msdt.exe" binary to execute arbitrary commands as seen in the follina (CVE-2022-30190) vulnerability

rules.title: Suspicious SYSTEM User Process Creation
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process creation as SYSTEM user (suspicious program or command line parameter)
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), David ANDRE (additional keywords)
falsepositives: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: HackTool - SharPersist Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the hacktool SharPersist - used to deploy various different kinds of persistence mechanisms

rules.title: Renamed NirCmd.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "NirCmd.exe" binary based on the PE metadata fields.

rules.title: PUA - Adidnsdump Execution
rules.description:
This tool enables enumeration and exporting of all DNS records in the zone for recon purposes of internal networks Python 3 and python.exe must be installed,
Usee to Query/modify DNS records for Active Directory integrated DNS via LDAP

rules.title: HackTool - Dumpert Process Dumper Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Dumpert process dumper, which dumps the lsass.exe process memory

rules.title: Renamed FTP.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "ftp.exe" binary based on the PE metadata fields

rules.title: Suspicious Usage of For Loop with Recursive Directory Search in CMD
rules.description:
Detects suspicious usage of the cmd.exe 'for /f' loop combined with the 'tokens=' parameter and a recursive directory listing.
This pattern may indicate an attempt to discover and execute system binaries dynamically, for example powershell, a technique sometimes used by attackers to evade detection.
This behavior has been observed in various malicious lnk files.

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation VAR+ Launcher
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated use of Environment Variables to execute PowerShell

rules.title: Suspicious Chromium Browser Instance Executed With Custom Extension
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process spawning a Chromium based browser process with the 'load-extension' flag to start an instance with a custom extension

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Setupapi.dll Activity
rules.description: setupapi.dll library provide InstallHinfSection function for processing INF files. INF file may contain instructions allowing to create values in the registry, modify files and install drivers. This technique could be used to obtain persistence via modifying one of Run or RunOnce registry keys, run process or use other DLLs chain calls (see references) InstallHinfSection function in setupapi.dll calls runonce.exe executable regardless of actual content of INF file.
falsepositives: Scripts and administrative tools that use INF files for driver installation with setupapi.dll

rules.title: RestrictedAdminMode Registry Value Tampering - ProcCreation
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "DisableRestrictedAdmin" registry value in order to disable or enable RestrictedAdmin mode.
RestrictedAdmin mode prevents the transmission of reusable credentials to the remote system to which you connect using Remote Desktop.
This prevents your credentials from being harvested during the initial connection process if the remote server has been compromise

rules.title: Potential Register_App.Vbs LOLScript Abuse
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of the "register_app.vbs" script that is part of the Windows SDK. The script offers the capability to register new VSS/VDS Provider as a COM+ application. Attackers can use this to install malicious DLLs for persistence and execution.
falsepositives: Other VB scripts that leverage the same starting command line flags

rules.title: Start Windows Service Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "net.exe" command to start a service using the "start" flag
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user executes a service for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Invocation of Active Directory Diagnostic Tool (ntdsutil.exe)
rules.description: Detects execution of ntdsutil.exe, which can be used for various attacks against the NTDS database (NTDS.DIT)

rules.title: Wscript Shell Run In CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the presence of the keywords "Wscript", "Shell" and "Run" in the command, which could indicate a suspicious activity
falsepositives: Inline scripting can be used by some rare third party applications or administrators. Investigate and apply additional filters accordingly

rules.title: PUA - Crassus Execution
rules.description: Detects Crassus, a Windows privilege escalation discovery tool, based on PE metadata characteristics.

rules.title: Renamed Visual Studio Code Tunnel Execution
rules.description: Detects renamed Visual Studio Code tunnel execution. Attackers can abuse this functionality to establish a C2 channel

rules.title: Indirect Command Execution From Script File Via Bash.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of Microsoft bash launcher without any flags to execute the content of a bash script directly.
This can be used to potentially bypass defenses and execute Linux or Windows-based binaries directly via bash.

rules.title: Suspicious Response File Execution Via Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with the "-f" flag in order to load a response file with a non-".rsp" extension.

rules.title: Microsoft IIS Service Account Password Dumped
rules.description: Detects the Internet Information Services (IIS) command-line tool, AppCmd, being used to list passwords
authors: Tim Rauch, Janantha Marasinghe, Elastic (original idea)
