rules.title: Potential SSH Tunnel Persistence Install Using A Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects the creation of new scheduled tasks via commandline, using Schtasks.exe. This rule detects tasks creating that call OpenSSH, which may indicate the creation of reverse SSH tunnel to the attacker's server.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - TacticalRMM Agent Registration to Potentially Attacker-Controlled Server
rules.description:
Detects TacticalRMM agent installations where the --api, --auth, and related flags are used on the command line.
These parameters configure the agent to connect to a specific RMM server with authentication, client ID, and site ID.
This technique could indicate a threat actor attempting to register the agent with an attacker-controlled RMM infrastructure silently.

rules.title: WebDav Client Execution Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description:
Detects "svchost.exe" spawning "rundll32.exe" with command arguments like "C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie".
This could be an indicator of exfiltration or use of WebDav to launch code (hosted on a WebDav server).

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Regsvr32 HTTP IP Pattern
rules.description: Detects regsvr32 execution to download and install DLLs located remotely where the address is an IP address.
falsepositives: FQDNs that start with a number such as "7-Zip"

rules.title: File Download Via Bitsadmin To A Suspicious Target Folder
rules.description: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file to a suspicious target folder
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Procdump Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of the SysInternals Procdump utility
falsepositives: Legitimate use of procdump by a developer or administrator

rules.title: Potential Adplus.EXE Abuse
rules.description: Detects execution of "AdPlus.exe", a binary that is part of the Windows SDK that can be used as a LOLBIN in order to dump process memory and execute arbitrary commands.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of Adplus for debugging purposes

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Potential MeshAgent Execution - Windows
rules.description:
Detects potential execution of MeshAgent which is a tool used for remote access.
Historical data shows that threat actors rename MeshAgent binary to evade detection.
Matching command lines with the '--meshServiceName' argument can indicate that the MeshAgent is being used for remote access.

rules.title: Sensitive File Dump Via Print.EXE
rules.description: Detects the abuse of the Print.exe utility for credential harvesting which involves using Print.Exe to copy sensitive files such as ntds.dit, SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM from the Windows directory in order to extract credentials, locally or remotely.

rules.title: Sticky Key Like Backdoor Execution
rules.description: Detects the usage and installation of a backdoor that uses an option to register a malicious debugger for built-in tools that are accessible in the login screen
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), @twjackomo, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious High IntegrityLevel Conhost Legacy Option
rules.description: ForceV1 asks for information directly from the kernel space. Conhost connects to the console application. High IntegrityLevel means the process is running with elevated privileges, such as an Administrator context.
falsepositives: Very Likely, including launching cmd.exe via Run As Administrator

rules.title: Visual Studio Code Tunnel Service Installation
rules.description: Detects the installation of VsCode tunnel (code-tunnel) as a service.
falsepositives: Legitimate installation of code-tunnel as a service

rules.title: Renamed BOINC Client Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed BOINC binary.

rules.title: Hidden Powershell in Link File Pattern
rules.description: Detects events that appear when a user click on a link file with a powershell command in it

rules.title: Potential AMSI Bypass Via .NET Reflection
rules.description: Detects Request to "amsiInitFailed" that can be used to disable AMSI Scanning

rules.title: Install New Package Via Winget Local Manifest
rules.description:
Detects usage of winget to install applications via manifest file. Adversaries can abuse winget to download payloads remotely and execute them.
The manifest option enables you to install an application by passing in a YAML file directly to the client.
Winget can be used to download and install exe, msi or msix files later.
falsepositives: Some false positives are expected in some environment that may use this functionality to install and test their custom applications

rules.title: New Port Forwarding Rule Added Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of netsh commands that configure a new port forwarding (PortProxy) rule
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), omkar72, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
falsepositives: WSL2 network bridge PowerShell script used for WSL/Kubernetes/Docker (e.g. https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/4150#issuecomment-504209723)

rules.title: PUA - Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Fast Reverse Proxy. frp is a fast reverse proxy to help you expose a local server behind a NAT or firewall to the Internet.

rules.title: HackTool - Empire PowerShell UAC Bypass
rules.description: Detects some Empire PowerShell UAC bypass methods

rules.title: Port Forwarding Activity Via SSH.EXE
rules.description: Detects port forwarding activity via SSH.exe
falsepositives: Administrative activity using a remote port forwarding to a local port

rules.title: Regsvr32 Execution From Highly Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects execution of regsvr32 where the DLL is located in a highly suspicious locations

rules.title: Shell32 DLL Execution in Suspicious Directory
rules.description: Detects shell32.dll executing a DLL in a suspicious directory

rules.title: Potential Homoglyph Attack Using Lookalike Characters
rules.description:
Detects the presence of unicode characters which are homoglyphs, or identical in appearance, to ASCII letter characters.
This is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques. Only "perfect" homoglyphs are included; these are characters that
are indistinguishable from ASCII characters and thus may make excellent candidates for homoglyph attack characters.
falsepositives: Commandlines with legitimate Cyrillic text; will likely require tuning (or not be usable) in countries where these alphabets are in use.

rules.title: Findstr Launching .lnk File
rules.description: Detects usage of findstr to identify and execute a lnk file as seen within the HHS redirect attack

rules.title: Sysinternals PsService Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals PsService which can be abused for service reconnaissance and tampering
falsepositives: Legitimate use of PsService by an administrator

rules.title: Renamed ZOHO Dctask64 Execution
rules.description:
Detects a renamed "dctask64.exe" execution, a signed binary by ZOHO Corporation part of ManageEngine Endpoint Central.
This binary can be abused for DLL injection, arbitrary command and process execution.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Loaded Module Enumeration Via Tasklist.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enumeration of a specific DLL or EXE being used by a binary via "tasklist.exe".
This is often used by attackers in order to find the specific process identifier (PID) that is using the DLL in question.
In order to dump the process memory or perform other nefarious actions.

rules.title: Netsh Allow Group Policy on Microsoft Defender Firewall
rules.description: Adversaries may modify system firewalls in order to bypass controls limiting network usage

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Shutdown
rules.description: Use of the commandline to shutdown or reboot windows

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell Parameter Substring
rules.description: Detects suspicious PowerShell invocation with a parameter substring
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Daniel Bohannon (idea), Roberto Rodriguez (Fix)

rules.title: SyncAppvPublishingServer VBS Execute Arbitrary PowerShell Code
rules.description: Executes arbitrary PowerShell code using SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs

rules.title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Binary Rename
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed binary often used by attackers or malware leveraging new Sysmon OriginalFileName datapoint.
authors: Matthew Green @mgreen27, Ecco, James Pemberton @4A616D6573, oscd.community, Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)
falsepositives: Custom applications use renamed binaries adding slight change to binary name. Typically this is easy to spot and add to whitelist

rules.title: HackTool - CreateMiniDump Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of CreateMiniDump hack tool used to dump the LSASS process memory for credential extraction on the attacker's machine

rules.title: File Deletion Via Del
rules.description:
Detects execution of the builtin "del"/"erase" commands in order to delete files.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was done within a network and how.
Removal of these files can occur during an intrusion, or as part of a post-intrusion process to minimize the adversary's footprint.
falsepositives: False positives levels will differ Depending on the environment. You can use a combination of ParentImage and other keywords from the CommandLine field to filter legitimate activity

rules.title: Hacktool Execution - PE Metadata
rules.description: Detects the execution of different Windows based hacktools via PE metadata (company, product, etc.) even if the files have been renamed

rules.title: Sysmon Discovery Via Default Driver Altitude Using Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "findstr" with the argument "385201". Which could indicate potential discovery of an installed Sysinternals Sysmon service using the default driver altitude (even if the name is changed).

rules.title: PUA - Seatbelt Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the PUA/Recon tool Seatbelt via PE information of command line parameters

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Existing Service Tampering
rules.description: Detects the modification of an existing service in order to execute an arbitrary payload when the service is started or killed as a potential method for persistence.

rules.title: HKTL - SharpSuccessor Privilege Escalation Tool Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of SharpSuccessor, a tool used to exploit the BadSuccessor attack for privilege escalation in WinServer 2025 Active Directory environments.
Successful usage of this tool can let the attackers gain the domain admin privileges by exploiting the BadSuccessor vulnerability.

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation Involving Temp Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involves a temporary folder and runs only once

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Of Wermgr.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious Windows Error Reporting manager (wermgr.exe) child process

rules.title: HackTool - Hashcat Password Cracker Execution
rules.description: Execute Hashcat.exe with provided SAM file from registry of Windows and Password list to crack against
falsepositives: Tools that use similar command line flags and values

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using NTFS Reparse Point - Process
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using NTFS reparse point and wusa.exe DLL hijacking (UACMe 36)

rules.title: Windows Shell/Scripting Processes Spawning Suspicious Programs
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of a Windows shell and scripting processes such as wscript, rundll32, powershell, mshta...etc.

rules.title: Windows Admin Share Mount Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects when an admin share is mounted using net.exe
authors: oscd.community, Teymur Kheirkhabarov @HeirhabarovT, Zach Stanford @svch0st, wagga

rules.title: Suspicious Explorer Process with Whitespace Padding - ClickFix/FileFix
rules.description:
Detects process creation with suspicious whitespace padding followed by a '#' character, which may indicate ClickFix or FileFix techniques used to conceal malicious commands from visual inspection.
ClickFix and FileFix are social engineering attack techniques where adversaries distribute phishing documents or malicious links that deceive users into opening the Windows Run dialog box or File Explorer search bar.
The victims are then instructed to paste commands from their clipboard, which contain extensive whitespace padding using various Unicode space characters to push the actual malicious command far to the right, effectively hiding it from immediate view.

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via MSPUB.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "MSPUB" (Microsoft Publisher) to download arbitrary files

rules.title: Notepad Password Files Discovery
rules.description: Detects the execution of Notepad to open a file that has the string "password" which may indicate unauthorized access to credentials or suspicious activity.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of opening files from remote hosts by administrators or users. However, storing passwords in text readable format could potentially be a violation of the organization's policy. Any match should be investigated further.

rules.title: PowerShell Download Pattern
rules.description: Detects a Powershell process that contains download commands in its command line string
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro

rules.title: Domain Trust Discovery Via Dsquery
rules.description: Detects execution of "dsquery.exe" for domain trust discovery
authors: E.M. Anhaus, Tony Lambert, oscd.community, omkar72
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the utilities by legitimate user for legitimate reason

rules.title: UAC Bypass Tools Using ComputerDefaults
rules.description: Detects tools such as UACMe used to bypass UAC with computerdefaults.exe (UACMe 59)

rules.title: Process Creation Using Sysnative Folder
rules.description: Detects process creation events that use the Sysnative folder (common for CobaltStrike spawns)

rules.title: Suspicious Process Created Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects WMIC executing "process call create" with suspicious calls to processes such as "rundll32", "regsrv32", etc.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Change Default File Association Via Assoc
rules.description:
Detects file association changes using the builtin "assoc" command.
When a file is opened, the default program used to open the file (also called the file association or handler) is checked. File association selections are stored in the Windows Registry and can be edited by users, administrators, or programs that have Registry access or by administrators using the built-in assoc utility. Applications can modify the file association for a given file extension to call an arbitrary program when a file with the given extension is opened.

rules.title: Potential Mftrace.EXE Abuse
rules.description: Detects child processes of the "Trace log generation tool for Media Foundation Tools" (Mftrace.exe) which can abused to execute arbitrary binaries.

rules.title: New Process Created Via Taskmgr.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of a process via the Windows task manager. This might be an attempt to bypass UAC

rules.title: Process Execution From A Potentially Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detects a potentially suspicious execution from an uncommon folder.

rules.title: Hardware Model Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of WMIC with the "csproduct" which is used to obtain information such as hardware models and vendor information

rules.title: Potential Data Stealing Via Chromium Headless Debugging
rules.description: Detects chromium based browsers starting in headless and debugging mode and pointing to a user profile. This could be a sign of data stealing or remote control

rules.title: Use NTFS Short Name in Image
rules.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid Image based detection

rules.title: Driver/DLL Installation Via Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with "INSTALLDRIVER" which installs a new ODBC driver. Attackers abuse this to install and run malicious DLLs.
falsepositives: Legitimate driver DLLs being registered via "odbcconf" will generate false positives. Investigate the path of the DLL and its contents to determine if the action is authorized.

rules.title: Certificate Exported Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of the certutil with the "exportPFX" flag which allows the utility to export certificates.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: There legitimate reasons to export certificates. Investigate the activity to determine if it's benign

rules.title: VolumeShadowCopy Symlink Creation Via Mklink
rules.description: Shadow Copies storage symbolic link creation using operating systems utilities
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator working with shadow copies, access for backup purposes

rules.title: Suspicious Csi.exe Usage
rules.description: Csi.exe is a signed binary from Microsoft that comes with Visual Studio and provides C# interactive capabilities. It can be used to run C# code from a file passed as a parameter in command line. Early version of this utility provided with Microsoft “Roslyn” Community Technology Preview was named 'rcsi.exe'

rules.title: Potential UAC Bypass Via Sdclt.EXE
rules.description: A General detection for sdclt being spawned as an elevated process. This could be an indicator of sdclt being used for bypass UAC techniques.

rules.title: ETW Logging Tamper In .NET Processes Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects changes to environment variables related to ETW logging via the CommandLine.
This could indicate potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.

rules.title: Compressed File Creation Via Tar.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to create a compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities to compress or encrypt data before exfiltration.

rules.title: Directory Removal Via Rmdir
rules.description:
Detects execution of the builtin "rmdir" command in order to delete directories.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was done within a network and how.
Removal of these files can occur during an intrusion, or as part of a post-intrusion process to minimize the adversary's footprint.

rules.title: HackTool - Sliver C2 Implant Activity Pattern
rules.description: Detects process activity patterns as seen being used by Sliver C2 framework implants
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Hiding Files with Attrib.exe
rules.description: Detects usage of attrib.exe to hide files from users.
falsepositives: IgfxCUIService.exe hiding *.cui files via .bat script (attrib.exe a child of cmd.exe and igfxCUIService.exe is the parent of the cmd.exe)

rules.title: Suspicious File Downloaded From File-Sharing Website Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with certain flags that allow the utility to download files from file-sharing websites.

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Execution
rules.description: This rule detect common flag combinations used by CrackMapExec in order to detect its use even if the binary has been replaced.

rules.title: Harvesting Of Wifi Credentials Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detect the harvesting of wifi credentials using netsh.exe

rules.title: Suspicious Vsls-Agent Command With AgentExtensionPath Load
rules.description: Detects Microsoft Visual Studio vsls-agent.exe lolbin execution with a suspicious library load using the --agentExtensionPath parameter
falsepositives: False positives depend on custom use of vsls-agent.exe

rules.title: New Kernel Driver Via SC.EXE
rules.description: Detects creation of a new service (kernel driver) with the type "kernel"
falsepositives: Rare legitimate installation of kernel drivers via sc.exe

rules.title: Computer Discovery And Export Via Get-ADComputer Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects usage of the Get-ADComputer cmdlet to collect computer information and output it to a file
falsepositives: Legitimate admin scripts may use the same technique, it's better to exclude specific computers or users who execute these commands or scripts often

rules.title: Suspicious Microsoft Office Child Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process spawning from one of the Microsoft Office suite products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Publisher, Visio, etc.)
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, FPT.EagleEye Team, Vadim Khrykov, Cyb3rEng, Michael Haag, Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, @scythe_io

rules.title: DSInternals Suspicious PowerShell Cmdlets
rules.description:
Detects execution and usage of the DSInternals PowerShell module. Which can be used to perform what might be considered as suspicious activity such as dumping DPAPI backup keys or manipulating NTDS.DIT files.
The DSInternals PowerShell Module exposes several internal features of Active Directory and Azure Active Directory. These include FIDO2 and NGC key auditing, offline ntds.dit file manipulation, password auditing, DC recovery from IFM backups and password hash calculation.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of DSInternals for administration or audit purpose.

rules.title: Dism Remove Online Package
rules.description: Deployment Image Servicing and Management tool. DISM is used to enumerate, install, uninstall, configure, and update features and packages in Windows images

rules.title: Potential Obfuscated Ordinal Call Via Rundll32
rules.description: Detects execution of "rundll32" with potential obfuscated ordinal calls
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - TruffleHog Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of TruffleHog, a tool used to search for secrets in different platforms like Git, Jira, Slack, SharePoint, etc. that could be used maliciously.
While it is a legitimate tool, intended for use in CI pipelines and security assessments,
It was observed in the Shai-Hulud malware campaign targeting npm packages to steal sensitive information.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of TruffleHog by security teams or developers.

rules.title: File Download Using Notepad++ GUP Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of the Notepad++ updater (gup) from a process other than Notepad++ to download files.
falsepositives: Other parent processes other than notepad++ using GUP that are not currently identified

rules.title: Suspicious CertReq Command to Download
rules.description:
Detects a suspicious CertReq execution downloading a file.
This behavior is often used by attackers to download additional payloads or configuration files.
Certreq is a built-in Windows utility used to request and retrieve certificates from a certification authority (CA). However, it can be abused by threat actors for malicious purposes.

rules.title: Obfuscated PowerShell OneLiner Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a specific OneLiner to download and execute powershell modules in memory.

rules.title: Process Proxy Execution Via Squirrel.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" binary to execute arbitrary processes. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
falsepositives: Expected FP with some Electron based applications such as (1Clipboard, Beaker Browser, Caret, Discord, GitHub Desktop, etc.)

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Defender Registry Key Tampering Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to tamper with different Windows Defender registry keys in order to disable some important features related to protection and detection
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Rare legitimate use by administrators to test software (should always be investigated)

rules.title: PUA - Suspicious ActiveDirectory Enumeration Via AdFind.EXE
rules.description: Detects active directory enumeration activity using known AdFind CLI flags

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via MSOHTMED.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "MSOHTMED" to download arbitrary files

rules.title: Run PowerShell Script from ADS
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script execution from Alternate Data Stream (ADS)

rules.title: Launch-VsDevShell.PS1 Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of the 'Launch-VsDevShell.ps1' Microsoft signed script to execute commands.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the script by a developer

rules.title: File Download Via Windows Defender MpCmpRun.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of Windows Defender MpCmdRun.EXE to download files

rules.title: HackTool - Impacket Tools Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of different compiled Windows binaries of the impacket toolset (based on names or part of their names - could lead to false positives)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the impacket tools

rules.title: Potential Browser Data Stealing
rules.description:
Adversaries may acquire credentials from web browsers by reading files specific to the target browser.
Web browsers commonly save credentials such as website usernames and passwords so that they do not need to be entered manually in the future.
Web browsers typically store the credentials in an encrypted format within a credential store.

rules.title: Permission Misconfiguration Reconnaissance Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects usage of findstr with the "EVERYONE" or "BUILTIN" keywords.
This was seen being used in combination with "icacls" and other utilities to spot misconfigured files or folders permissions.

rules.title: Python Spawning Pretty TTY on Windows
rules.description: Detects python spawning a pretty tty

rules.title: SQLite Firefox Profile Data DB Access
rules.description: Detect usage of the "sqlite" binary to query databases in Firefox and other Gecko-based browsers for potential data stealing.

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Defender Folder Exclusion Added Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" to add Defender folder exclusions. Qbot has been seen using this technique to add exclusions for folders within AppData and ProgramData.

rules.title: Suspicious Plink Port Forwarding
rules.description: Detects suspicious Plink tunnel port forwarding to a local port
falsepositives: Administrative activity using a remote port forwarding to a local port

rules.title: Sysinternals PsSuspend Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of Sysinternals PsSuspend which can be abused to suspend critical processes

rules.title: Filter Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
rules.description: Detect filter driver unloading activity via fltmc.exe

rules.title: Use of Wfc.exe
rules.description: The Workflow Command-line Compiler can be used for AWL bypass and is listed in Microsoft's recommended block rules.
falsepositives: Legitimate use by a software developer

rules.title: Application Termination Attempt via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects an attempt to terminate a process via "wmic" with the "call terminate" flag. Adversaries may
use wmic to terminate security products or other applications on the compromised host. This event is
triggered on on attempt and process creation can be either successful or unsuccessful.

rules.title: UAC Bypass via ICMLuaUtil
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using ICMLuaUtil Elevated COM interface

rules.title: Renamed ProcDump Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a renamed ProcDump executable.
This often done by attackers or malware in order to evade defensive mechanisms.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Procdump illegally bundled with legitimate software.
Administrators who rename binaries (should be investigated).

rules.title: Suspicious MsiExec Embedding Parent
rules.description: Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy the execution of malicious payloads

rules.title: Taskkill Symantec Endpoint Protection
rules.description:
Detects one of the possible scenarios for disabling Symantec Endpoint Protection.
Symantec Endpoint Protection antivirus software services incorrectly implement the protected service mechanism.
As a result, the NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM user can execute the taskkill /im command several times ccSvcHst.exe /f, thereby killing the process belonging to the service, and thus shutting down the service.

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Execution With Image Extension
rules.description: Detects the execution of Rundll32.exe with DLL files masquerading as image files

rules.title: UEFI Persistence Via Wpbbin - ProcessCreation
rules.description: Detects execution of the binary "wpbbin" which is used as part of the UEFI based persistence method described in the reference section
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the file by hardware manufacturer such as lenovo (Thanks @0gtweet for the tip)

rules.title: TrustedPath UAC Bypass Pattern
rules.description: Detects indicators of a UAC bypass method by mocking directories

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary File Download Using Office Application
rules.description: Detects potential arbitrary file download using a Microsoft Office application
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Beyu Denis, oscd.community

rules.title: Use Icacls to Hide File to Everyone
rules.description: Detect use of icacls to deny access for everyone in Users folder sometimes used to hide malicious files

rules.title: Deleted Data Overwritten Via Cipher.EXE
rules.description:
Detects usage of the "cipher" built-in utility in order to overwrite deleted data from disk.
Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources.
Data destruction is likely to render stored data irrecoverable by forensic techniques through overwriting files or data on local and remote drives

rules.title: Suspicious Extrac32 Alternate Data Stream Execution
rules.description: Extract data from cab file and hide it in an alternate data stream

rules.title: CMSTP UAC Bypass via COM Object Access
rules.description: Detects UAC Bypass Attempt Using Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer Autoelevate-capable COM Objects (e.g. UACMe ID of 41, 43, 58 or 65)
falsepositives: Legitimate CMSTP use (unlikely in modern enterprise environments)

rules.title: RDP Enable or Disable via Win32_TerminalServiceSetting WMI Class
rules.description:
Detects enabling or disabling of Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) using alternate methods such as WMIC or PowerShell.
In PowerShell one-liner commands, the "SetAllowTSConnections" method of the "Win32_TerminalServiceSetting" class may be used to enable or disable RDP.
In WMIC, the "rdtoggle" alias or "Win32_TerminalServiceSetting" class may be used for the same purpose.
authors: Daniel Koifman (KoifSec), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate system administrators enabling RDP for remote support

rules.title: Unusual Parent Process For Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious parent process for cmd.exe

rules.title: Suspicious Velociraptor Child Process
rules.description: Detects the suspicious use of the Velociraptor DFIR tool to execute other tools or download additional payloads, as seen in a campaign where it was abused for remote access and to stage further attacks.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrators or incident responders might use Velociraptor to execute scripts or tools. However, the combination of Velociraptor spawning these specific processes with these command lines is suspicious. Tuning may be required to exclude known administrative actions or specific scripts.

rules.title: Sysinternals PsSuspend Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious execution of Sysinternals PsSuspend, where the utility is used to suspend critical processes such as AV or EDR to bypass defenses

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Obfuscated IEX Invocation
rules.description: Detects all variations of obfuscated powershell IEX invocation code generated by Invoke-Obfuscation framework from the following code block

rules.title: Process Access via TrolleyExpress Exclusion
rules.description: Detects a possible process memory dump that uses the white-listed Citrix TrolleyExpress.exe filename as a way to dump the lsass process memory

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using IDiagnostic Profile
rules.description: Detects the "IDiagnosticProfileUAC" UAC bypass technique

rules.title: Sysmon Driver Unloaded Via Fltmc.EXE
rules.description: Detects possible Sysmon filter driver unloaded via fltmc.exe

rules.title: PUA - NirCmd Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of NirCmd tool for command execution, which could be the result of legitimate administrative activity
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Fake Instance Of Hxtsr.EXE Executed
rules.description:
HxTsr.exe is a Microsoft compressed executable file called Microsoft Outlook Communications.
HxTsr.exe is part of Outlook apps, because it resides in a hidden "WindowsApps" subfolder of "C:\Program Files".
Any instances of hxtsr.exe not in this folder may be malware camouflaging itself as HxTsr.exe

rules.title: Webshell Hacking Activity Patterns
rules.description: Detects certain parent child patterns found in cases in which a web shell is used to perform certain credential dumping or exfiltration activities on a compromised system

rules.title: Use of Remote.exe
rules.description: Remote.exe is part of WinDbg in the Windows SDK and can be used for AWL bypass and running remote files.
falsepositives: Approved installs of Windows SDK with Debugging Tools for Windows (WinDbg).

rules.title: WinRAR Execution in Non-Standard Folder
rules.description: Detects a suspicious WinRAR execution in a folder which is not the default installation folder
falsepositives: Legitimate use of WinRAR in a folder of a software that bundles WinRAR

rules.title: Operator Bloopers Cobalt Strike Modules
rules.description: Detects Cobalt Strike module/commands accidentally entered in CMD shell

rules.title: Uncommon AddinUtil.EXE CommandLine Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) with uncommon Addinroot or Pipelineroot paths. An adversary may execute AddinUtil.exe with uncommon Addinroot/Pipelineroot paths that point to the adversaries Addins.Store payload.

rules.title: Mavinject Inject DLL Into Running Process
rules.description: Detects process injection using the signed Windows tool "Mavinject" via the "INJECTRUNNING" flag

rules.title: PUA - NimScan Execution
rules.description:
Detects usage of NimScan, a portscanner utility.
In early 2025, adversaries were observed using this utility to scan for open ports on remote hosts in a compromised environment.
This rule identifies the execution of NimScan based on the process image name and specific hash values associated with different versions of the tool.

rules.title: Security Tools Keyword Lookup Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "findstr" to search for common names of security tools. Attackers often pipe the results of recon commands such as "tasklist" or "whoami" to "findstr" in order to filter out the results.
This detection focuses on the keywords that the attacker might use as a filter.

rules.title: Local Accounts Discovery
rules.description: Local accounts, System Owner/User discovery using operating systems utilities
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user enumerates local users for legitimate reason

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using ChangePK and SLUI
rules.description: Detects an UAC bypass that uses changepk.exe and slui.exe (UACMe 61)

rules.title: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Uncommon Extension
rules.description: Detects a "regsvr32" execution where the DLL doesn't contain a common file extension.
falsepositives: Other legitimate extensions currently not in the list either from third party or specific Windows components.

rules.title: Python One-Liners with Base64 Decoding
rules.description:
Detects Python one-liners that use base64 decoding functions in command line executions.
Malicious scripts or attackers often use python one-liners to decode and execute base64-encoded payloads, which is a common technique for obfuscation and evasion.
authors: Hugh Ryan (HueCodes), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Python for decoding data, which is uncommon in typical enterprise environments but possible in development or data analysis contexts.

rules.title: Abuse of Service Permissions to Hide Services Via Set-Service
rules.description: Detects usage of the "Set-Service" powershell cmdlet to configure a new SecurityDescriptor that allows a service to be hidden from other utilities such as "sc.exe", "Get-Service"...etc. (Works only in powershell 7)
falsepositives: Rare intended use of hidden services

rules.title: PUA - AdFind.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of Adfind.exe utility, which can be used for reconnaissance in an Active Directory environment

rules.title: CreateDump Process Dump
rules.description: Detects uses of the createdump.exe LOLOBIN utility to dump process memory
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Command lines that use the same flags

rules.title: Potential Shim Database Persistence via Sdbinst.EXE
rules.description:
Detects installation of a new shim using sdbinst.exe.
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims

rules.title: Potential Windows Defender Tampering Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential tampering with Windows Defender settings such as adding exclusion using wmic

rules.title: Process Creation Attempt via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the attempt to create a process via "wmic" with the "process call create" flag, which might
indicate an attempt to execute a malicious process on the compromised host. Adversaries may use
wmic to execute a process on the compromised host as part of their attack. This event is triggered on
on attempt and process creation can be either successful or unsuccessful.
authors: Michael Haag, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), juju4, oscd.community

rules.title: JScript Compiler Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the "jsc.exe" (JScript Compiler).
Attacker might abuse this in order to compile JScript files on the fly and bypassing application whitelisting.
falsepositives: Legitimate use to compile JScript by developers.

rules.title: HTML Help HH.EXE Suspicious Child Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious child process of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Update Agent Empty Cmdline
rules.description: Detects suspicious Windows Update Agent activity in which a wuauclt.exe process command line doesn't contain any command line flags

rules.title: HackTool - PPID Spoofing SelectMyParent Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of parent process ID spoofing tools like Didier Stevens tool SelectMyParent

rules.title: Explorer NOUACCHECK Flag
rules.description: Detects suspicious starts of explorer.exe that use the /NOUACCHECK flag that allows to run all sub processes of that newly started explorer.exe without any UAC checks
falsepositives: Unknown how many legitimate software products use that method

rules.title: COM Object Execution via Xwizard.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Xwizard tool with the "RunWizard" flag and a GUID like argument.
This utility can be abused in order to run custom COM object created in the registry.

rules.title: Process Memory Dump Via Dotnet-Dump
rules.description: Detects the execution of "dotnet-dump" with the "collect" flag. The execution could indicate potential process dumping of critical processes such as LSASS.
falsepositives: Process dumping is the expected behavior of the tool. So false positives are expected in legitimate usage. The PID/Process Name of the process being dumped needs to be investigated

rules.title: PUA - Advanced Port Scanner Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Advanced Port Scanner.

rules.title: Suspicious Ping/Del Command Combination
rules.description: Detects a method often used by ransomware. Which combines the "ping" to wait a couple of seconds and then "del" to delete the file in question. Its used to hide the file responsible for the initial infection for example

rules.title: Potential Excel.EXE DCOM Lateral Movement Via ActivateMicrosoftApp
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of Excel which could be an indicator of lateral movement leveraging the "ActivateMicrosoftApp" Excel DCOM object.

rules.title: Suspicious Recursive Takeown
rules.description: Adversaries can interact with the DACLs using built-in Windows commands takeown which can grant adversaries higher permissions on specific files and folders
falsepositives: Scripts created by developers and admins

rules.title: Potential SMB Relay Attack Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects different hacktools used for relay attacks on Windows for privilege escalation
falsepositives: Legitimate files with these rare hacktool names

rules.title: Outlook EnableUnsafeClientMailRules Setting Enabled
rules.description: Detects an attacker trying to enable the outlook security setting "EnableUnsafeClientMailRules" which allows outlook to run applications or execute macros

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Netsh Helper DLL
rules.description: Detects the execution of netsh with "add helper" flag in order to add a custom helper DLL. This technique can be abused to add a malicious helper DLL that can be used as a persistence proxy that gets called when netsh.exe is executed.

rules.title: VMToolsd Suspicious Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious child process creations of VMware Tools process which may indicate persistence setup

rules.title: HackTool - Default PowerSploit/Empire Scheduled Task Creation
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask via PowerSploit or Empire Default Configuration.

rules.title: PUA - System Informer Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of System Informer, a task manager tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level operations
falsepositives: System Informer is regularly used legitimately by system administrators or developers. Apply additional filters accordingly

rules.title: Potential Reconnaissance Activity Via GatherNetworkInfo.VBS
rules.description: Detects execution of the built-in script located in "C:\Windows\System32\gatherNetworkInfo.vbs". Which can be used to gather information about the target machine

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Firewall Disabled via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects netsh commands that turns off the Windows firewall

rules.title: PUA - Radmin Viewer Utility Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of Radmin which can be abused by an adversary to remotely control Windows machines

rules.title: Potential CommandLine Obfuscation Using Unicode Characters From Suspicious Image
rules.description:
Detects potential commandline obfuscation using unicode characters.
Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the system or in transit.
authors: frack113, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Josh Nickels

rules.title: Remote File Download Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "findstr" with specific flags and a remote share path. This specific set of CLI flags would allow "findstr" to download the content of the file located on the remote share as described in the LOLBAS entry.

rules.title: HackTool - WSASS Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of WSASS, a tool used to dump LSASS memory on Windows systems by leveraging WER's
(Windows Error Reporting) WerFaultSecure.EXE to bypass PPL (Protected Process Light) protections.

rules.title: Suspicious Serv-U Process Pattern
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process pattern which could be a sign of an exploited Serv-U service
falsepositives: Legitimate uses in which users or programs use the SSH service of Serv-U for remote command execution

rules.title: Windows Credential Manager Access via VaultCmd
rules.description: List credentials currently stored in Windows Credential Manager via the native Windows utility vaultcmd.exe

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Created as System
rules.description: Detection of child processes spawned with SYSTEM privileges by parents with LOCAL SERVICE or NETWORK SERVICE accounts
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Roberto Rodriguez (@Cyb3rWard0g), Open Threat Research (OTR)

rules.title: Execute Code with Pester.bat
rules.description: Detects code execution via Pester.bat (Pester - Powershell Modulte for testing)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Pester for writing tests for Powershell scripts and modules

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of VsCode
rules.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes spawning from a VsCode "code.exe" process. This could indicate an attempt of persistence via VsCode tasks or terminal profiles.
falsepositives: In development environment where VsCode is used heavily. False positives may occur when developers use task to compile or execute different types of code. Remove or add processes accordingly

rules.title: Cmd Launched with Hidden Start Flags to Suspicious Targets
rules.description:
Detects cmd.exe executing commands with the "start" utility using "/b" (no window) or "/min" (minimized) flags.
To reduce false positives from standard background tasks, detection is restricted to scenarios where the target is a known script extension or located in suspicious temporary/public directories.
This technique was observed in Chaos, DarkSide, and Emotet malware campaigns.
authors: Vladan Sekulic, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative scripts running from temporary folders.
Niche software updaters utilizing hidden batch files in ProgramData.

rules.title: Potential LSASS Process Dump Via Procdump
rules.description:
Detects potential credential harvesting attempts through LSASS memory dumps using ProcDump.
This rule identifies suspicious command-line patterns that combine memory dump flags (-ma, -mm, -mp) with LSASS-related process markers.
LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) contains sensitive authentication data including plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets in memory.
Attackers commonly dump LSASS memory to extract credentials for lateral movement and privilege escalation.
falsepositives: Unlikely, because no one should dump an lsass process memory
Another tool that uses command line flags similar to ProcDump

rules.title: Suspicious Manipulation Of Default Accounts Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious manipulations of default accounts such as 'administrator' and 'guest'. For example 'enable' or 'disable' accounts or change the password...etc
falsepositives: Some false positives could occur with the admin or guest account. It depends on the scripts being used by the admins in your env. If you experience a lot of FP you could reduce the level to medium

rules.title: File With Suspicious Extension Downloaded Via Bitsadmin
rules.description: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file with a suspicious extension
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Github Self-Hosted Runner Execution
rules.description:
Detects GitHub self-hosted runners executing workflows on local infrastructure that could be abused for persistence and code execution.
Shai-Hulud is an npm supply chain worm targeting CI/CD environments.
It installs runners on compromised systems to maintain access after credential theft, leveraging their access to secrets and internal networks.
falsepositives: Legitimate GitHub self-hosted runner installations on designated CI/CD infrastructure
Authorized runner deployments by DevOps/Platform teams following change management
Scheduled runner updates or reconfigurations on existing build agents
Self-hosted runners that follow expected/known naming patterns
Installation via expected/known configuration management tools (reflected mostly as parent process name)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution Without Parameters
rules.description: Detects rundll32 execution without parameters as observed when running Metasploit windows/smb/psexec exploit module
falsepositives: False positives may occur if a user called rundll32 from CLI with no options

rules.title: Suspicious Processes Spawned by WinRM
rules.description: Detects suspicious processes including shells spawnd from WinRM host process

rules.title: Potential Recon Activity Via Nltest.EXE
rules.description: Detects nltest commands that can be used for information discovery
falsepositives: Legitimate administration use but user and host must be investigated

rules.title: Rundll32 UNC Path Execution
rules.description:
Detects rundll32 execution where the DLL is located on a remote location (share).
Threat actors can abuse the rundll32.exe binary to execute remote DLLs from a UNC pathh.

rules.title: HackTool - Koadic Execution
rules.description: Detects command line parameters used by Koadic hack tool

rules.title: Suspicious Invoke-WebRequest Execution
rules.description: Detects a suspicious call to Invoke-WebRequest cmdlet where the and output is located in a suspicious location

rules.title: Suspicious Parent Double Extension File Execution
rules.description: Detect execution of suspicious double extension files in ParentCommandLine

rules.title: Security Service Disabled Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" to disable security services such as Windows Defender.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), John Lambert (idea), elhoim

rules.title: Indirect Inline Command Execution Via Bash.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of Microsoft bash launcher with the "-c" flag.
This can be used to potentially bypass defenses and execute Linux or Windows-based binaries directly via bash.

rules.title: Response File Execution Via Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with the "-f" flag in order to load a response file which might contain a malicious action.
authors: Kirill Kiryanov, Beyu Denis, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: The rule is looking for any usage of response file, which might generate false positive when this function is used legitimately. Investigate the contents of the ".rsp" file to determine if it is malicious and apply additional filters if necessary.

rules.title: Registry Modification Via Regini.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of regini.exe which can be used to modify registry keys, the changes are imported from one or more text files.

rules.title: Root Certificate Installed From Susp Locations
rules.description: Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Usage Of Qemu
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Qemu utility in a Windows environment.
Threat actors have leveraged this utility and this technique for achieving network access as reported by Kaspersky.

rules.title: Mstsc.EXE Execution With Local RDP File
rules.description: Detects potential RDP connection via Mstsc using a local ".rdp" file
falsepositives: Likely with legitimate usage of ".rdp" files

rules.title: Execute Pcwrun.EXE To Leverage Follina
rules.description: Detects indirect command execution via Program Compatibility Assistant "pcwrun.exe" leveraging the follina (CVE-2022-30190) vulnerability

rules.title: Suspicious SysAidServer Child
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of SysAidServer (as seen in MERCURY threat actor intrusions)

rules.title: New Capture Session Launched Via DXCap.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "DXCap.EXE" with the "-c" flag, which allows a user to launch any arbitrary binary or windows package through DXCap itself. This can be abused to potentially bypass application whitelisting.
authors: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate execution of dxcap.exe by legitimate user

rules.title: Interactive AT Job
rules.description: Detects an interactive AT job, which may be used as a form of privilege escalation.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

rules.title: AddinUtil.EXE Execution From Uncommon Directory
rules.description: Detects execution of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) from a non-standard directory.

rules.title: Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI) Related Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects the tampering of Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI) related registry values via command line tool reg.exe.
HVCI uses virtualization-based security to protect code integrity by ensuring that only trusted code can run in kernel mode.
Adversaries may tamper with HVCI to load malicious or unsigned drivers, which can be used to escalate privileges, maintain persistence, or evade security mechanisms.
falsepositives: Legitimate system administration tasks that require disabling HVCI for troubleshooting purposes when certain drivers or applications are incompatible with it.

rules.title: Share And Session Enumeration Using Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects attempts to enumerate file shares, printer shares and sessions using "net.exe" with the "view" flag.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of net.exe utility by legitimate user

rules.title: Service StartupType Change Via PowerShell Set-Service
rules.description: Detects the use of the PowerShell "Set-Service" cmdlet to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "manual"
falsepositives: False positives may occur with troubleshooting scripts

rules.title: PowerShell Base64 Encoded Reflective Assembly Load
rules.description: Detects base64 encoded .NET reflective loading of Assembly

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Registry File Imported Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the import of '.reg' files from suspicious paths using the 'reg.exe' utility

rules.title: Tor Client/Browser Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Tor or Tor-Browser to connect to onion routing networks

rules.title: Suspicious AddinUtil.EXE CommandLine Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) with suspicious Addinroot or Pipelineroot paths. An adversary may execute AddinUtil.exe with uncommon Addinroot/Pipelineroot paths that point to the adversaries Addins.Store payload.
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Michael McKinley (@McKinleyMike), Tony Latteri (@TheLatteri)

rules.title: ManageEngine Endpoint Central Dctask64.EXE Potential Abuse
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "dctask64.exe", a signed binary by ZOHO Corporation part of ManageEngine Endpoint Central.
This binary can be abused for DLL injection, arbitrary command and process execution.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Malicious Windows Script Components File Execution by TAEF Detection
rules.description:
Windows Test Authoring and Execution Framework (TAEF) framework allows you to run automation by executing tests files written on different languages (C, C#, Microsoft COM Scripting interfaces
Adversaries may execute malicious code (such as WSC file with VBScript, dll and so on) directly by running te.exe
falsepositives: It's not an uncommon to use te.exe directly to execute legal TAEF tests

rules.title: PowerShell Base64 Encoded Invoke Keyword
rules.description: Detects UTF-8 and UTF-16 Base64 encoded powershell 'Invoke-' calls

rules.title: All Backups Deleted Via Wbadmin.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of all backups or system state backups via "wbadmin.exe".
This technique is used by numerous ransomware families and actors.
This may only be successful on server platforms that have Windows Backup enabled.

rules.title: Fsutil Drive Enumeration
rules.description: Attackers may leverage fsutil to enumerated connected drives.
references: Turla has used fsutil fsinfo drives to list connected drives.
falsepositives: Certain software or administrative tasks may trigger false positives.

rules.title: Renamed MegaSync Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed MegaSync.exe as seen used by ransomware families like Nefilim, Sodinokibi, Pysa, and Conti.
falsepositives: Software that illegally integrates MegaSync in a renamed form

rules.title: Execute Files with Msdeploy.exe
rules.description: Detects file execution using the msdeploy.exe lolbin

rules.title: Process Memory Dump Via Comsvcs.DLL
rules.description: Detects a process memory dump via "comsvcs.dll" using rundll32, covering multiple different techniques (ordinal, minidump function, etc.)
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Modexp, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Use of Scriptrunner.exe
rules.description: The "ScriptRunner.exe" binary can be abused to proxy execution through it and bypass possible whitelisting
falsepositives: Legitimate use when App-v is deployed

rules.title: Operator Bloopers Cobalt Strike Commands
rules.description: Detects use of Cobalt Strike commands accidentally entered in the CMD shell

rules.title: RegAsm.EXE Execution Without CommandLine Flags or Files
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "RegAsm.exe" without a commandline flag or file, which might indicate potential process injection activity.
Usually "RegAsm.exe" should point to a dedicated DLL file or call the help with the "/?" flag.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Regasm by developers.

rules.title: Visual Studio NodejsTools PressAnyKey Renamed Execution
rules.description: Detects renamed execution of "Microsoft.NodejsTools.PressAnyKey.exe", which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute arbitrary binaries
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary Code Execution Via Node.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution node.exe which is shipped with multiple software such as VMware, Adobe...etc. In order to execute arbitrary code. For example to establish reverse shell as seen in Log4j attacks...etc

rules.title: Potential Crypto Mining Activity
rules.description: Detects command line parameters or strings often used by crypto miners

rules.title: HackTool - XORDump Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious use of XORDump process memory dumping utility
falsepositives: Another tool that uses the command line switches of XORdump

rules.title: Suspicious JavaScript Execution Via Mshta.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of javascript code using "mshta.exe".
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Execution Via DLL
rules.description:
Detects potential PowerShell execution from a DLL instead of the usual PowerShell process as seen used in PowerShdll.
This detection assumes that PowerShell commands are passed via the CommandLine.

rules.title: Potential Unquoted Service Path Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects known WMI recon method to look for unquoted service paths using wmic. Often used by pentester and attacker enumeration scripts

rules.title: HH.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of "hh.exe" to open ".chm" files.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Dan Beavin), oscd.community
falsepositives: False positives are expected with legitimate ".CHM"

rules.title: PUA - NPS Tunneling Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of NPS, a port forwarding and intranet penetration proxy server

rules.title: Potential WMI Lateral Movement WmiPrvSE Spawned PowerShell
rules.description: Detects Powershell as a child of the WmiPrvSE process. Which could be a sign of lateral movement via WMI.

rules.title: HackTool - Certipy Execution
rules.description: Detects Certipy execution, a tool for Active Directory Certificate Services enumeration and abuse based on PE metadata characteristics and common command line arguments.

rules.title: Veeam Backup Database Suspicious Query
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious SQL queries using SQLCmd targeting the Veeam backup databases in order to steal information.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution From Parent Process In Public Folder
rules.description: Detects a potentially suspicious execution of a parent process located in the "\Users\Public" folder executing a child process containing references to shell or scripting binaries and commandlines.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - TruffleSnout Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of TruffleSnout.exe an iterative AD discovery toolkit for offensive operators, situational awareness and targeted low noise enumeration.

rules.title: Uninstall Sysinternals Sysmon
rules.description: Detects the removal of Sysmon, which could be a potential attempt at defense evasion
falsepositives: Legitimate administrators might use this command to remove Sysmon for debugging purposes

rules.title: Esentutl Steals Browser Information
rules.description: One way Qbot steals sensitive information is by extracting browser data from Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge by using the built-in utility esentutl.exe

rules.title: Suspicious Diantz Alternate Data Stream Execution
rules.description: Compress target file into a cab file stored in the Alternate Data Stream (ADS) of the target file.

rules.title: Odbcconf.EXE Suspicious DLL Location
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" where the path of the DLL being registered is located in a potentially suspicious location.

rules.title: Potential MSTSC Shadowing Activity
rules.description: Detects RDP session hijacking by using MSTSC shadowing

rules.title: Suspicious RASdial Activity
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rasdial.exe
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Potential NTLM Coercion Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects possible NTLM coercion via certutil using the 'syncwithWU' flag

rules.title: Allow Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to allow access to a service from a suspicious trustee. This can be used to override access restrictions set by previous ACLs.

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation STDIN+ Launcher
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated use of stdin to execute PowerShell

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious JWT Token Search Via CLI
rules.description:
Detects potentially suspicious search for JWT tokens via CLI by looking for the string "eyJ0eX" or "eyJhbG".
JWT tokens are often used for access-tokens across various applications and services like Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and others.
Threat actors may search for these tokens to steal them for lateral movement or privilege escalation.

rules.title: Use of W32tm as Timer
rules.description: When configured with suitable command line arguments, w32tm can act as a delay mechanism

rules.title: PUA - Restic Backup Tool Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the Restic backup tool, which can be used for data exfiltration.
Threat actors may leverage Restic to back up and exfiltrate sensitive data to remote storage locations, including cloud services.
If not legitimately used in the enterprise environment, its presence may indicate malicious activity.
authors: Nounou Mbeiri, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Restic for backup purposes within the organization.

rules.title: Suspicious Mstsc.EXE Execution With Local RDP File
rules.description: Detects potential RDP connection via Mstsc using a local ".rdp" file located in suspicious locations.
falsepositives: Likelihood is related to how often the paths are used in the environment

rules.title: Uncommon Link.EXE Parent Process
rules.description:
Detects an uncommon parent process of "LINK.EXE".
Link.EXE in Microsoft incremental linker. Its a utility usually bundled with Visual Studio installation.
Multiple utilities often found in the same folder (editbin.exe, dumpbin.exe, lib.exe, etc) have a hardcode call to the "LINK.EXE" binary without checking its validity.
This would allow an attacker to sideload any binary with the name "link.exe" if one of the aforementioned tools get executed from a different location.
By filtering the known locations of such utilities we can spot uncommon parent process of LINK.EXE that might be suspicious or malicious.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of Regsvr32
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "regsvr32.exe".
authors: elhoim, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Unlikely, but can rarely occur. Apply additional filters accordingly.

rules.title: WSL Kali-Linux Usage
rules.description: Detects the use of Kali Linux through Windows Subsystem for Linux
falsepositives: Legitimate installation or usage of Kali Linux WSL by administrators or security teams

rules.title: Files Added To An Archive Using Rar.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "rar" to add files to an archive for potential compression. An adversary may compress data (e.g. sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.
falsepositives: Highly likely if rar is a default archiver in the monitored environment.

rules.title: Suspicious Msiexec Execute Arbitrary DLL
rules.description:
Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads.
Msiexec.exe is the command-line utility for the Windows Installer and is thus commonly associated with executing installation packages (.msi)

rules.title: Import LDAP Data Interchange Format File Via Ldifde.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "Ldifde.exe" with the import flag "-i". The can be abused to include HTTP-based arguments which will allow the arbitrary download of files from a remote server.
falsepositives: Since the content of the files are unknown, false positives are expected

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec PowerShell Obfuscation
rules.description: The CrachMapExec pentesting framework implements a PowerShell obfuscation with some static strings detected by this rule.

rules.title: File Recovery From Backup Via Wbadmin.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the recovery of files from backups via "wbadmin.exe".
Attackers can restore sensitive files such as NTDS.DIT or Registry Hives from backups in order to potentially extract credentials.

rules.title: Potential Mpclient.DLL Sideloading Via Defender Binaries
rules.description: Detects potential sideloading of "mpclient.dll" by Windows Defender processes ("MpCmdRun" and "NisSrv") from their non-default directory.

rules.title: Cloudflared Tunnel Connections Cleanup
rules.description: Detects execution of the "cloudflared" tool with the tunnel "cleanup" flag in order to cleanup tunnel connections.

rules.title: Console CodePage Lookup Via CHCP
rules.description: Detects use of chcp to look up the system locale value as part of host discovery
falsepositives: During Anaconda update the 'conda.exe' process will eventually execution the 'chcp' command.
Discord was seen using chcp to look up code pages

rules.title: File Download via CertOC.EXE
rules.description: Detects when a user downloads a file by using CertOC.exe

rules.title: Execution Of Non-Existing File
rules.description:
Detects process creation events where the Image field lacks an absolute path,
which occurs when the backing file no longer exists on disk at the time of
logging - commonly caused by Process Ghosting or other unorthodox process creation techniques.

rules.title: Suspicious Kernel Dump Using Dtrace
rules.description: Detects suspicious way to dump the kernel on Windows systems using dtrace.exe, which is available on Windows systems since Windows 10 19H1

rules.title: Suspicious Where Execution
rules.description:
Adversaries may enumerate browser bookmarks to learn more about compromised hosts.
Browser bookmarks may reveal personal information about users (ex: banking sites, interests, social media, etc.) as well as details about
internal network resources such as servers, tools/dashboards, or other related infrastructure.

rules.title: Lolbin Unregmp2.exe Use As Proxy
rules.description: Detect usage of the "unregmp2.exe" binary as a proxy to launch a custom version of "wmpnscfg.exe"

rules.title: MpiExec Lolbin
rules.description: Detects a certain command line flag combination used by mpiexec.exe LOLBIN from HPC pack that can be used to execute any other binary

rules.title: Psexec Execution
rules.description: Detects user accept agreement execution in psexec commandline

rules.title: Suspicious Rundll32 Activity Invoking Sys File
rules.description: Detects suspicious process related to rundll32 based on command line that includes a *.sys file as seen being used by UNC2452

rules.title: Remote PowerShell Session Host Process (WinRM)
rules.description: Detects remote PowerShell sections by monitoring for wsmprovhost (WinRM host process) as a parent or child process (sign of an active PowerShell remote session).
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of remote Powershell, e.g. for monitoring purposes.

rules.title: Suspicious Calculator Usage
rules.description: Detects suspicious use of 'calc.exe' with command line parameters or in a suspicious directory, which is likely caused by some PoC or detection evasion.

rules.title: Imports Registry Key From a File
rules.description: Detects the import of the specified file to the registry with regedit.exe.

rules.title: ConvertTo-SecureString Cmdlet Usage Via CommandLine
rules.description: Detects usage of the "ConvertTo-SecureString" cmdlet via the commandline. Which is fairly uncommon and could indicate potential suspicious activity
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Vasiliy Burov (rule), oscd.community, Tim Shelton
falsepositives: Legitimate use to pass password to different powershell commands

rules.title: Potential Process Injection Via Msra.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential process injection via Microsoft Remote Asssistance (Msra.exe) by looking at suspicious child processes spawned from the aforementioned process. It has been a target used by many threat actors and used for discovery and persistence tactics

rules.title: PUA - Nimgrab Execution
rules.description: Detects the usage of nimgrab, a tool bundled with the Nim programming framework and used for downloading files.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Nim on a developer systems

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - MeshAgent Command Execution via MeshCentral
rules.description:
Detects the use of MeshAgent to execute commands on the target host, particularly when threat actors might abuse it to execute commands directly.
MeshAgent can execute commands on the target host by leveraging win-console to obscure their activities and win-dispatcher to run malicious code through IPC with child processes.
falsepositives: False positives can be found in environments using MeshAgent for remote management, analysis should prioritize the grandparent process, MeshAgent.exe, and scrutinize the resulting child processes triggered by any suspicious interactive commands directed at the target host.

rules.title: Renamed CURL.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "CURL.exe" binary based on the PE metadata fields

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell Parent Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious or uncommon parent processes of PowerShell

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - NetSupport Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Installation Execution
rules.description: Detects ScreenConnect program starts that establish a remote access to a system.

rules.title: Remote XSL Execution Via Msxsl.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of the "msxsl" binary with an "http" keyword in the command line. This might indicate a potential remote execution of XSL files.
falsepositives: Msxsl is not installed by default and is deprecated, so unlikely on most systems.

rules.title: File Download Via InstallUtil.EXE
rules.description: Detects use of .NET InstallUtil.exe in order to download arbitrary files. The files will be written to "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\IE\"

rules.title: Write Protect For Storage Disabled
rules.description:
Detects applications trying to modify the registry in order to disable any write-protect property for storage devices.
This could be a precursor to a ransomware attack and has been an observed technique used by cypherpunk group.

rules.title: Indirect Command Execution via SFTP ProxyCommand
rules.description:
Detects the use of SFTP.exe to execute commands indirectly via ProxyCommand parameter.
Threat actors were seen leveraging this legitimate Windows binary to bypass security controls and execute arbitrary commands while evading detection.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of SFTP with proxy commands for administration or networking tasks

rules.title: HackTool - Certify Execution
rules.description: Detects Certify a tool for Active Directory certificate abuse based on PE metadata characteristics and common command line arguments.

rules.title: HackTool - NetExec Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the hacktool NetExec.
NetExec (formerly CrackMapExec) is a widely used post-exploitation tool designed for Active Directory penetration testing and network enumeration
In enterprise environments, the use of NetExec is considered suspicious or potentially malicious because it enables attackers to enumerate hosts, exploit network services, and move laterally across systems.
Threat actors and red teams commonly use NetExec to identify vulnerable systems, harvest credentials, and execute commands remotely.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of NetExec by security professionals or system administrators for network assessment and management.

rules.title: HackTool - SecurityXploded Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of SecurityXploded Tools

rules.title: Service Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
An adversary might use WMI to check if a certain remote service is running on a remote device.
When the test completes, a service information will be displayed on the screen if it exists.
A common feedback message is that "No instance(s) Available" if the service queried is not running.
A common error message is "Node - (provided IP or default) ERROR Description =The RPC server is unavailable" if the provided remote host is unreachable

rules.title: PUA - NSudo Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of NSudo tool for command execution

rules.title: WMIC Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of WMIC to query information on a remote system

rules.title: Suspicious Registry Modification From ADS Via Regini.EXE
rules.description: Detects the import of an alternate data stream with regini.exe, regini.exe can be used to modify registry keys.

rules.title: Portable Gpg.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of "gpg.exe" from uncommon location. Often used by ransomware and loaders to decrypt/encrypt data.

rules.title: RDP Port Forwarding Rule Added Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of netsh to configure a port forwarding of port 3389 (RDP) rule

rules.title: Password Set to Never Expire via WMI
rules.description: Detects the use of wmic.exe to modify user account settings and explicitly disable password expiration.

rules.title: Suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Child Process
rules.description:
Detects suspicious Speech Runtime Binary Execution by monitoring its child processes.
Child processes spawned by SpeechRuntime.exe could indicate an attempt for lateral movement via COM & DCOM hijacking.

rules.title: WMI Backdoor Exchange Transport Agent
rules.description: Detects a WMI backdoor in Exchange Transport Agents via WMI event filters

rules.title: Msiexec Quiet Installation
rules.description:
Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads.
Msiexec.exe is the command-line utility for the Windows Installer and is thus commonly associated with executing installation packages (.msi)
falsepositives: WindowsApps installing updates via the quiet flag

rules.title: Potential SysInternals ProcDump Evasion
rules.description: Detects uses of the SysInternals ProcDump utility in which ProcDump or its output get renamed, or a dump file is moved or copied to a different name
