falsepositives: False positives are expected in cases in which ProcDump just gets copied to a different directory without any renaming

rules.title: Whoami.EXE Execution From Privileged Process
rules.description: Detects the execution of "whoami.exe" by privileged accounts that are often abused by threat actors

rules.title: Potential Lateral Movement via Windows Remote Shell
rules.description: Detects a child process spawned by 'winrshost.exe', which suggests remote command execution through Windows Remote Shell (WinRs) and may indicate potential lateral movement activity.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of WinRM within the organization

rules.title: HackTool - Empire PowerShell Launch Parameters
rules.description: Detects suspicious powershell command line parameters used in Empire
falsepositives: Other tools that incidentally use the same command line parameters

rules.title: UAC Bypass Abusing Winsat Path Parsing - Process
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using a path parsing issue in winsat.exe (UACMe 52)

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Schedule Type With High Privileges
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations or modification to be run with high privileges on a suspicious schedule type
falsepositives: Some installers were seen using this method of creation unfortunately. Filter them in your environment

rules.title: HackTool - Stracciatella Execution
rules.description: Detects Stracciatella which executes a Powershell runspace from within C# (aka SharpPick technique) with AMSI, ETW and Script Block Logging disabled based on PE metadata characteristics.

rules.title: Suspicious MSDT Parent Process
rules.description: Detects msdt.exe executed by a suspicious parent as seen in CVE-2022-30190 / Follina exploitation

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via VMwareToolBoxCmd.EXE VM State Change Script
rules.description: Detects execution of the "VMwareToolBoxCmd.exe" with the "script" and "set" flag to setup a specific script to run for a specific VM state

rules.title: HackTool - Windows Credential Editor (WCE) Execution
rules.description:
Detects the use of Windows Credential Editor (WCE), a popular post-exploitation tool used to extract plaintext passwords, hash, PIN code and Kerberos tickets from memory.
It is often used by threat actors for credential dumping and lateral movement within compromised networks.

rules.title: Visual Basic Command Line Compiler Usage
rules.description: Detects successful code compilation via Visual Basic Command Line Compiler that utilizes Windows Resource to Object Converter.
falsepositives: Utilization of this tool should not be seen in enterprise environment

rules.title: Renamed Vmnat.exe Execution
rules.description: Detects renamed vmnat.exe or portable version that can be used for DLL side-loading

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Potential Suspicious Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes launched via the ScreenConnect client service.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale
falsepositives: If the script being executed make use of any of the utilities mentioned in the detection then they should filtered out or allowed.

rules.title: Obfuscated PowerShell MSI Install via WindowsInstaller COM
rules.description:
Detects the execution of obfuscated PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`).
The technique involves manipulating strings to hide functionality, such as constructing class names using string insertion (e.g., 'indowsInstaller.Installer'.Insert(0,'W')) and correcting
malformed URLs (e.g., converting 'htps://' to 'https://') at runtime. This behavior is commonly associated with malware loaders or droppers that aim to bypass static detection
by hiding intent in runtime-generated strings and using legitimate tools for code execution. The use of `InstallProduct` and COM object creation, particularly combined with
hidden window execution and suppressed UI, indicates an attempt to install software (likely malicious) without user interaction.

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Hostname
rules.description: Use of hostname to get information

rules.title: System Restore Registry Modification via CommandLine
rules.description: Detects system restore registry modification via command line, which can be used by adversaries to disable system restore on the computer.

rules.title: File And SubFolder Enumeration Via Dir Command
rules.description: Detects usage of the "dir" command part of Windows CMD with the "/S" command line flag in order to enumerate files in a specified directory and all subdirectories.

rules.title: New User Account Creation Attempt Via ADSI in CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects PowerShell command line arguments containing ADSI (Active Directory Service Interfaces) patterns
trying to create a new user account via the WinNT or LDAP provider. This is an uncommon method to create
user accounts and may indicate an attempt to evade detection by avoiding more commonly monitored commands
such as "net user", "New-LocalUser" or "New-ADUser".
authors: William Gokah (idea), Raylee Hawkins, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative scripts that use ADSI to provision user accounts but should be rare in most environments

rules.title: Potential Execution of Sysinternals Tools
rules.description: Detects command lines that contain the 'accepteula' flag which could be a sign of execution of one of the Sysinternals tools
falsepositives: Programs that use the same command line flag

rules.title: Potential Binary Impersonating Sysinternals Tools
rules.description:
Detects binaries that use the same name as legitimate sysinternals tools to evade detection.
This rule looks for the execution of binaries that are named similarly to Sysinternals tools.
Adversary may rename their malicious tools as legitimate Sysinternals tools to evade detection.

rules.title: Potential Data Exfiltration Activity Via CommandLine Tools
rules.description: Detects the use of various CLI utilities exfiltrating data via web requests

rules.title: Uncommon Sigverif.EXE Child Process
rules.description: Detects uncommon child processes spawning from "sigverif.exe", which could indicate potential abuse of the latter as a living of the land binary in order to proxy execution.

rules.title: CMSTP Execution Process Creation
rules.description: Detects various indicators of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer execution
falsepositives: Legitimate CMSTP use (unlikely in modern enterprise environments)

rules.title: Program Executed Using Proxy/Local Command Via SSH.EXE
rules.description: Detect usage of the "ssh.exe" binary as a proxy to launch other programs.

rules.title: Windows AMSI Related Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects tampering of AMSI (Anti-Malware Scan Interface) related registry values via command line tools such as reg.exe or PowerShell.
AMSI provides a generic interface for applications and services to integrate with antimalware products.
Adversaries may disable AMSI to evade detection of malicious scripts and code execution.

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Conhost.EXE
rules.description: Detects uncommon "conhost" child processes. This could be a sign of "conhost" usage as a LOLBIN or potential process injection activity.

rules.title: Esentutl Gather Credentials
rules.description: Conti recommendation to its affiliates to use esentutl to access NTDS dumped file. Trickbot also uses this utilities to get MSEdge info via its module pwgrab.

rules.title: Windows Internet Hosted WebDav Share Mount Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects when an internet hosted webdav share is mounted using the "net.exe" utility

rules.title: PowerShell Web Access Feature Enabled Via DISM
rules.description: Detects the use of DISM to enable the PowerShell Web Access feature, which could be used for remote access and potential abuse
falsepositives: Legitimate PowerShell Web Access installations by administrators

rules.title: HackTool - Rubeus Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the hacktool Rubeus via PE information of command line parameters

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation COMPRESS OBFUSCATION
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via COMPRESS OBFUSCATION

rules.title: AgentExecutor PowerShell Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the AgentExecutor.exe binary. Which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute powershell scripts with the ExecutionPolicy "Bypass" or any binary named "powershell.exe" located in the path provided by 6th positional argument
falsepositives: Legitimate use via Intune management. You exclude script paths and names to reduce FP rate

rules.title: BitLockerTogo.EXE Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "BitLockerToGo.EXE".
BitLocker To Go is BitLocker Drive Encryption on removable data drives. This feature includes the encryption of, USB flash drives, SD cards, External hard disk drives, Other drives that are formatted by using the NTFS, FAT16, FAT32, or exFAT file system.
This is a rarely used application and usage of it at all is worth investigating.
Malware such as Lumma stealer has been seen using this process as a target for process hollowing.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of BitLockerToGo.exe to encrypt portable devices.

rules.title: OpenEDR Spawning Command Shell
rules.description:
Detects the OpenEDR ssh-shellhost.exe spawning a command shell (cmd.exe) or PowerShell with PTY (pseudo-terminal) capabilities.
This may indicate remote command execution through OpenEDR's remote management features, which could be legitimate administrative activity or potential abuse of the remote access tool.
Threat actors may leverage OpenEDR's remote shell capabilities to execute commands on compromised systems, facilitating lateral movement or other command-and-control operations.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of OpenEDR for remote command execution

rules.title: Execute From Alternate Data Streams
rules.description: Detects execution from an Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries may use NTFS file attributes to hide their malicious data in order to evade detection

rules.title: Potential Provlaunch.EXE Binary Proxy Execution Abuse
rules.description: Detects child processes of "provlaunch.exe" which might indicate potential abuse to proxy execution.
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel

rules.title: Bypass UAC via Fodhelper.exe
rules.description: Identifies use of Fodhelper.exe to bypass User Account Control. Adversaries use this technique to execute privileged processes.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Tony Lambert), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate use of fodhelper.exe utility by legitimate user

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using IEInstal - Process
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using IEInstal.exe (UACMe 64)

rules.title: PUA - Process Hacker Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Process Hacker based on binary metadata information (Image, Hash, Imphash, etc).
Process Hacker is a tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level options.
Threat actors abused older vulnerable versions to manipulate system processes.
falsepositives: While sometimes 'Process Hacker is used by legitimate administrators, the execution of Process Hacker must be investigated and allowed on a case by case basis

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Of BgInfo.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of "BgInfo.exe" which could be a sign of potential abuse of the binary to proxy execution via external VBScript

rules.title: Schedule Task Creation From Env Variable Or Potentially Suspicious Path Via Schtasks.EXE
rules.description: Detects Schtask creations that point to a suspicious folder or an environment variable often used by malware
falsepositives: Benign scheduled tasks creations or executions that happen often during software installations
Software that uses the AppData folder and scheduled tasks to update the software in the AppData folders

rules.title: Use of OpenConsole
rules.description: Detects usage of OpenConsole binary as a LOLBIN to launch other binaries to bypass application Whitelisting

rules.title: Suspicious Msiexec Quiet Install From Remote Location
rules.description: Detects usage of Msiexec.exe to install packages hosted remotely quietly

rules.title: Windows Recall Feature Enabled Via Reg.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation.
Windows Recall can be enabled by deleting the existing "DisableAIDataAnalysis" value, or setting it to 0.
Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities.
This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.

rules.title: Add Insecure Download Source To Winget
rules.description:
Detects usage of winget to add a new insecure (http) download source.
Winget will not allow the addition of insecure sources, hence this could indicate potential suspicious activity (or typos)
falsepositives: False positives might occur if the users are unaware of such control checks

rules.title: Stop Windows Service Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the "sc.exe" utility
authors: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behavior in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly

rules.title: Potential Application Whitelisting Bypass via Dnx.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Dnx.EXE. The Dnx utility allows for the execution of C# code.
Attackers might abuse this in order to bypass application whitelisting.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of dnx.exe by legitimate user

rules.title: Suspicious Process By Web Server Process
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious processes being spawned by a web server process which could be the result of a successfully placed web shell or exploitation
authors: Thomas Patzke, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Zach Stanford @svch0st, Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Particular web applications may spawn a shell process legitimately

rules.title: Exports Critical Registry Keys To a File
rules.description: Detects the export of a crital Registry key to a file.
falsepositives: Dumping hives for legitimate purpouse i.e. backup or forensic investigation

rules.title: File In Suspicious Location Encoded To Base64 Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with the "encode" flag to encode a file to base64 where the files are located in potentially suspicious locations

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Setres.EXE
rules.description:
Detects uncommon child process of Setres.EXE.
Setres.EXE is a Windows server only process and tool that can be used to set the screen resolution.
It can potentially be abused in order to launch any arbitrary file with a name containing the word "choice" from the current execution path.

rules.title: MSExchange Transport Agent Installation
rules.description: Detects the Installation of a Exchange Transport Agent
falsepositives: Legitimate installations of exchange TransportAgents. AssemblyPath is a good indicator for this.

rules.title: Audio Capture via SoundRecorder
rules.description: Detect attacker collecting audio via SoundRecorder application.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate audio capture by legitimate user.

rules.title: Suspicious DLL Loaded via CertOC.EXE
rules.description: Detects when a user installs certificates by using CertOC.exe to load the target DLL file.

rules.title: Potential Tampering With Security Products Via WMIC
rules.description: Detects uninstallation or termination of security products using the WMIC utility
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sensitive File Recovery From Backup Via Wbadmin.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the dump of highly sensitive files such as "NTDS.DIT" and "SECURITY" hive.
Attackers can leverage the "wbadmin" utility in order to dump sensitive files that might contain credential or sensitive information.

rules.title: Suspicious CustomShellHost Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of CustomShellHost.exe where the child isn't located in 'C:\Windows\explorer.exe'. CustomShellHost is a known LOLBin that can be abused by attackers for defense evasion techniques.
falsepositives: False positives are unlikely, investigate matches carefully.

rules.title: OneNote.EXE Execution of Malicious Embedded Scripts
rules.description:
Detects the execution of malicious OneNote documents that contain embedded scripts.
When a user clicks on a OneNote attachment and then on the malicious link inside the ".one" file, it exports and executes the malicious embedded script from specific directories.

rules.title: DllUnregisterServer Function Call Via Msiexec.EXE
rules.description: Detects MsiExec loading a DLL and calling its DllUnregisterServer function

rules.title: C# IL Code Compilation Via Ilasm.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of "Ilasm.EXE" in order to compile C# intermediate (IL) code to EXE or DLL.

rules.title: Suspicious Download From File-Sharing Website Via Bitsadmin
rules.description: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file from a suspicious domain
falsepositives: Some legitimate apps use this, but limited.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Inline JavaScript Execution via NodeJS Binary
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious inline JavaScript execution using Node.js with specific keywords in the command line.
falsepositives: Legitimate scripts using Node.js with these modules

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using DismHost
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using DismHost DLL hijacking (UACMe 63)

rules.title: Copy From Or To Admin Share Or Sysvol Folder
rules.description: Detects a copy command or a copy utility execution to or from an Admin share or remote
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Teymur Kheirkhabarov @HeirhabarovT, Zach Stanford @svch0st, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Folder Compress To Potentially Suspicious Output Via Compress-Archive Cmdlet
rules.description:
Detects PowerShell scripts that make use of the "Compress-Archive" Cmdlet in order to compress folders and files where the output is stored in a potentially suspicious location that is used often by malware for exfiltration.
An adversary might compress data (e.g., sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.

rules.title: PowerShell Download and Execution Cradles
rules.description: Detects PowerShell download and execution cradles.
falsepositives: Some PowerShell installers were seen using similar combinations. Apply filters accordingly

rules.title: Service StartupType Change Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detect the use of "sc.exe" to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "demand"
falsepositives: False positives may occur with troubleshooting scripts

rules.title: HackTool - HollowReaper Execution
rules.description:
Detects usage of HollowReaper, a process hollowing shellcode launcher used for stealth payload execution through process hollowing.
It replaces the memory of a legitimate process with custom shellcode, allowing the attacker to execute payloads under the guise of trusted binaries.

rules.title: Devcon Execution Disabling VMware VMCI Device
rules.description:
Detects execution of devcon.exe with commands that disable the VMware Virtual Machine Communication Interface (VMCI) device.
This can be legitimate during VMware Tools troubleshooting or driver conflicts, but may also indicate malware attempting to hijack communication with the hardware via the VMCI device.
This has been used to facilitate VMware ESXi vulnerability exploits to escape VMs and execute code on the ESXi host.
authors: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)
falsepositives: Legitimate VMware administration, Tools installation/uninstallation, or troubleshooting driver conflicts.
Automated scripts in virtualized environments for device cleanup.

rules.title: New Service Creation Using Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new service using the "sc.exe" utility.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user creates a service for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via IMEWDBLD.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "IMEWDBLD.exe" to download arbitrary files

rules.title: Scheduled Task Executing Payload from Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtasks that potentially executes a payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Regsvr32 HTTP/FTP Pattern
rules.description: Detects regsvr32 execution to download/install/register new DLLs that are hosted on Web or FTP servers.

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Of SQL Server
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of the SQLServer process. This could indicate potential RCE or SQL Injection.

rules.title: Suspicious UltraVNC Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious UltraVNC command line flag combination that indicate a auto reconnect upon execution, e.g. startup (as seen being used by Gamaredon threat group)

rules.title: Sysmon Configuration Update
rules.description: Detects updates to Sysmon's configuration. Attackers might update or replace the Sysmon configuration with a bare bone one to avoid monitoring without shutting down the service completely
falsepositives: Legitimate administrators might use this command to update Sysmon configuration.

rules.title: Enumeration for 3rd Party Creds From CLI
rules.description: Detects processes that query known 3rd party registry keys that holds credentials via commandline

rules.title: Change PowerShell Policies to an Insecure Level
rules.description: Detects changing the PowerShell script execution policy to a potentially insecure level using the "-ExecutionPolicy" flag.

rules.title: Suspicious ShellExec_RunDLL Call Via Ordinal
rules.description:
Detects suspicious call to the "ShellExec_RunDLL" exported function of SHELL32.DLL through the ordinal number to launch other commands.
Adversary might only use the ordinal number in order to bypass existing detection that alert on usage of ShellExec_RunDLL on CommandLine.

rules.title: PsExec/PAExec Escalation to LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects suspicious commandline flags used by PsExec and PAExec to escalate a command line to LOCAL_SYSTEM rights
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Admins that use PsExec or PAExec to escalate to the SYSTEM account for maintenance purposes (rare)
Users that debug Microsoft Intune issues using the commands mentioned in the official documentation; see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/apps/intune-management-extension

rules.title: Regedit as Trusted Installer
rules.description: Detects a regedit started with TrustedInstaller privileges or by ProcessHacker.exe

rules.title: Suspicious Service Binary Directory
rules.description: Detects a service binary running in a suspicious directory

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - UltraViewer Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Stop Windows Service Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the "net" utility.
authors: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behaviour in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly

rules.title: Suspicious Regsvr32 Execution From Remote Share
rules.description: Detects REGSVR32.exe to execute DLL hosted on remote shares

rules.title: Chromium Browser Instance Executed With Custom Extension
rules.description: Detects a Chromium based browser process with the 'load-extension' flag to start a instance with a custom extension
falsepositives: Usage of Chrome Extensions in testing tools such as BurpSuite will trigger this alert

rules.title: PowerShell Base64 Encoded IEX Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects usage of a base64 encoded "IEX" cmdlet in a process command line

rules.title: Python Inline Command Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of python using the "-c" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live python code.
falsepositives: Python libraries that use a flag starting with "-c". Filter according to your environment

rules.title: UAC Bypass WSReset
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass via WSReset usable by default sysmon-config

rules.title: Schtasks Creation Or Modification With SYSTEM Privileges
rules.description: Detects the creation or update of a scheduled task to run with "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM" privileges

rules.title: Windows Backup Deleted Via Wbadmin.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the deletion of backups or system state backups via "wbadmin.exe".
This technique is used by numerous ransomware families and actors.
This may only be successful on server platforms that have Windows Backup enabled.
falsepositives: Legitimate backup activity from administration scripts and software.

rules.title: PUA - Memory Dump Mount Via MemProcFS
rules.description:
Detects execution of MemProcFS a memory forensics tool with the '-device' parameter.
MemProcFS mounts physical memory as a virtual file system, allowing direct access to process memory and system structures.
Threat actors were seen abusing this utility to mount memory dumps and then extract sensitive information from processes like LSASS or extract registry hives to obtain credentials, LSA secrets, SAM data, and cached domain credentials.
MemProcFS usage that is not part of authorized forensic analysis should be treated as suspicious and warrants further investigation.
falsepositives: Legitimate use during memory forensics; if not part of authorized analysis, warrants urgent investigation

rules.title: Potential Remote Desktop Tunneling
rules.description: Detects potential use of an SSH utility to establish RDP over a reverse SSH Tunnel. This can be used by attackers to enable routing of network packets that would otherwise not reach their intended destination.

rules.title: Renamed BrowserCore.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects process creation with a renamed BrowserCore.exe (used to extract Azure tokens)

rules.title: Suspicious WmiPrvSE Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious and uncommon child processes of WmiPrvSE
authors: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - SysmonEOP Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the PoC that can be used to exploit Sysmon CVE-2022-41120

rules.title: Schtasks From Suspicious Folders
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creations that have suspicious action command and folder combinations

rules.title: PUA - Chisel Tunneling Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of the Chisel tunneling tool via the commandline arguments
falsepositives: Some false positives may occur with other tools with similar commandlines

rules.title: Sensitive File Dump Via Wbadmin.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the dump of highly sensitive files such as "NTDS.DIT" and "SECURITY" hive.
Attackers can leverage the "wbadmin" utility in order to dump sensitive files that might contain credential or sensitive information.
falsepositives: Legitimate backup operation by authorized administrators. Matches must be investigated and allowed on a case by case basis.

rules.title: Suspicious Process Patterns NTDS.DIT Exfil
rules.description: Detects suspicious process patterns used in NTDS.DIT exfiltration

rules.title: LSA PPL Protection Setting Modification via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects modification of LSA PPL protection settings via CommandLine.
It may indicate an attempt to disable protection and enable credential dumping tools to access LSASS process memory.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Using Reg.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "reg.exe" to alter registry keys that would replace the user's desktop background.
This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
falsepositives: Administrative scripts that change the desktop background to a company logo or other image.

rules.title: Potential Remote SquiblyTwo Technique Execution
rules.description:
Detects potential execution of the SquiblyTwo technique that leverages Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)
to execute malicious code remotely. This technique bypasses application whitelisting by using wmic.exe to process
malicious XSL (eXtensible Stylesheet Language) scripts that can contain embedded JScript or VBScript.
The attack typically works by fetching XSL content from a remote source (using HTTP/HTTPS) and executing it
with full trust privileges directly in memory, avoiding disk-based detection mechanisms. This is a common
LOLBin (Living Off The Land Binary) technique used for defense evasion and code execution.
authors: Markus Neis, Florian Roth, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Whoami.EXE Execution Anomaly
rules.description: Detects the execution of whoami.exe with suspicious parent processes.
falsepositives: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious CMD Shell Output Redirect
rules.description:
Detects inline Windows shell commands redirecting output via the ">" symbol to a suspicious location.
This technique is sometimes used by malicious actors in order to redirect the output of reconnaissance commands such as "hostname" and "dir" to files for future exfiltration.
falsepositives: Legitimate admin or third party scripts used for diagnostic collection might generate some false positives

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Spawned By Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects an uncommon child process of "odbcconf.exe" binary which normally shouldn't have any child processes.
falsepositives: In rare occurrences where "odbcconf" crashes. It might spawn a "werfault" process

Other child processes will depend on the DLL being registered by actions like "regsvr". In case where the DLLs have external calls (which should be rare). Other child processes might spawn and additional filters need to be applied.

rules.title: Suspicious ArcSOC.exe Child Process
rules.description:
Detects script interpreters, command-line tools, and similar suspicious child processes of ArcSOC.exe.
ArcSOC.exe is the process name which hosts ArcGIS Server REST services. If an attacker compromises an ArcGIS
Server system and uploads a malicious Server Object Extension (SOE), they can send crafted requests to the corresponding
service endpoint and remotely execute code from the ArcSOC.exe process.

rules.title: Non-privileged Usage of Reg or Powershell
rules.description: Search for usage of reg or Powershell by non-privileged users to modify service configuration in registry

rules.title: User Shell Folders Registry Modification via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects modifications to User Shell Folders registry values via reg.exe or PowerShell, which could indicate persistence attempts.
Attackers may modify User Shell Folders registry values to point to malicious executables or scripts that will be executed during startup.
This technique is often used to maintain persistence on a compromised system by ensuring that malicious payloads are executed automatically.
falsepositives: Usage of reg.exe or PowerShell to modify User Shell Folders for legitimate purposes; but rare.

rules.title: Java Running with Remote Debugging
rules.description: Detects a JAVA process running with remote debugging allowing more than just localhost to connect

rules.title: Nltest.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects nltest commands that can be used for information discovery

rules.title: Arbitrary MSI Download Via Devinit.EXE
rules.description: Detects a certain command line flag combination used by "devinit.exe", which can be abused as a LOLBIN to download arbitrary MSI packages on a Windows system

rules.title: Visual Studio Code Tunnel Execution
rules.description: Detects Visual Studio Code tunnel execution. Attackers can abuse this functionality to establish a C2 channel
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Visual Studio Code tunnel

rules.title: Suspicious ZipExec Execution
rules.description: ZipExec is a Proof-of-Concept (POC) tool to wrap binary-based tools into a password-protected zip file.

rules.title: NTLM Hash Leak Via Curl NTLM Authentication
rules.description:
Detects the use of curl with NTLM authentication and empty credentials (-u :), which can be abused to leak the currently logged-in user's NTLMv2 challenge-response to an
attacker-controlled server, enabling offline cracking or relay attacks.
When no credentials are provided, the Microsoft-shipped curl passes a NULL identity to Windows SSPI, which automatically falls back to the current user's logon session credentials
stored in LSASS — without requiring a plaintext password.
This behavior is exclusive to the curl binary shipped by Microsoft (available since Windows 10 / Windows Server 2019), which is built with SSPI support.
falsepositives: Should be very rare as it's not widely known or used, but could occur in legitimate use cases where curl is used with NTLM authentication and empty credentials, such as in certain scripts or automation tasks.

rules.title: Findstr GPP Passwords
rules.description: Look for the encrypted cpassword value within Group Policy Preference files on the Domain Controller. This value can be decrypted with gpp-decrypt.

rules.title: Active Directory Database Snapshot Via ADExplorer
rules.description: Detects the execution of Sysinternals ADExplorer with the "-snapshot" flag in order to save a local copy of the active directory database. This can be used by attackers to extract data for Bloodhound, usernames for password spraying or use the meta data for social engineering. The snapshot doesn't contain password hashes but there have been cases, where administrators put passwords in the comment field.

rules.title: Registry Modification Attempt Via VBScript
rules.description:
Detects attempts to modify the registry using VBScript's CreateObject("Wscript.shell") and RegWrite methods via common LOLBINs.
It could be an attempt to modify the registry for persistence without using straightforward methods like regedit.exe, reg.exe, or PowerShell.
Threat Actors may use this technique to evade detection by security solutions that monitor for direct registry modifications through traditional tools.

rules.title: Potential Rundll32 Execution With DLL Stored In ADS
rules.description: Detects execution of rundll32 where the DLL being called is stored in an Alternate Data Stream (ADS).

rules.title: Binary Proxy Execution Via Dotnet-Trace.EXE
rules.description: Detects commandline arguments for executing a child process via dotnet-trace.exe
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the utility in order to debug and trace a program.

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks.EXE
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks by user accounts via the "schtasks" utility.

rules.title: Replace.exe Usage
rules.description: Detects the use of Replace.exe which can be used to replace file with another file

rules.title: Potential AMSI Bypass Using NULL Bits
rules.description: Detects usage of special strings/null bits in order to potentially bypass AMSI functionalities

rules.title: PUA - RunXCmd Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of the RunXCmd tool to execute commands with System or TrustedInstaller accounts

rules.title: Audio Capture via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects audio capture via PowerShell Cmdlet.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate audio capture by legitimate user.

rules.title: Capture Credentials with Rpcping.exe
rules.description: Detects using Rpcping.exe to send a RPC test connection to the target server (-s) and force the NTLM hash to be sent in the process.

rules.title: Code Execution via Pcwutl.dll
rules.description: Detects launch of executable by calling the LaunchApplication function from pcwutl.dll library.
falsepositives: Use of Program Compatibility Troubleshooter Helper

rules.title: IIS Native-Code Module Command Line Installation
rules.description: Detects suspicious IIS native-code module installations via command line
falsepositives: Unknown as it may vary from organisation to organisation how admins use to install IIS modules

rules.title: File Download From Browser Process Via Inline URL
rules.description: Detects execution of a browser process with a URL argument pointing to a file with a potentially interesting extension. This can be abused to download arbitrary files or to hide from the user for example by launching the browser in a minimized state.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Explorer Process Tree Break
rules.description:
Detects a command line process that uses explorer.exe to launch arbitrary commands or binaries,
which is similar to cmd.exe /c, only it breaks the process tree and makes its parent a new instance of explorer spawning from "svchost"
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), @gott_cyber

rules.title: HackTool - RedMimicry Winnti Playbook Execution
rules.description: Detects actions caused by the RedMimicry Winnti playbook a automated breach emulations utility

rules.title: Regsvr32 Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects execution of regsvr32 where the DLL is located in a potentially suspicious location.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Some installers might execute "regsvr32" with DLLs located in %TEMP% or in %PROGRAMDATA%. Apply additional filters if necessary.

rules.title: New Remote Desktop Connection Initiated Via Mstsc.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the usage of "mstsc.exe" with the "/v" flag to initiate a connection to a remote server.
Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a computer using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Simple Help Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell Invocation From Script Engines
rules.description: Detects suspicious powershell invocations from interpreters or unusual programs

rules.title: Windows Processes Suspicious Parent Directory
rules.description: Detect suspicious parent processes of well-known Windows processes
falsepositives: Some security products seem to spawn these

rules.title: Execution via stordiag.exe
rules.description: Detects the use of stordiag.exe to execute schtasks.exe systeminfo.exe and fltmc.exe

rules.title: Suspicious File Characteristics Due to Missing Fields
rules.description: Detects Executables in the Downloads folder without FileVersion,Description,Product,Company likely created with py2exe

rules.title: Potential Configuration And Service Reconnaissance Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" in order to query reconnaissance information from the registry. Adversaries may interact with the Windows registry to gather information about credentials, the system, configuration, and installed software.

rules.title: Uncommon One Time Only Scheduled Task At 00:00
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creation events that include suspicious actions, and is run once at 00:00

rules.title: Windows Defender Definition Files Removed
rules.description: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid possible detection of their tools and activities by removing Windows Defender Definition Files

rules.title: Security Privileges Enumeration Via Whoami.EXE
rules.description: Detects a whoami.exe executed with the /priv command line flag instructing the tool to show all current user privileges. This is often used after a privilege escalation attempt.

rules.title: Microsoft IIS Connection Strings Decryption
rules.description: Detects use of aspnet_regiis to decrypt Microsoft IIS connection strings. An attacker with Microsoft IIS web server access via a webshell or alike can decrypt and dump any hardcoded connection strings, such as the MSSQL service account password using aspnet_regiis command.

rules.title: File Download And Execution Via IEExec.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of the IEExec utility to download and execute files

rules.title: Suspicious WebDav Client Execution Via Rundll32.EXE
rules.description: Detects "svchost.exe" spawning "rundll32.exe" with command arguments like C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie. This could be an indicator of exfiltration or use of WebDav to launch code (hosted on WebDav Server) or potentially a sign of exploitation of CVE-2023-23397
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious TSCON Start as SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects a tscon.exe start as LOCAL SYSTEM

rules.title: Gzip Archive Decode Via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects attempts of decoding encoded Gzip archives via PowerShell.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative scripts may use this functionality. Use "ParentImage" in combination with the script names and allowed users and applications to filter legitimate executions

rules.title: DNS Exfiltration and Tunneling Tools Execution
rules.description: Well-known DNS Exfiltration tools execution

rules.title: HackTool - winPEAS Execution
rules.description: WinPEAS is a script that search for possible paths to escalate privileges on Windows hosts. The checks are explained on book.hacktricks.xyz

rules.title: Service Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detection of sc.exe utility adding a new service with special permission which hides that service.

rules.title: Enable LM Hash Storage - ProcCreation
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes.
By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.

rules.title: Tap Installer Execution
rules.description: Well-known TAP software installation. Possible preparation for data exfiltration using tunneling techniques

rules.title: Cscript/Wscript Uncommon Script Extension Execution
rules.description: Detects Wscript/Cscript executing a file with an uncommon (i.e. non-script) extension

rules.title: Suspicious Download From Direct IP Via Bitsadmin
rules.description: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file using an URL that contains an IP

rules.title: Setup16.EXE Execution With Custom .Lst File
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "Setup16.EXE" and old installation utility with a custom ".lst" file.
These ".lst" file can contain references to external program that "Setup16.EXE" will execute.
Attackers and adversaries might leverage this as a living of the land utility.
falsepositives: On modern Windows system, the "Setup16" utility is practically never used, hence false positive should be very rare.

rules.title: Deny Service Access Using Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications to deny access to a service that affects critical trustees. This can be used to hide services or make them unstoppable.

rules.title: Cloudflared Tunnel Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the "cloudflared" tool to connect back to a tunnel. This was seen used by threat actors to maintain persistence and remote access to compromised networks.

rules.title: PUA - AdFind Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects AdFind execution with common flags seen used during attacks
authors: Janantha Marasinghe (https://github.com/blueteam0ps), FPT.EagleEye Team, omkar72, oscd.community

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Via WER
rules.description: Detects potential credential dumping via Windows Error Reporting LSASS Shtinkering technique which uses the Windows Error Reporting to dump lsass
falsepositives: Windows Error Reporting might produce similar behavior. In that case, check the PID associated with the "-p" parameter in the CommandLine.

rules.title: Forfiles Command Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "forfiles" with the "/c" flag.
While this is an expected behavior of the tool, it can be abused in order to proxy execution through it with any binary.
Can be used to bypass application whitelisting.
authors: Tim Rauch, Elastic, E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate use via a batch script or by an administrator.

rules.title: Disable Important Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by disabling their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities

rules.title: Changing Existing Service ImagePath Value Via Reg.EXE
rules.description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the Registry entries used by services.
Adversaries may use flaws in the permissions for registry to redirect from the originally specified executable to one that they control, in order to launch their own code at Service start.
Windows stores local service configuration information in the Registry under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services

rules.title: Privilege Escalation via Named Pipe Impersonation
rules.description: Detects a remote file copy attempt to a hidden network share. This may indicate lateral movement or data staging activity.
falsepositives: Other programs that cause these patterns (please report)

rules.title: Suspicious Encoded And Obfuscated Reflection Assembly Load Function Call
rules.description: Detects suspicious base64 encoded and obfuscated "LOAD" keyword used in .NET "reflection.assembly"

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Stdin
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via Stdin in Scripts

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Appvlp.EXE
rules.description:
Detects uncommon child processes of Appvlp.EXE
Appvlp or the Application Virtualization Utility is included with Microsoft Office. Attackers are able to abuse "AppVLP" to execute shell commands.
Normally, this binary is used for Application Virtualization, but it can also be abused to circumvent the ASR file path rule folder
or to mark a file as a system file.

rules.title: MSDT Execution Via Answer File
rules.description: Detects execution of "msdt.exe" using an answer file which is simulating the legitimate way of calling msdt via "pcwrun.exe" (For example from the compatibility tab).
falsepositives: Possible undocumented parents of "msdt" other than "pcwrun".

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process of AspNetCompiler
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "aspnet_compiler.exe".

rules.title: Wlrmdr.EXE Uncommon Argument Or Child Process
rules.description:
Detects the execution of "Wlrmdr.exe" with the "-u" command line flag which allows anything passed to it to be an argument of the ShellExecute API, which would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary binaries.
This detection also focuses on any uncommon child processes spawned from "Wlrmdr.exe" as a supplement for those that posses "ParentImage" telemetry.

rules.title: MMC Executing Files with Reversed Extensions Using RTLO Abuse
rules.description: Detects malicious behavior where the MMC utility (`mmc.exe`) executes files with reversed extensions caused by Right-to-Left Override (RLO) abuse, disguising them as document formats.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative actions using MMC to execute misnamed `.msc` files.
Unconventional but non-malicious usage of RLO or reversed extensions.

rules.title: Uncommon System Information Discovery Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the use of the WMI command-line (WMIC) utility to identify and display various system information,
including OS, CPU, GPU, and disk drive names; memory capacity; display resolution; and baseboard, BIOS,
and GPU driver products/versions.
Some of these commands were used by Aurora Stealer in late 2022/early 2023.

rules.title: Computer System Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of wmic utility with the "computersystem" flag in order to obtain information about the machine such as the domain, username, model, etc.

rules.title: Remote Code Execute via Winrm.vbs
rules.description: Detects an attempt to execute code or create service on remote host via winrm.vbs.

rules.title: Msxsl.EXE Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the MSXSL utility. This can be used to execute Extensible Stylesheet Language (XSL) files. These files are commonly used to describe the processing and rendering of data within XML files.
Adversaries can abuse this functionality to execute arbitrary files while potentially bypassing application whitelisting defenses.
falsepositives: Msxsl is not installed by default and is deprecated, so unlikely on most systems.

rules.title: Certificate Exported Via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects calls to cmdlets that are used to export certificates from the local certificate store. Threat actors were seen abusing this to steal private keys from compromised machines.
falsepositives: Legitimate certificate exports by administrators. Additional filters might be required.

rules.title: Hiding User Account Via SpecialAccounts Registry Key - CommandLine
rules.description: Detects changes to the registry key "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\Userlist" where the value is set to "0" in order to hide user account from being listed on the logon screen.

rules.title: New DLL Registered Via Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with "REGSVR" in order to register a new DLL (equivalent to running regsvr32). Attackers abuse this to install and run malicious DLLs.
authors: Kirill Kiryanov, Beyu Denis, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate DLLs being registered via "odbcconf" will generate false positives. Investigate the path of the DLL and its content to determine if the action is authorized.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Cabinet File Expansion
rules.description: Detects the expansion or decompression of cabinet files from potentially suspicious or uncommon locations, e.g. seen in Iranian MeteorExpress related attacks

rules.title: Suspicious BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the BitLocker Access Agent Update Utility (baaupdate.exe) which is not a common parent process for other processes.
Suspicious child processes spawned by baaupdate.exe could indicate an attempt at lateral movement via BitLocker DCOM & COM Hijacking.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious ASP.NET Compilation Via AspNetCompiler
rules.description: Detects execution of "aspnet_compiler.exe" with potentially suspicious paths for compilation.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of DiskShadow.EXE
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "Diskshadow.exe". This could be an attempt to bypass parent/child relationship detection or application whitelisting rules.
falsepositives: False postitve can occur in cases where admin scripts levreage the "exec" flag to execute applications

rules.title: Scheduled Task Creation Masquerading as System Processes
rules.description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks that involve system processes, which may indicate malicious actors masquerading as or abusing these processes to execute payloads or maintain persistence.
falsepositives: Legitimate system administration tasks scheduling trusted system processes.

rules.title: Compress Data and Lock With Password for Exfiltration With 7-ZIP
rules.description: An adversary may compress or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration using 3rd party utilities
falsepositives: Legitimate activity is expected since compressing files with a password is common.

rules.title: Usage Of Web Request Commands And Cmdlets
rules.description: Detects the use of various web request commands with commandline tools and Windows PowerShell cmdlets (including aliases) via CommandLine
authors: James Pemberton / @4A616D6573, Endgame, JHasenbusch, oscd.community, Austin Songer @austinsonger
falsepositives: Use of Get-Command and Get-Help modules to reference Invoke-WebRequest and Start-BitsTransfer.

rules.title: Taskmgr as LOCAL_SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects the creation of taskmgr.exe process in context of LOCAL_SYSTEM

rules.title: Suspicious Execution From Outlook Temporary Folder
rules.description: Detects a suspicious program execution in Outlook temp folder

rules.title: AspNetCompiler Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of "aspnet_compiler.exe" which can be abused to compile and execute C# code.

rules.title: Potential Process Execution Proxy Via CL_Invocation.ps1
rules.description: Detects calls to "SyncInvoke" that is part of the "CL_Invocation.ps1" script to proxy execution using "System.Diagnostics.Process"
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova

rules.title: Registry Enumeration via WMI Stdregprov
rules.description:
Detects the usage of wmic.exe to enumerate or read Windows registry via the WMI StdRegProv class read methods (EnumKey, EnumValues, GetStringValue, etc.).
While registry reads are common, attackers may use this technique to perform reconnaissance and discover sensitive configuration values, credentials, or installed software.
The use of WMI as an alternative to standard tools like reg.exe can indicate an attempt to evade detection focused on traditional registry query commands.

rules.title: Cmd.EXE Missing Space Characters Execution Anomaly
rules.description:
Detects Windows command lines that miss a space before or after the /c flag when running a command using the cmd.exe.
This could be a sign of obfuscation of a fat finger problem (typo by the developer).
falsepositives: Legitimate use of cmd.exe with no arguments e.g. via system("") in C to enable ANSI escape codes

rules.title: HackTool - WinRM Access Via Evil-WinRM
rules.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a computer using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user.

rules.title: Disabling Windows Defender WMI Autologger Session via Reg.exe
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe to disable the Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) Autologger session for Windows Defender API and Audit events.
By setting the 'Start' value to '0' for the 'DefenderApiLogger' or 'DefenderAuditLogger' session, an attacker can prevent these critical security events
from being logged, effectively blinding monitoring tools that rely on this data. This is a powerful defense evasion technique.

rules.title: Visual Studio NodejsTools PressAnyKey Arbitrary Binary Execution
rules.description: Detects child processes of Microsoft.NodejsTools.PressAnyKey.exe that can be used to execute any other binary
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use by developers as part of NodeJS development with Visual Studio Tools

rules.title: ETW Trace Evasion Activity
rules.description: Detects command line activity that tries to clear or disable any ETW trace log which could be a sign of logging evasion.
authors: @neu5ron, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: DLL Execution Via Register-cimprovider.exe
rules.description: Detects using register-cimprovider.exe to execute arbitrary dll file.

rules.title: HackTool - Pypykatz Credentials Dumping Activity
rules.description: Detects the usage of "pypykatz" to obtain stored credentials. Adversaries may attempt to extract credential material from the Security Account Manager (SAM) database through Windows registry where the SAM database is stored

rules.title: Suspicious Network Command
rules.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems

rules.title: Suspicious Driver Install by pnputil.exe
rules.description: Detects when a possible suspicious driver is being installed via pnputil.exe lolbin
authors: Hai Vaknin @LuxNoBulIshit, Avihay eldad  @aloneliassaf, Austin Songer @austinsonger
falsepositives: Pnputil.exe being used may be performed by a system administrator.
Verify whether the user identity, user agent, and/or hostname should be making changes in your environment.
Pnputil.exe being executed from unfamiliar users should be investigated. If known behavior is causing false positives, it can be exempted from the rule.

rules.title: Raccine Uninstall
rules.description: Detects commands that indicate a Raccine removal from an end system. Raccine is a free ransomware protection tool.

rules.title: HackTool - PowerTool Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the tool PowerTool which has the ability to kill a process, delete its process file, unload drivers, and delete the driver files

rules.title: Suspicious Program Location Whitelisted In Firewall Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects Netsh command execution that whitelists a program located in a suspicious location in the Windows Firewall
authors: Sander Wiebing, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Key Manager Access
rules.description: Detects the invocation of the Stored User Names and Passwords dialogue (Key Manager)

rules.title: Potential File Overwrite Via Sysinternals SDelete
rules.description: Detects the use of SDelete to erase a file not the free space

rules.title: Unusual Child Process of dns.exe
rules.description: Detects an unexpected process spawning from dns.exe which may indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)

rules.title: Service DACL Abuse To Hide Services Via Sc.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of the "sc.exe" utility adding a new service with special permission seen used by threat actors which makes the service hidden and unremovable.

rules.title: Suspicious Usage Of Active Directory Diagnostic Tool (ntdsutil.exe)
rules.description: Detects execution of ntdsutil.exe to perform different actions such as restoring snapshots...etc.

rules.title: HackTool - Mimikatz Execution
rules.description: Detection well-known mimikatz command line arguments
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, oscd.community, David ANDRE (additional keywords), Tim Shelton

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Powershell Script Execution From Temp Folder
rules.description: Detects a potentially suspicious powershell script executions from temporary folder
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton

rules.title: RemoteFXvGPUDisablement Abuse Via AtomicTestHarnesses
rules.description: Detects calls to the AtomicTestHarnesses "Invoke-ATHRemoteFXvGPUDisablementCommand" which is designed to abuse the "RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.exe" binary to run custom PowerShell code via module load-order hijacking.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using PkgMgr and DISM
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using pkgmgr.exe and dism.exe (UACMe 23)

rules.title: SQL Client Tools PowerShell Session Detection
rules.description:
This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqltoolsps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the Microsoft SQL Server Management studio.
Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on the analysis of these logs.
falsepositives: Direct PS command execution through SQLToolsPS.exe is uncommon, childprocess sqltoolsps.exe spawned by smss.exe is a legitimate action.

rules.title: HackTool - RemoteKrbRelay Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of RemoteKrbRelay, a Kerberos relaying tool via CommandLine flags and PE metadata.

rules.title: Potential Dosfuscation Activity
rules.description: Detects possible payload obfuscation via the commandline

rules.title: Bad Opsec Defaults Sacrificial Processes With Improper Arguments
rules.description:
Detects attackers using tooling with bad opsec defaults.
E.g. spawning a sacrificial process to inject a capability into the process without taking into account how the process is normally run.
One trivial example of this is using rundll32.exe without arguments as a sacrificial process (default in CS, now highlighted by c2lint), running WerFault without arguments (Kraken - credit am0nsec), and other examples.
authors: Oleg Kolesnikov @securonix invrep_de, oscd.community, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Disable Windows Defender AV Security Monitoring
rules.description: Detects attackers attempting to disable Windows Defender using Powershell
falsepositives: Minimal, for some older versions of dev tools, such as pycharm, developers were known to sometimes disable Windows Defender to improve performance, but this generally is not considered a good security practice.

rules.title: Use Of The SFTP.EXE Binary As A LOLBIN
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "sftp.exe" binary as a LOLBIN by abusing the "-D" flag

rules.title: Suspicious Service DACL Modification Via Set-Service Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects suspicious DACL modifications via the "Set-Service" cmdlet using the "SecurityDescriptorSddl" flag (Only available with PowerShell 7) that can be used to hide services or make them unstopable

rules.title: Use Short Name Path in Image
rules.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid Image detection
falsepositives: Applications could use this notation occasionally which might generate some false positives. In that case Investigate the parent and child process.

rules.title: Suspicious Use of CSharp Interactive Console
rules.description: Detects the execution of CSharp interactive console by PowerShell
falsepositives: Possible depending on environment. Pair with other factors such as net connections, command-line args, etc.

rules.title: Potential Download/Upload Activity Using Type Command
rules.description: Detects usage of the "type" command to download/upload data from WebDAV server

rules.title: Recon Information for Export with Command Prompt
rules.description: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.

rules.title: Suspicious Binary In User Directory Spawned From Office Application
rules.description: Detects an executable in the users directory started from one of the Microsoft Office suite applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Publisher, Visio)

rules.title: Suspicious Extrac32 Execution
rules.description: Download or Copy file with Extrac32

rules.title: HackTool - Hydra Password Bruteforce Execution
rules.description: Detects command line parameters used by Hydra password guessing hack tool
falsepositives: Software that uses the caret encased keywords PASS and USER in its command line

rules.title: Suspicious Use of PsLogList
rules.description: Detects usage of the PsLogList utility to dump event log in order to extract admin accounts and perform account discovery or delete events logs
falsepositives: Another tool that uses the command line switches of PsLogList
Legitimate use of PsLogList by an administrator

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of BgInfo.EXE
rules.description: Detects uncommon child processes of "BgInfo.exe" which could be a sign of potential abuse of the binary to proxy execution via external VBScript
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Beyu Denis, oscd.community

rules.title: Scripting/CommandLine Process Spawned Regsvr32
rules.description: Detects various command line and scripting engines/processes such as "PowerShell", "Wscript", "Cmd", etc. spawning a "regsvr32" instance.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate ".bat", ".hta", ".ps1" or ".vbs" scripts leverage legitimately often. Apply additional filter and exclusions as necessary

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Team Viewer Session Started On Windows Host
rules.description:
Detects the command line executed when TeamViewer starts a session started by a remote host.
Once a connection has been started, an investigator can verify the connection details by viewing the "incoming_connections.txt" log file in the TeamViewer folder.

rules.title: Suspicious Redirection to Local Admin Share
rules.description: Detects a suspicious output redirection to the local admins share, this technique is often found in malicious scripts or hacktool stagers

rules.title: PowerShell Script Run in AppData
rules.description: Detects a suspicious command line execution that invokes PowerShell with reference to an AppData folder
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Potential Binary Proxy Execution Via VSDiagnostics.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "VSDiagnostics.exe" with the "start" command in order to launch and proxy arbitrary binaries.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage for tracing and diagnostics purposes

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Use MSHTA
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via use MSHTA in Scripts

rules.title: Potential Defense Evasion Via Right-to-Left Override
rules.description:
Detects the presence of the "u202+E" character, which causes a terminal, browser, or operating system to render text in a right-to-left sequence.
This character is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques by adversaries to trick users into opening malicious files.
authors: Micah Babinski, @micahbabinski, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems), Luc Génaux
falsepositives: Commandlines that contains scriptures such as arabic or hebrew might make use of this character

rules.title: User Added to Local Administrators Group
rules.description: Detects addition of users to the local administrator group via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using MSConfig Token Modification - Process
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using a msconfig GUI hack (UACMe 55)

rules.title: Modify Group Policy Settings
rules.description: Detect malicious GPO modifications can be used to implement many other malicious behaviors.

rules.title: Fsutil Suspicious Invocation
rules.description:
Detects suspicious parameters of fsutil (deleting USN journal, configuring it with small size, etc).
Might be used by ransomwares during the attack (seen by NotPetya and others).
falsepositives: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Suspicious Debugger Registration Cmdline
rules.description: Detects the registration of a debugger for a program that is available in the logon screen (sticky key backdoor).
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro

rules.title: Change Default File Association To Executable Via Assoc
rules.description:
Detects when a program changes the default file association of any extension to an executable.
When a file is opened, the default program used to open the file (also called the file association or handler) is checked. File association selections are stored in the Windows Registry and can be edited by users, administrators, or programs that have Registry access or by administrators using the built-in assoc utility. Applications can modify the file association for a given file extension to call an arbitrary program when a file with the given extension is opened.

rules.title: Writing Of Malicious Files To The Fonts Folder
rules.description: Monitors for the hiding possible malicious files in the C:\Windows\Fonts\ location. This folder doesn't require admin privillege to be written and executed from.

rules.title: CobaltStrike Load by Rundll32
rules.description: Rundll32 can be use by Cobalt Strike with StartW function to load DLLs from the command line.

rules.title: Suspicious Git Clone
rules.description: Detects execution of "git" in order to clone a remote repository that contain suspicious keywords which might be suspicious

rules.title: Finger.EXE Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the "finger.exe" utility.
Finger.EXE or "TCPIP Finger Command" is an old utility that is still present on modern Windows installation. It Displays information about users on a specified remote computer (typically a UNIX computer) that is running the finger service or daemon.
Due to the old nature of this utility and the rareness of machines having the finger service. Any execution of "finger.exe" can be considered "suspicious" and worth investigating.
falsepositives: Admin activity (unclear what they do nowadays with finger.exe)

rules.title: Windows MSIX Package Support Framework AI_STUBS Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of Advanced Installer MSIX Package Support Framework (PSF) components, specifically AI_STUBS executables with original filename 'popupwrapper.exe'.
This activity may indicate malicious MSIX packages build with Advanced Installer leveraging the Package Support Framework to bypass application control restrictions.
authors: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate applications packaged with Advanced Installer using Package Support Framework

rules.title: Proxy Execution Via Wuauclt.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) for proxy execution.
authors: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Sreeman, FPT.EagleEye Team

rules.title: New Agent Skills Installation Attempt Via Node.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the attempt to install new skills for AI agents using the "npx skills" command.
Agent skills enhance AI agents with new capabilities, but attackers may abuse this mechanism to inject malicious commands executed by the agent on behalf of the user.
The "npx skills" command can install skills for various agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, and others).
Analysts should review any installed skills to verify their legitimacy.
Note: Tune this rule based on whether AI agent tooling is allowed in your environment.
In environments where such tooling is authorized, this detection may reflect normal activity and the alert level should be adjusted accordingly.
In environments where AI agent tooling is not permitted, this activity is likely suspicious and may require immediate investigation.
falsepositives: This rule will be triggered when a new agent skill is installed regardless if it is benign or malicious.
High false positive rate expected in environments where AI agent tooling is authorized and commonly used.

rules.title: Suspicious Greedy Compression Using Rar.EXE
rules.description: Detects RAR usage that creates an archive from a suspicious folder, either a system folder or one of the folders often used by attackers for staging purposes

rules.title: ShimCache Flush
rules.description: Detects actions that clear the local ShimCache and remove forensic evidence

rules.title: HackTool - SharpWSUS/WSUSpendu Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of SharpWSUS or WSUSpendu, utilities that allow for lateral movement through WSUS.
Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) is a critical component of Windows systems and is frequently configured in a way that allows an attacker to circumvent internal networking limitations.

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via PresentationHost.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "PresentationHost" which is a utility that runs ".xbap" (Browser Applications) files to download arbitrary files

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Piped Password Via CLI
rules.description: Detects piping the password to an anydesk instance via CMD and the '--set-password' flag.
falsepositives: Legitimate piping of the password to anydesk
Some FP could occur with similar tools that uses the same command line '--set-password'

rules.title: Shadow Copies Creation Using Operating Systems Utilities
rules.description: Shadow Copies creation using operating systems utilities, possible credential access
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator working with shadow copies, access for backup purposes

rules.title: HackTool - SafetyKatz Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the hacktool SafetyKatz via PE information and default Image name

rules.title: HackTool - F-Secure C3 Load by Rundll32
rules.description: F-Secure C3 produces DLLs with a default exported StartNodeRelay function.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Server Web Shell Execution
rules.description: Detects potential web shell execution from the ScreenConnect server process.

rules.title: PUA - PingCastle Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of PingCastle, a tool designed to quickly assess the Active Directory security level.

rules.title: New Generic Credentials Added Via Cmdkey.EXE
rules.description:
Detects usage of "cmdkey.exe" to add generic credentials.
As an example, this can be used before connecting to an RDP session via command line interface.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Remote Command Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a system command via the ScreenConnect RMM service.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of ScreenConnect. Disable this rule if ScreenConnect is heavily used.

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation CLIP+ Launcher
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated use of Clip.exe to execute PowerShell

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of Defaultpack.EXE
rules.description: Detects uncommon child processes of "DefaultPack.EXE" binary as a proxy to launch other programs

rules.title: HackTool - SharpView Execution
rules.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems

rules.title: Potential Regsvr32 Commandline Flag Anomaly
rules.description: Detects a potential command line flag anomaly related to "regsvr32" in which the "/i" flag is used without the "/n" which should be uncommon.
falsepositives: Administrator typo might cause some false positives

rules.title: Discovery of a System Time
rules.description: Identifies use of various commands to query a systems time. This technique may be used before executing a scheduled task or to discover the time zone of a target system.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the system utilities to discover system time for legitimate reason

rules.title: Use of TTDInject.exe
rules.description: Detects the executiob of TTDInject.exe, which is used by Windows 10 v1809 and newer to debug time travel (underlying call of tttracer.exe)

rules.title: PowerShell Get-Process LSASS
rules.description: Detects a "Get-Process" cmdlet and it's aliases on lsass process, which is in almost all cases a sign of malicious activity

rules.title: Self Extracting Package Creation Via Iexpress.EXE From Potentially Suspicious Location
rules.description:
Detects the use of iexpress.exe to create binaries via Self Extraction Directive (SED) files located in potentially suspicious locations.
This behavior has been observed in-the-wild by different threat actors.

rules.title: Using SettingSyncHost.exe as LOLBin
rules.description: Detects using SettingSyncHost.exe to run hijacked binary

rules.title: Use of VisualUiaVerifyNative.exe
rules.description: VisualUiaVerifyNative.exe is a Windows SDK that can be used for AWL bypass and is listed in Microsoft's recommended block rules.
falsepositives: Legitimate testing of Microsoft UI parts.

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Downgrade Attack
rules.description: Detects PowerShell downgrade attack by comparing the host versions with the actually used engine version 2.0

rules.title: PUA - PingCastle Execution From Potentially Suspicious Parent
rules.description: Detects the execution of PingCastle, a tool designed to quickly assess the Active Directory security level via a script located in a potentially suspicious or uncommon location.

rules.title: Browser Started with Remote Debugging
rules.description: Detects browsers starting with the remote debugging flags. Which is a technique often used to perform browser injection attacks

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - Renamed MeshAgent Execution - Windows
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a renamed instance of the Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tool, MeshAgent.
RMM tools such as MeshAgent are commonly utilized by IT administrators for legitimate remote support and system management.
However, malicious actors may exploit these tools by renaming them to bypass detection mechanisms, enabling unauthorized access and control over compromised systems.

rules.title: DirLister Execution
rules.description: Detect the usage of "DirLister.exe" a utility for quickly listing folder or drive contents. It was seen used by BlackCat ransomware to create a list of accessible directories and files.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Execution
rules.description:
