An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Application Removed Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the removal or uninstallation of an application via "Wmic.EXE".

rules.title: Uncommon Child Process Of AddinUtil.EXE
rules.description: Detects uncommon child processes of the Add-In deployment cache updating utility (AddInutil.exe) which could be a sign of potential abuse of the binary to proxy execution via a custom Addins.Store payload.

rules.title: VeeamBackup Database Credentials Dump Via Sqlcmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects dump of credentials in VeeamBackup dbo

rules.title: Suspicious FileFix Execution Pattern
rules.description:
Detects suspicious FileFix execution patterns where users are tricked into running malicious commands through browser file upload dialog manipulation.
This attack typically begins when users visit malicious websites impersonating legitimate services or news platforms,
which may display fake CAPTCHA challenges or direct instructions to open file explorer and paste clipboard content.
The clipboard content usually contains commands that download and execute malware, such as information stealing tools.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of PowerShell or other utilities launched from browser extensions or automation tools

rules.title: Potential Binary Proxy Execution Via Cdb.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "cdb.exe" to launch arbitrary processes or commands from a debugger script file
authors: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Userinit Child Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious child process of userinit

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Powershell Search Order Hijacking - Task
rules.description: Detects suspicious powershell execution via a schedule task where the command ends with an suspicious flags to hide the powershell instance instead of executeing scripts or commands. This could be a sign of persistence via PowerShell "Get-Variable" technique as seen being used in Colibri Loader

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Disk Cleanup
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using scheduled tasks and variable expansion of cleanmgr.exe (UACMe 34)

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Obfuscation Via Reversed Commands
rules.description: Detects the presence of reversed PowerShell commands in the CommandLine. This is often used as a method of obfuscation by attackers
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Vasiliy Burov (rule), oscd.community, Tim Shelton

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - GoToAssist Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: Csc.EXE Execution Form Potentially Suspicious Parent
rules.description: Detects a potentially suspicious parent of "csc.exe", which could be a sign of payload delivery.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Dropping Of Password Filter DLL
rules.description: Detects dropping of dll files in system32 that may be used to retrieve user credentials from LSASS

rules.title: Suspicious VBoxDrvInst.exe Parameters
rules.description:
Detect VBoxDrvInst.exe run with parameters allowing processing INF file.
This allows to create values in the registry and install drivers.
For example one could use this technique to obtain persistence via modifying one of Run or RunOnce registry keys
falsepositives: Legitimate use of VBoxDrvInst.exe utility by VirtualBox Guest Additions installation process

rules.title: Reg Add Suspicious Paths
rules.description: Detects when an adversary uses the reg.exe utility to add or modify new keys or subkeys
falsepositives: Rare legitimate add to registry via cli (to these locations)

rules.title: File Download From IP Based URL Via CertOC.EXE
rules.description: Detects when a user downloads a file from an IP based URL using CertOC.exe

rules.title: DeviceCredentialDeployment Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of DeviceCredentialDeployment to hide a process from view.

rules.title: Use of FSharp Interpreters
rules.description:
Detects the execution of FSharp Interpreters "FsiAnyCpu.exe" and "FSi.exe"
Both can be used for AWL bypass and to execute F# code via scripts or inline.
falsepositives: Legitimate use by a software developer.

rules.title: Indirect Command Execution By Program Compatibility Wizard
rules.description: Detect indirect command execution via Program Compatibility Assistant pcwrun.exe
falsepositives: Need to use extra processing with 'unique_count' / 'filter' to focus on outliers as opposed to commonly seen artifacts

rules.title: Remotely Hosted HTA File Executed Via Mshta.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of the "mshta" utility with an argument containing the "http" keyword, which could indicate that an attacker is executing a remotely hosted malicious hta file

rules.title: HackTool - Inveigh Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Inveigh a cross-platform .NET IPv4/IPv6 machine-in-the-middle tool

rules.title: PowerShell Get-Clipboard Cmdlet Via CLI
rules.description: Detects usage of the 'Get-Clipboard' cmdlet via CLI

rules.title: Monitoring For Persistence Via BITS
rules.description:
BITS will allow you to schedule a command to execute after a successful download to notify you that the job is finished.
When the job runs on the system the command specified in the BITS job will be executed.
This can be abused by actors to create a backdoor within the system and for persistence.
It will be chained in a BITS job to schedule the download of malware/additional binaries and execute the program after being downloaded.

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell Encoded Command Patterns
rules.description: Detects PowerShell command line patterns in combincation with encoded commands that often appear in malware infection chains
falsepositives: Other tools that work with encoded scripts in the command line instead of script files

rules.title: Windows Defender Context Menu Removed
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe or PowerShell to delete the Windows Defender context menu handler registry keys.
This action removes the "Scan with Microsoft Defender" option from the right-click menu for files, directories, and drives.
Attackers may use this technique to hinder manual, on-demand scans and reduce the visibility of the security product.
falsepositives: May be part of a system customization or "debloating" script, but this is highly unusual in a managed corporate environment.

rules.title: New User Created Via Net.EXE With Never Expire Option
rules.description: Detects creation of local users via the net.exe command with the option "never expire"

rules.title: Potential Network Sniffing Activity Using Network Tools
rules.description:
Detects potential network sniffing via use of network tools such as "tshark", "windump".
Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection.
An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data.
authors: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate administration activity to troubleshoot network issues

rules.title: NodeJS Execution of JavaScript File
rules.description:
Detects execution of JavaScript or JSC files using NodeJs binary node.exe, that could be potentially suspicious.
Node.js is a popular open-source JavaScript runtime that runs code outside browsers and is widely used for both frontend and backend development.
Adversaries have been observed abusing Node.js to disguise malware as legitimate processes, evade security defenses, and maintain persistence within target systems.
Because Node.js is commonly used, this rule may generate false positives in some environments. However, if such activity is unusual in your environment, it is highly suspicious and warrants immediate investigation.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of node.exe to execute JavaScript or JSC files on your environment

rules.title: Potential WinAPI Calls Via CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the use of WinAPI Functions via the commandline. As seen used by threat actors via the tool winapiexec
falsepositives: Some legitimate action or applications may use these functions. Investigate further to determine the legitimacy of the activity.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious DLL Registered Via Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with the "REGSVR" action where the DLL in question doesn't contain a ".dll" extension. Which is often used as a method to evade defenses.

rules.title: Virtualbox Driver Installation or Starting of VMs
rules.description: Adversaries can carry out malicious operations using a virtual instance to avoid detection. This rule is built to detect the registration of the Virtualbox driver or start of a Virtualbox VM.
falsepositives: This may have false positives on hosts where Virtualbox is legitimately being used for operations

rules.title: Potential Password Spraying Attempt Using Dsacls.EXE
rules.description: Detects possible password spraying attempts using Dsacls
falsepositives: Legitimate use of dsacls to bind to an LDAP session

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Using New NetworkProvider - CLI
rules.description: Detects when an attacker tries to add a new network provider in order to dump clear text credentials, similar to how the NPPSpy tool does it
falsepositives: Other legitimate network providers used and not filtred in this rule

rules.title: Abusing Print Executable
rules.description: Attackers can use print.exe for remote file copy

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process of Notepad++ Updater - GUP.Exe
rules.description:
Detects suspicious child process creation by the Notepad++ updater process (gup.exe).
This could indicate potential exploitation of the updater component to deliver unwanted malware.

rules.title: Suspicious Desktopimgdownldr Command
rules.description: Detects a suspicious Microsoft desktopimgdownldr execution with parameters used to download files from the Internet
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Suspicious NTLM Authentication on the Printer Spooler Service
rules.description: Detects a privilege elevation attempt by coercing NTLM authentication on the Printer Spooler service

rules.title: Suspicious XOR Encoded PowerShell Command
rules.description: Detects presence of a potentially xor encoded powershell command
authors: Sami Ruohonen, Harish Segar, Tim Shelton, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Vasiliy Burov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Winrs Local Command Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Winrs.exe where it is used to execute commands locally.
Commands executed this way are launched under Winrshost.exe and can represent proxy execution used for defense evasion or lateral movement.

rules.title: Renamed Msdt.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "Msdt.exe" binary

rules.title: Group Membership Reconnaissance Via Whoami.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of whoami.exe with the /group command line flag to show group membership for the current user, account type, security identifiers (SID), and attributes.

rules.title: PUA - Wsudo Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of wsudo (Windows Sudo Utility). Which is a tool that let the user execute programs with different permissions (System, Trusted Installer, Administrator...etc)

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Event Viewer Child Process
rules.description: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes of "eventvwr.exe" which might indicate a UAC bypass attempt

rules.title: Suspicious Process Masquerading As SvcHost.EXE
rules.description:
Detects a suspicious process that is masquerading as the legitimate "svchost.exe" by naming its binary "svchost.exe" and executing from an uncommon location.
Adversaries often disguise their malicious binaries by naming them after legitimate system processes like "svchost.exe" to evade detection.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious EventLog Recon Activity Using Log Query Utilities
rules.description:
Detects execution of different log query utilities and commands to search and dump the content of specific event logs or look for specific event IDs.
This technique is used by threat actors in order to extract sensitive information from events logs such as usernames, IP addresses, hostnames, etc.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of the utility by administrators to query the event log

rules.title: Webshell Detection With Command Line Keywords
rules.description: Detects certain command line parameters often used during reconnaissance activity via web shells
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Anton Kutepov, oscd.community, Chad Hudson, Matt Anderson

rules.title: HackTool - SharpEvtMute Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of SharpEvtHook, a tool that tampers with the Windows event logs

rules.title: PUA - Advanced IP Scanner Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of Advanced IP Scanner. Seems to be a popular tool for ransomware groups.

rules.title: Compressed File Extraction Via Tar.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to extract compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities in order to decompress data to avoid detection.

rules.title: New Service Creation Using PowerShell
rules.description: Detects the creation of a new service using powershell.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user creates a service for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Service Startup Type Change Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects changes to service startup type to 'disabled' or 'manual' using the WMIC command-line utility.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative changes to service startup types using WMIC, investigate accordingly.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious NTFS Symlink Behavior Modification
rules.description: Detects the modification of NTFS symbolic link behavior using fsutil, which could be used to enable remote to local or remote to remote symlinks for potential attacks.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage, investigate the parent process and context to determine if benign.

rules.title: Suspicious AgentExecutor PowerShell Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the AgentExecutor.exe binary. Which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute powershell scripts with the ExecutionPolicy "Bypass" or any binary named "powershell.exe" located in the path provided by 6th positional argument

rules.title: RunMRU Registry Key Deletion
rules.description:
Detects deletion of the RunMRU registry key, which stores the history of commands executed via the Run dialog.
In the clickfix techniques, the phishing lures instruct users to open a run dialog through (Win + R) and execute malicious commands.
Adversaries may delete this key to cover their tracks after executing commands.

rules.title: Add Potential Suspicious New Download Source To Winget
rules.description: Detects usage of winget to add new potentially suspicious download sources

rules.title: Windows Credential Guard Registry Tampering Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects attempts to add, modify, or delete Windows Credential Guard related registry keys or values via command line tools such as Reg.exe or PowerShell.
Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may disable Credential Guard to gain access to sensitive credentials stored in the system, such as NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets, which can be used for lateral movement and privilege escalation.
The rule matches suspicious command lines that target DeviceGuard or LSA registry paths and manipulate keys like EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity, RequirePlatformSecurityFeatures, or LsaCfgFlags.
Such activity may indicate an attempt to disable or tamper with Credential Guard, potentially exposing sensitive credentials for misuse.

rules.title: Renamed Sysinternals Sdelete Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of a renamed SysInternals Sdelete, which is something an administrator shouldn't do (the renaming)

rules.title: Enumerate All Information With Whoami.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "whoami.exe" with the "/all" flag
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Covenant PowerShell Launcher
rules.description: Detects suspicious command lines used in Covenant luanchers
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Suspicious Microsoft OneNote Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of the Microsoft OneNote application. This may indicate an attempt to execute malicious embedded objects from a .one file.
authors: Tim Rauch (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Elastic (idea)
falsepositives: File located in the AppData folder with trusted signature

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Activity Using SeCEdit
rules.description: Detects potential suspicious behaviour using secedit.exe. Such as exporting or modifying the security policy

rules.title: Whoami.EXE Execution With Output Option
rules.description: Detects the execution of "whoami.exe" with the "/FO" flag to choose CSV as output format or with redirection options to export the results to a file for later use.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Import PowerShell Modules From Suspicious Directories - ProcCreation
rules.description: Detects powershell scripts that import modules from suspicious directories

rules.title: Potential Manage-bde.wsf Abuse To Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of the "manage-bde.wsf" script as a LOLBIN to proxy execution
authors: oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Rundll32 Execution With Uncommon DLL Extension
rules.description: Detects the execution of rundll32 with a command line that doesn't contain a common extension
authors: Tim Shelton, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Yassine Oukessou

rules.title: File Explorer Folder Opened Using Explorer Folder Shortcut Via Shell
rules.description: Detects the initial execution of "cmd.exe" which spawns "explorer.exe" with the appropriate command line arguments for opening the "My Computer" folder.

rules.title: System Language Discovery via Reg.Exe
rules.description:
Detects the usage of Reg.Exe to query system language settings.
Attackers may discover the system language to determine the geographic location of victims, customize payloads for specific regions,
or avoid targeting certain locales to evade detection.

rules.title: Suspicious Uninstall of Windows Defender Feature via PowerShell
rules.description: Detects the use of PowerShell with Uninstall-WindowsFeature or Remove-WindowsFeature cmdlets to disable or remove the Windows Defender GUI feature, a common technique used by adversaries to evade defenses.

rules.title: Registry Manipulation via WMI Stdregprov
rules.description:
Detects the usage of wmic.exe to modify Windows registry via the WMI StdRegProv class write methods (CreateKey, DeleteKey, SetStringValue, etc.).
This behaviour could be potentially suspicious because it uses an alternative method to modify registry keys instead of legitimate registry tools like reg.exe or regedit.exe.
Attackers specifically choose this technique to evade detection and bypass security monitoring focused on traditional registry modification commands.

rules.title: HackTool - SharpUp PrivEsc Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of SharpUp, a tool for local privilege escalation

rules.title: Stop Windows Service Via PowerShell Stop-Service
rules.description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the PowerShell Cmdlet "Stop-Service"
authors: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behaviour in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly

rules.title: Renamed PAExec Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of renamed version of PAExec. Often used by attackers
falsepositives: Weird admins that rename their tools
Software companies that bundle PAExec with their software and rename it, so that it is less embarrassing
When executed with the "-s" flag. PAExec will copy itself to the "C:\Windows\" directory with a different name. Usually like this "PAExec-[XXXXX]-[ComputerName]"

rules.title: Scheduled Task Executing Encoded Payload from Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that potentially executes a base64 encoded payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
authors: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Assembly Loading Via CL_LoadAssembly.ps1
rules.description: Detects calls to "LoadAssemblyFromPath" or "LoadAssemblyFromNS" that are part of the "CL_LoadAssembly.ps1" script. This can be abused to load different assemblies and bypass App locker controls.

rules.title: Hacktool - EDR-Freeze Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of EDR-Freeze, a tool that exploits the MiniDumpWriteDump function and WerFaultSecure.exe to suspend EDR and Antivirus processes on Windows.
EDR-Freeze leverages a race-condition attack to put security processes into a dormant state by suspending WerFaultSecure at the moment it freezes the target process.
This technique does not require kernel-level exploits or BYOVD, but instead abuses user-mode functionality to temporarily disable monitoring by EDR or Antimalware solutions.

rules.title: Suspicious Schtasks Execution AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects the creation of a schtask that executes a file from C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local

rules.title: Data Export From MSSQL Table Via BCP.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the BCP utility in order to export data from the database.
Attackers were seen saving their malware to a database column or table and then later extracting it via "bcp.exe" into a file.
authors: Omar Khaled (@beacon_exe), MahirAli Khan (in/mahiralikhan), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Permission Check Via Accesschk.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of the "Accesschk" utility, an access and privilege audit tool developed by SysInternal and often being abused by attacker to verify process privileges
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Mangatas Tondang, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Audit Policy Tampering Via NT Resource Kit Auditpol
rules.description:
Threat actors can use an older version of the auditpol binary available inside the NT resource kit to change audit policy configuration to impair detection capability.
This can be carried out by selectively disabling/removing certain audit policies as well as restoring a custom policy owned by the threat actor.
falsepositives: The old auditpol utility isn't available by default on recent versions of Windows as it was replaced by a newer version. The FP rate should be very low except for tools that use a similar flag structure

rules.title: Powershell Base64 Encoded MpPreference Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects base64 encoded "MpPreference" PowerShell cmdlet code that tries to modifies or tamper with Windows Defender AV

rules.title: Copy From VolumeShadowCopy Via Cmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of the builtin "copy" command that targets a shadow copy (sometimes used to copy registry hives that are in use)
authors: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious CodePage Switch Via CHCP
rules.description: Detects a code page switch in command line or batch scripts to a rare language
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
falsepositives: Administrative activity (adjust code pages according to your organization's region)

rules.title: System Disk And Volume Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
An adversary might use WMI to discover information about the system, such as the volume name, size,
free space, and other disk information. This can be done using the 'wmic' command-line utility and has been
observed being used by threat actors such as Volt Typhoon.

rules.title: HackTool - SharpDPAPI Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of the SharpDPAPI tool based on CommandLine flags and PE metadata.
SharpDPAPI is a C# port of some DPAPI functionality from the Mimikatz project.

rules.title: Suspicious Autorun Registry Modified via WMI
rules.description: Detects suspicious activity where the WMIC process is used to create an autorun registry entry via reg.exe, which is often indicative of persistence mechanisms employed by malware.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative activity or software installations

rules.title: Run PowerShell Script from Redirected Input Stream
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script execution via input stream redirect

rules.title: Net WebClient Casing Anomalies
rules.description: Detects PowerShell command line contents that include a suspicious abnormal casing in the Net.Webclient (e.g. nEt.WEbCliEnT) string as used in obfuscation techniques

rules.title: Suspicious Reconnaissance Activity Using Get-LocalGroupMember Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects suspicious reconnaissance command line activity on Windows systems using the PowerShell Get-LocalGroupMember Cmdlet

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Via LSASS Process Clone
rules.description: Detects a suspicious LSASS process process clone that could be a sign of credential dumping activity

rules.title: PUA - Mouse Lock Execution
rules.description: In Kaspersky's 2020 Incident Response Analyst Report they listed legitimate tool "Mouse Lock" as being used for both credential access and collection in security incidents.
falsepositives: Legitimate uses of Mouse Lock software

rules.title: Shadow Copies Deletion Using Operating Systems Utilities
rules.description: Shadow Copies deletion using operating systems utilities
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Michael Haag, Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)
falsepositives: Legitimate Administrator deletes Shadow Copies using operating systems utilities for legitimate reason

rules.title: Potential Ransomware or Unauthorized MBR Tampering Via Bcdedit.EXE
rules.description: Detects potential malicious and unauthorized usage of bcdedit.exe

rules.title: Suspicious Encoded PowerShell Command Line
rules.description: Detects suspicious powershell process starts with base64 encoded commands (e.g. Emotet)
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Anton Kutepov, oscd.community

rules.title: PUA - SoftPerfect Netscan Execution
rules.description:
Detects usage of SoftPerfect's "netscan.exe". An application for scanning networks.
It is actively used in-the-wild by threat actors to inspect and understand the network architecture of a victim.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Process of KeyScrambler.exe
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of KeyScrambler.exe

rules.title: HackTool - HandleKatz LSASS Dumper Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of HandleKatz, a tool that demonstrates the usage of cloned handles to Lsass in order to create an obfuscated memory dump of the same

rules.title: RunDLL32 Spawning Explorer
rules.description: Detects RunDLL32.exe spawning explorer.exe as child, which is very uncommon, often observes Gamarue spawning the explorer.exe process in an unusual way

rules.title: Suspicious Kerberos Ticket Request via CLI
rules.description:
Detects suspicious Kerberos ticket requests via command line using System.IdentityModel.Tokens.KerberosRequestorSecurityToken class.
Threat actors may use command line interfaces to request Kerberos tickets for service accounts in order to
perform offline password cracking attacks commonly known as Kerberoasting or other Kerberos ticket abuse
techniques like silver ticket attacks.
falsepositives: Legitimate command line usage by administrators or security tools.

rules.title: PrintBrm ZIP Creation of Extraction
rules.description: Detects the execution of the LOLBIN PrintBrm.exe, which can be used to create or extract ZIP files. PrintBrm.exe should not be run on a normal workstation.

rules.title: Suspicious Driver/DLL Installation Via Odbcconf.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with the "INSTALLDRIVER" action where the driver doesn't contain a ".dll" extension. This is often used as a defense evasion method.

rules.title: Unmount Share Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects when when a mounted share is removed. Adversaries may remove share connections that are no longer useful in order to clean up traces of their operation
falsepositives: Administrators or Power users may remove their shares via cmd line

rules.title: Conhost Spawned By Uncommon Parent Process
rules.description: Detects when the Console Window Host (conhost.exe) process is spawned by an uncommon parent process, which could be indicative of potential code injection activity.

rules.title: Suspicious Process Parents
rules.description: Detects suspicious parent processes that should not have any children or should only have a single possible child program

rules.title: Registry Export of Third-Party Credentials
rules.description:
Detects the use of reg.exe to export registry paths associated with third-party credentials.
Credential stealers have been known to use this technique to extract sensitive information from the registry.

rules.title: Devtoolslauncher.exe Executes Specified Binary
rules.description: The Devtoolslauncher.exe executes other binary
falsepositives: Legitimate use of devtoolslauncher.exe by legitimate user

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution Of Regasm/Regsvcs From Uncommon Location
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Regasm/Regsvcs utilities from a potentially suspicious location

rules.title: Suspicious Eventlog Clearing or Configuration Change Activity
rules.description:
Detects the clearing or configuration tampering of EventLog using utilities such as "wevtutil", "powershell" and "wmic".
This technique were seen used by threat actors and ransomware strains in order to evade defenses.
authors: Ecco, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, D3F7A5105, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Tasks Folder Evasion
rules.description:
The Tasks folder in system32 and syswow64 are globally writable paths.
Adversaries can take advantage of this and load or influence any script hosts or ANY .NET Application
in Tasks to load and execute a custom assembly into cscript, wscript, regsvr32, mshta, eventvwr

rules.title: MSHTA Execution with Suspicious File Extensions
rules.description:
Detects execution of mshta.exe with file types that looks like they do not typically represent HTA (HTML Application) content,
such as .png, .jpg, .zip, .pdf, and others, which are often polyglots. MSHTA is a legitimate Windows utility for executing HTML Applications
containing VBScript or JScript. Threat actors often abuse this lolbin utility to download and
execute malicious scripts disguised as benign files or hosted under misleading extensions to evade detection.
authors: Diego Perez (@darkquassar), Markus Neis, Swisscom (Improve Rule), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: File Decoded From Base64/Hex Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with either the "decode" or "decodehex" flags to decode base64 or hex encoded files. This can be abused by attackers to decode an encoded payload before execution
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community

rules.title: Recon Command Output Piped To Findstr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a potential recon command where the results are piped to "findstr". This is meant to trigger on inline calls of "cmd.exe" via the "/c" or "/k" for example.
Attackers often time use this technique to extract specific information they require in their reconnaissance phase.

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Trace ETW Session Tamper Via Logman.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "logman" utility in order to disable or delete Windows trace sessions
falsepositives: Installer tools that disable services, e.g. before log collection agent installation

rules.title: New User Created Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Identifies the creation of local users via the net.exe command.
authors: Endgame, JHasenbusch (adapted to Sigma for oscd.community)
falsepositives: Better use event IDs for user creation rather than command line rules.

rules.title: DLL Execution via Rasautou.exe
rules.description: Detects using Rasautou.exe for loading arbitrary .DLL specified in -d option and executes the export specified in -p.

rules.title: New Firewall Rule Added Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects the addition of a new rule to the Windows firewall via netsh

value.pattern: ^.*advfirewall\ firewall\ add\ rule\ name=Dropbox\ dir=in\ action=allow\ "program=.:\\Program\ Files\ \(x86\)\\Dropbox\\Client\\Dropbox\.exe"\ enable=yes\ profile=Any.*$
^.*advfirewall\ firewall\ add\ rule\ name=Dropbox\ dir=in\ action=allow\ "program=.:\\Program\ Files\\Dropbox\\Client\\Dropbox\.exe"\ enable=yes\ profile=Any.*$

rules.title: Lolbin Runexehelper Use As Proxy
rules.description: Detect usage of the "runexehelper.exe" binary as a proxy to launch other programs

rules.title: Renamed SysInternals DebugView Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious renamed SysInternals DebugView execution

rules.title: HackTool - ADCSPwn Execution
rules.description: Detects command line parameters used by ADCSPwn, a tool to escalate privileges in an active directory network by coercing authenticate from machine accounts and relaying to the certificate service

rules.title: Always Install Elevated Windows Installer
rules.description: Detects Windows Installer service (msiexec.exe) trying to install MSI packages with SYSTEM privilege

rules.title: Potential Encoded PowerShell Patterns In CommandLine
rules.description: Detects specific combinations of encoding methods in PowerShell via the commandline
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Vasiliy Burov (rule), oscd.community, Tim Shelton

rules.title: Suspicious Windows Service Tampering
rules.description: Detects the usage of binaries such as 'net', 'sc' or 'powershell' in order to stop, pause, disable or delete critical or important Windows services such as AV, Backup, etc. As seen being used in some ransomware scripts
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113 , X__Junior (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Administrators or tools shutting down the services due to upgrade or removal purposes. If you experience some false positive, please consider adding filters to the parent process launching this command and not removing the entry

rules.title: InfDefaultInstall.exe .inf Execution
rules.description: Executes SCT script using scrobj.dll from a command in entered into a specially prepared INF file.

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Of Manage Engine ServiceDesk
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of the "Manage Engine ServiceDesk Plus" Java web service
falsepositives: Legitimate sub processes started by Manage Engine ServiceDesk Pro

rules.title: Potential Dropper Script Execution Via WScript/CScript/MSHTA
rules.description: Detects wscript/cscript/mshta executions of scripts located in user directories
authors: Margaritis Dimitrios (idea), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Dave Johnson
falsepositives: Some installers might generate a similar behavior. An initial baseline is required

rules.title: OpenWith.exe Executes Specified Binary
rules.description: The OpenWith.exe executes other binary

rules.title: HackTool - Impersonate Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the Impersonate tool. Which can be used to manipulate tokens on a Windows computers remotely (PsExec/WmiExec) or interactively

rules.title: HackTool - SharpChisel Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of the Sharp Chisel via the commandline arguments

rules.title: Kavremover Dropped Binary LOLBIN Usage
rules.description: Detects the execution of a signed binary dropped by Kaspersky Lab Products Remover (kavremover) which can be abused as a LOLBIN to execute arbitrary commands and binaries.

rules.title: File Download Via Bitsadmin
rules.description: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file
falsepositives: Some legitimate apps use this, but limited.

rules.title: Verclsid.exe Runs COM Object
rules.description: Detects when verclsid.exe is used to run COM object via GUID

rules.title: PUA - CsExec Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of the lesser known remote execution tool named CsExec a PsExec alternative

rules.title: PUA - WebBrowserPassView Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of WebBrowserPassView.exe. A password recovery tool that reveals the passwords stored by the following Web browsers, Internet Explorer (Version 4.0 - 11.0), Mozilla Firefox (All Versions), Google Chrome, Safari, and Opera

rules.title: Potential Amazon SSM Agent Hijacking
rules.description: Detects potential Amazon SSM agent hijack attempts as outlined in the Mitiga research report.

rules.title: New Root Certificate Installed Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "certutil" with the "addstore" flag in order to install a new certificate on the system.
Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.
falsepositives: Help Desk or IT may need to manually add a corporate Root CA on occasion. Need to test if GPO push doesn't trigger FP

rules.title: WmiPrvSE Spawned A Process
rules.description: Detects WmiPrvSE spawning a process
falsepositives: False positives are expected (e.g. in environments where WinRM is used legitimately)

rules.title: XBAP Execution From Uncommon Locations Via PresentationHost.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of ".xbap" (Browser Applications) files via PresentationHost.EXE from an uncommon location. These files can be abused to run malicious ".xbap" files any bypass AWL

rules.title: PUA - AdvancedRun Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of AdvancedRun utility

rules.title: Suspicious Cross-User Process Spawn
rules.description:
Detects suspicious spawning of a process under a different user context than the parent process.
Processes such as notepad.exe, calculator etc. are generally spawned under the same user context and
also they are often targeted as sacrificial process or decoy process to check successful privilege escalation.
falsepositives: RunAs usage spawning one of the listed binaries under a different account

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Command Targeting Teams Sensitive Files
rules.description:
Detects a commandline containing references to the Microsoft Teams database or cookies files from a process other than Teams.
The database might contain authentication tokens and other sensitive information about the logged in accounts.

rules.title: HackTool - UACMe Akagi Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of UACMe, a tool used for UAC bypasses, via default PE metadata
authors: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - DIT Snapshot Viewer
rules.description: Detects the use of Ditsnap tool, an inspection tool for Active Directory database, ntds.dit.

rules.title: Ie4uinit Lolbin Use From Invalid Path
rules.description: Detect use of ie4uinit.exe to execute commands from a specially prepared ie4uinit.inf file from a directory other than the usual directories
falsepositives: ViberPC updater calls this binary with the following commandline "ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache"

rules.title: New Network Trace Capture Started Via Netsh.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of netsh with the "trace" flag in order to start a network capture

rules.title: Password Provided In Command Line Of Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects a when net.exe is called with a password in the command line

rules.title: HackTool - Doppelanger LSASS Dumper Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the Doppelanger hacktool which is used to dump LSASS memory via process cloning while evading common detection methods

rules.title: Suspicious ClickFix/FileFix Execution Pattern
rules.description:
Detects suspicious execution patterns where users are tricked into running malicious commands via clipboard manipulation, either through the Windows Run dialog (ClickFix) or File Explorer address bar (FileFix).
Attackers leverage social engineering campaigns—such as fake CAPTCHA challenges or urgent alerts—encouraging victims to paste clipboard contents, often executing mshta.exe, powershell.exe, or similar commands to infect systems.

rules.title: Abused Debug Privilege by Arbitrary Parent Processes
rules.description: Detection of unusual child processes by different system processes

rules.title: HackTool - WinPwn Execution
rules.description: Detects commandline keywords indicative of potential usge of the tool WinPwn. A tool for Windows and Active Directory reconnaissance and exploitation.

rules.title: Sysprep on AppData Folder
rules.description: Detects suspicious sysprep process start with AppData folder as target (as used by Trojan Syndicasec in Thrip report by Symantec)
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: PDQ Deploy Remote Adminstartion Tool Execution
rules.description: Detect use of PDQ Deploy remote admin tool

rules.title: Suspicious FromBase64String Usage On Gzip Archive - Process Creation
rules.description: Detects attempts of decoding a base64 Gzip archive via PowerShell. This technique is often used as a method to load malicious content into memory afterward.

rules.title: PUA- IOX Tunneling Tool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of IOX - a tool for port forwarding and intranet proxy purposes

rules.title: Add SafeBoot Keys Via Reg Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "add" or "copy" flags on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to allow the ransomware to work in safe mode as some security products do not

rules.title: HackTool - DInjector PowerShell Cradle Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of the Dinject PowerShell cradle based on the specific flags

rules.title: Bypass UAC via WSReset.exe
rules.description: Detects use of WSReset.exe to bypass User Account Control (UAC). Adversaries use this technique to execute privileged processes.
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Tony Lambert), oscd.community, Florian Roth

rules.title: Windows EventLog Autologger Session Registry Modification Via CommandLine
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable Windows EventLog autologger sessions via registry modification.
The AutoLogger event tracing session records events that occur early in the operating system boot process.
Applications and device drivers can use the AutoLogger session to capture traces before the user logs in.
Adversaries may disable these sessions to evade detection and prevent security monitoring of early boot activities and system events.

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Command Line Obfuscation
rules.description: Detects the PowerShell command lines with special characters
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Vasiliy Burov (rule), oscd.community, Tim Shelton (fp)

rules.title: Proxy Execution via Vshadow
rules.description:
Detects the invocation of vshadow.exe with the -exec parameter that executes a specified script or command after the shadow copies are created but before the VShadow tool exits.
VShadow is a command-line tool that you can use to create and manage volume shadow copies. While legitimate backup or administrative scripts may use this flag,
attackers can leverage this parameter to proxy the execution of malware.

rules.title: Suspicious Control Panel DLL Load
rules.description: Detects suspicious Rundll32 execution from control.exe as used by Equation Group and Exploit Kits

rules.title: Arbitrary DLL or Csproj Code Execution Via Dotnet.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of arbitrary DLLs or unsigned code via a ".csproj" files via Dotnet.EXE.

rules.title: Php Inline Command Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of php using the "-r" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live php code.

rules.title: Remote Access Tool - LogMeIn Execution
rules.description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

rules.title: PUA - NirCmd Execution As LOCAL SYSTEM
rules.description: Detects the use of NirCmd tool for command execution as SYSTEM user
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - SharpLdapWhoami Execution
rules.description: Detects SharpLdapWhoami, a whoami alternative that queries the LDAP service on a domain controller
falsepositives: Programs that use the same command line flags

rules.title: Possible Privilege Escalation via Weak Service Permissions
rules.description: Detection of sc.exe utility spawning by user with Medium integrity level to change service ImagePath or FailureCommand

rules.title: Suspicious Group And Account Reconnaissance Activity Using Net.EXE
rules.description:
Detects suspicious reconnaissance command line activity on Windows systems using Net.EXE
Check if the user that executed the commands is suspicious (e.g. service accounts, LOCAL_SYSTEM)
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), omkar72, @svch0st, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Sdclt Child Processes
rules.description: A General detection for sdclt spawning new processes. This could be an indicator of sdclt being used for bypass UAC techniques.

rules.title: Windows Defender Disabled Via SystemSettingsAdminFlows.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the usage of SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe to disable Windows Defender.
SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe is a legitimate Windows component used for administrative configuration tasks.
However, attackers may abuse it to disable Windows Defender as part of their attack chain, especially in the context of ransomware or other malware campaigns.
authors: Chirag Damani (KPMG India), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate turn off of Windows Defender by the technical users or administrators for troubleshooting or other purposes.

rules.title: Windows Recovery Environment Disabled Via Reagentc
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable windows recovery environment using Reagentc.
ReAgentc.exe is a command-line tool in Windows used to manage the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE).
It allows users to enable, disable, and configure WinRE, which is used for troubleshooting and repairing common boot issues.

rules.title: Delete Important Scheduled Task
rules.description: Detects when adversaries stop services or processes by deleting their respective scheduled tasks in order to conduct data destructive activities

rules.title: Suspicious Cabinet File Execution Via Msdt.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of msdt.exe using the "cab" flag which could indicates suspicious diagcab files with embedded answer files leveraging CVE-2022-30190

rules.title: Dynamic .NET Compilation Via Csc.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "csc.exe" to compile .NET code. Attackers often leverage this to compile code on the fly and use it in other stages.

rules.title: Suspicious Spool Service Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious print spool service (spoolsv.exe) child processes.

rules.title: Windows Default Domain GPO Modification via GPME
rules.description:
Detects the use of the Group Policy Management Editor (GPME) to modify Default Domain or Default Domain Controllers Group Policy Objects (GPOs).
Adversaries may leverage GPME to make stealthy changes in these default GPOs to deploy malicious GPOs configurations across the domain without raising suspicion.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of GPME to modify GPOs

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation via Masqueraded XML File
rules.description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task using the "-XML" flag with a file without the '.xml' extension. This behavior could be indicative of potential defense evasion attempt during persistence

rules.title: Registry Modification of MS-settings Protocol Handler
rules.description:
Detects registry modifications to the 'ms-settings' protocol handler, which is frequently targeted for UAC bypass or persistence.
Attackers can modify this registry to execute malicious code with elevated privileges by hijacking the command execution path.

rules.title: Use NTFS Short Name in Command Line
rules.description: Detect use of the Windows 8.3 short name. Which could be used as a method to avoid command-line detection
falsepositives: Applications could use this notation occasionally which might generate some false positives. In that case Investigate the parent and child process.

rules.title: Suspicious LNK Command-Line Padding with Whitespace Characters
rules.description:
Detects exploitation of LNK file command-line length discrepancy, where attackers hide malicious commands beyond the 260-character UI limit while the actual command-line argument field supports 4096 characters using whitespace padding (e.g., 0x20, 0x09-0x0D).
Adversaries insert non-printable whitespace characters (e.g., Line Feed \x0A, Carriage Return \x0D) to pad the visible section of the LNK file, pushing malicious commands past the UI-visible boundary.
The hidden payload, executed at runtime but invisible in Windows Explorer properties, enables stealthy execution and evasion—commonly used for social engineering attacks.
This rule flags suspicious use of such padding observed in real-world attacks.

rules.title: Data Copied To Clipboard Via Clip.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of clip.exe in order to copy data to the clipboard. Adversaries may collect data stored in the clipboard from users copying information within or between applications.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Run Keys Using Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects suspicious command line reg.exe tool adding key to RUN key in Registry
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.

rules.title: Powershell Token Obfuscation - Process Creation
rules.description: Detects TOKEN OBFUSCATION technique from Invoke-Obfuscation

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Ping/Copy Command Combination
rules.description: Detects uncommon and potentially suspicious one-liner command containing both "ping" and "copy" at the same time, which is usually used by malware.

rules.title: DumpMinitool Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of "DumpMinitool.exe" a tool that allows the dump of process memory via the use of the "MiniDumpWriteDump"
authors: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Disabled Volume Snapshots
rules.description: Detects commands that temporarily turn off Volume Snapshots

rules.title: Node Process Executions
rules.description: Detects the execution of other scripts using the Node executable packaged with Adobe Creative Cloud

rules.title: Renamed AdFind Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of a renamed Adfind.exe. AdFind continues to be seen across majority of breaches. It is used to domain trust discovery to plan out subsequent steps in the attack chain.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Child Processes Spawned by ConHost
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes related to Windows Shell utilities spawned by `conhost.exe`, which could indicate malicious activity using trusted system components.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative tasks using `conhost.exe` to spawn child processes such as `cmd.exe`, `powershell.exe`, or `regsvr32.exe`.

rules.title: Windows Hotfix Updates Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of wmic with the "qfe" flag in order to obtain information about installed hotfix updates on the system. This is often used by pentester and attacker enumeration scripts

rules.title: Enumeration for Credentials in Registry
rules.description:
Adversaries may search the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials.
The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs.
Adversaries may query the Registry looking for credentials and passwords that have been stored for use by other programs or services

rules.title: Renamed Cloudflared.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "cloudflared" binary.

rules.title: Detected Windows Software Discovery
rules.description: Adversaries may attempt to enumerate software for a variety of reasons, such as figuring out what security measures are present or if the compromised system has a version of software that is vulnerable.

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Use Clip
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via use Clip.exe in Scripts

rules.title: Suspicious WMIC Execution Via Office Process
rules.description: Office application called wmic to proxye execution through a LOLBIN process. This is often used to break suspicious parent-child chain (Office app spawns LOLBin).

rules.title: Potential DLL Sideloading Via DeviceEnroller.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the use of the PhoneDeepLink parameter to potentially sideload a DLL file that does not exist. This non-existent DLL file is named "ShellChromeAPI.dll".
Adversaries can drop their own renamed DLL and execute it via DeviceEnroller.exe using this parameter

rules.title: QuickAssist Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of Microsoft Quick Assist tool "QuickAssist.exe". This utility can be used by attackers to gain remote access.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Quick Assist in the environment.

rules.title: Suspicious Remote Child Process From Outlook
rules.description: Detects a suspicious child process spawning from Outlook where the image is located in a remote location (SMB/WebDav shares).

rules.title: Suspicious Curl.EXE Download
rules.description: Detects a suspicious curl process start on Windows and outputs the requested document to a local file
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential MsiExec Masquerading
rules.description: Detects the execution of msiexec.exe from an uncommon directory

rules.title: LOLBAS Data Exfiltration by DataSvcUtil.exe
rules.description: Detects when a user performs data exfiltration by using DataSvcUtil.exe
falsepositives: DataSvcUtil.exe being used may be performed by a system administrator.
Verify whether the user identity, user agent, and/or hostname should be making changes in your environment.
DataSvcUtil.exe being executed from unfamiliar users should be investigated. If known behavior is causing false positives, it can be exempted from the rule.

rules.title: Compress Data and Lock With Password for Exfiltration With WINZIP
rules.description: An adversary may compress or encrypt data that is collected prior to exfiltration using 3rd party utilities

rules.title: PUA - Netcat Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of Netcat. Adversaries may use a non-application layer protocol for communication between host and C2 server or among infected hosts within a network

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Obfuscation Via WCHAR/CHAR
rules.description: Detects suspicious encoded character syntax often used for defense evasion

rules.title: Curl File Upload To File Sharing Websites
rules.description: Detects usage of curl to upload files to known file sharing domains, which may indicate data exfiltration.
falsepositives: Legitimate file uploads to these services by administrators or developers

rules.title: Base64 Encoded PowerShell Command Detected
rules.description: Detects usage of the "FromBase64String" function in the commandline which is used to decode a base64 encoded string

rules.title: Suspicious Mshta.EXE Execution Patterns
rules.description: Detects suspicious mshta process execution patterns
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: PUA - Rclone Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of RClone utility for exfiltration as used by various ransomwares strains like REvil, Conti, FiveHands, etc
authors: Bhabesh Raj, Sittikorn S, Aaron Greetham (@beardofbinary) - NCC Group

rules.title: System File Execution Location Anomaly
rules.description: Detects the execution of a Windows system binary that is usually located in the system folder from an uncommon location.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Patrick Bareiss, Anton Kutepov, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Disable Windows IIS HTTP Logging
rules.description: Disables HTTP logging on a Windows IIS web server as seen by Threat Group 3390 (Bronze Union)

rules.title: UAC Bypass via Windows Firewall Snap-In Hijack
rules.description: Detects attempts to bypass User Account Control (UAC) by hijacking the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) Windows Firewall snap-in

rules.title: Potential Product Class Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the execution of WMIC in order to get a list of firewall, antivirus and antispywware products.
Adversaries often enumerate security products installed on a system to identify security controls and potential ways to evade detection or disable protection mechanisms.
This information helps them plan their next attack steps and choose appropriate techniques to bypass security measures.
authors: Michael Haag, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), juju4, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of wmic.exe for reconnaissance of firewall, antivirus and antispywware products.

rules.title: Gpresult Display Group Policy Information
rules.description: Detects cases in which a user uses the built-in Windows utility gpresult to display the Resultant Set of Policy (RSoP) information

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32 Activity
rules.description: Detects suspicious execution of rundll32, with specific calls to some DLLs with known LOLBIN functionalities
authors: juju4, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Active Directory Structure Export Via Csvde.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of "csvde.exe" in order to export organizational Active Directory structure.

rules.title: File Encoded To Base64 Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with the "encode" flag to encode a file to base64. This can be abused by threat actors and attackers for data exfiltration
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: As this is a general purpose rule, legitimate usage of the encode functionality will trigger some false positives. Apply additional filters accordingly

rules.title: Network Reconnaissance Activity
rules.description: Detects a set of suspicious network related commands often used in recon stages
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Renamed Mavinject.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed version of the "Mavinject" process. Which can be abused to perform process injection using the "/INJECTRUNNING" flag

rules.title: Bypass UAC via CMSTP
rules.description: Detect commandline usage of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) to install specially formatted local .INF files
authors: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
falsepositives: Legitimate use of cmstp.exe utility by legitimate user

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell Download and Execute Pattern
rules.description: Detects suspicious PowerShell download patterns that are often used in malicious scripts, stagers or downloaders (make sure that your backend applies the strings case-insensitive)
falsepositives: Software installers that pull packages from remote systems and execute them

rules.title: PUA - Kernel Driver Utility (KDU) Execution
rules.description:
Detects execution of the Kernel Driver Utility (KDU) tool.
KDU can be used to bypass driver signature enforcement and load unsigned or malicious drivers into the Windows kernel.
Potentially allowing for privilege escalation, persistence, or evasion of security controls.
authors: Matt Anderson, Dray Agha, Anna Pham (Huntress)
falsepositives: Legitimate driver development, testing, or administrative troubleshooting (e.g., enabling/disabling hardware)

rules.title: Dllhost.EXE Execution Anomaly
rules.description: Detects a "dllhost" process spawning with no commandline arguments which is very rare to happen and could indicate process injection activity or malware mimicking similar system processes.

rules.title: Copying Sensitive Files with Credential Data
rules.description: Files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) copying
falsepositives: Copying sensitive files for legitimate use (eg. backup) or forensic investigation by legitimate incident responder or forensic investigator.

rules.title: Interesting Service Enumeration Via Sc.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the enumeration and query of interesting and in some cases sensitive services on the system via "sc.exe".
Attackers often try to enumerate the services currently running on a system in order to find different attack vectors.

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via MSEDGE_PROXY.EXE
rules.description: Detects usage of "msedge_proxy.exe" to download arbitrary files

rules.title: Suspicious HH.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects a suspicious execution of a Microsoft HTML Help (HH.exe)

rules.title: HackTool - CoercedPotato Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of CoercedPotato, a tool for privilege escalation

rules.title: WhoAmI as Parameter
rules.description: Detects a suspicious process command line that uses whoami as first parameter (as e.g. used by EfsPotato)

rules.title: HackTool - SOAPHound Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of SOAPHound, a .NET tool for collecting Active Directory data, using specific command-line arguments that may indicate an attempt to extract sensitive AD information.

rules.title: HackTool - KrbRelay Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of KrbRelay, a Kerberos relaying tool

rules.title: Potential Privilege Escalation Using Symlink Between Osk and Cmd
rules.description: Detects the creation of a symbolic link between "cmd.exe" and the accessibility on-screen keyboard binary (osk.exe) using "mklink". This technique provides an elevated command prompt to the user from the login screen without the need to log in.

rules.title: Invoke-Obfuscation VAR++ LAUNCHER OBFUSCATION
rules.description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via VAR++ LAUNCHER

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution Of Regasm/Regsvcs With Uncommon Extension
rules.description: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Regasm/Regsvcs utilities with an uncommon extension.

rules.title: Potential PsExec Remote Execution
rules.description: Detects potential psexec command that initiate execution on a remote systems via common commandline flags used by the utility
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious File Encoded To Base64 Via Certutil.EXE
rules.description: Detects the execution of certutil with the "encode" flag to encode a file to base64 where the extensions of the file is suspicious

rules.title: Suspicious DumpMinitool Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious ways to use the "DumpMinitool.exe" binary

rules.title: HackTool - EDRSilencer Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of EDRSilencer, a tool that leverages Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) to block Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents from reporting security events to the server based on PE metadata information.

rules.title: DLL Sideloading by VMware Xfer Utility
rules.description: Detects execution of VMware Xfer utility (VMwareXferlogs.exe) from the non-default directory which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL

rules.title: NewActiveScriptEventConsumer Creation Attempt via Wmic.EXE
rules.description:
Detects the attempt to create an ActiveScriptEventConsumer via WMIC.EXE.
An ActiveScriptEventConsumer is a built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) class that
automatically executes a predefined script (in VBScript or JScript) whenever a specific system event occurs.
Adversaries often abuse ActiveScriptEventConsumer to maintain persistence on a compromised host by executing a malicious script whenever a specific event occurs.
falsepositives: Legitimate software creating script event consumers

rules.title: Renamed Gpg.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "gpg.exe". Often used by ransomware and loaders to decrypt/encrypt data.

rules.title: WMI Persistence - Script Event Consumer
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a script event consumer. When scrcons.exe launches, it does so in response to the creation of an ActiveScriptEventConsumer instance
and will execute registered JScript or VBScript code as a result.
Script event consumers are a built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) class that
automatically executes a predefined script (in VBScript or JScript) whenever a specific system event occurs.
Adversaries often abuse script event consumers to maintain persistence on a compromised host
by executing a malicious script whenever a specific event occurs.
falsepositives: Dell computers on some versions register an event consumer that is known to cause false positives when brightness is changed by the corresponding keyboard button

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Shutdown to Log Out
rules.description: Detects the rare use of the command line tool shutdown to logoff a user

rules.title: 7Zip Compressing Dump Files
rules.description: Detects execution of 7z in order to compress a file with a ".dmp"/".dump" extension, which could be a step in a process of dump file exfiltration.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of 7z with a command line in which ".dmp" or ".dump" appears accidentally
Legitimate use of 7z to compress WER ".dmp" files for troubleshooting

rules.title: Suspicious Runscripthelper.exe
rules.description: Detects execution of powershell scripts via Runscripthelper.exe

rules.title: Installation of WSL Kali-Linux
rules.description:
Detects installation of Kali Linux distribution through Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
Attackers may use Kali Linux WSL to leverage its penetration testing tools and capabilities for malicious purposes.
falsepositives: Legitimate installation or usage of Kali Linux WSL by administrators or security teams

rules.title: Potential LethalHTA Technique Execution
rules.description: Detects potential LethalHTA technique where the "mshta.exe" is spawned by an "svchost.exe" process

rules.title: Windows Binary Executed From WSL
rules.description:
Detects the execution of Windows binaries from within a WSL instance.
This could be used to masquerade parent-child relationships

rules.title: Process Memory Dump via RdrLeakDiag.EXE
rules.description: Detects the use of the Microsoft Windows Resource Leak Diagnostic tool "rdrleakdiag.exe" to dump process memory
authors: Cedric MAURUGEON, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Potential Powershell ReverseShell Connection
rules.description: Detects usage of the "TcpClient" class. Which can be abused to establish remote connections and reverse-shells. As seen used by the Nishang "Invoke-PowerShellTcpOneLine" reverse shell and other.
falsepositives: In rare administrative cases, this function might be used to check network connectivity

rules.title: Renamed Jusched.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a renamed "jusched.exe" as seen used by the cobalt group

rules.title: Powershell Inline Execution From A File
rules.description: Detects inline execution of PowerShell code from a file

rules.title: PUA - Ngrok Execution
rules.description:
Detects the use of Ngrok, a utility used for port forwarding and tunneling, often used by threat actors to make local protected services publicly available.
Involved domains are bin.equinox.io for download and *.ngrok.io for connections.
falsepositives: Another tool that uses the command line switches of Ngrok

rules.title: Conhost.exe CommandLine Path Traversal
rules.description: detects the usage of path traversal in conhost.exe indicating possible command/argument confusion/hijacking

rules.title: Arbitrary File Download Via GfxDownloadWrapper.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of GfxDownloadWrapper.exe with a URL as an argument to download file.

rules.title: Suspicious Active Directory Database Snapshot Via ADExplorer
rules.description: Detects the execution of Sysinternals ADExplorer with the "-snapshot" flag in order to save a local copy of the active directory database to a suspicious directory. This can be used by attackers to extract data for Bloodhound, usernames for password spraying or use the meta data for social engineering. The snapshot doesn't contain password hashes but there have been cases, where administrators put passwords in the comment field.

rules.title: Browser Execution In Headless Mode
rules.description: Detects execution of Chromium based browser in headless mode

rules.title: Suspicious Program Names
rules.description: Detects suspicious patterns in program names or folders that are often found in malicious samples or hacktools
falsepositives: Legitimate tools that accidentally match on the searched patterns

rules.title: Set Suspicious Files as System Files Using Attrib.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of attrib with the "+s" option to set scripts or executables located in suspicious locations as system files to hide them from users and make them unable to be deleted with simple rights. The rule limits the search to specific extensions and directories to avoid FPs

rules.title: Suspicious File Execution From Internet Hosted WebDav Share
rules.description: Detects the execution of the "net use" command to mount a WebDAV server and then immediately execute some content in it. As seen being used in malicious LNK files

rules.title: PUA - DefenderCheck Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of DefenderCheck, a tool to evaluate the signatures used in Microsoft Defender. It can be used to figure out the strings / byte chains used in Microsoft Defender to detect a tool and thus used for AV evasion.

rules.title: Potential Commandline Obfuscation Using Escape Characters
rules.description: Detects potential commandline obfuscation using known escape characters

rules.title: Exports Registry Key To a File
rules.description: Detects the export of the target Registry key to a file.

rules.title: Uninstall Crowdstrike Falcon Sensor
rules.description: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid possible detection of their tools and activities by uninstalling Crowdstrike Falcon
falsepositives: Administrator might leverage the same command line for debugging or other purposes. However this action must be always investigated

rules.title: Renamed Whoami Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of whoami that has been renamed to a different name to avoid detection

rules.title: Windows Share Mount Via Net.EXE
rules.description: Detects when a share is mounted using the "net.exe" utility
falsepositives: Legitimate activity by administrators and scripts

rules.title: PowerShell AppLocker Policy Discovery Via Get-AppLockerPolicy
rules.description: Detects AppLocker policy enumeration attempts via PowerShell using the Get-AppLockerPolicy cmdlet and an policy scope of either Effective, LDAP, or Local.
falsepositives: PowerShell-based AppLocker auditing and policy troubleshooting by administrators.

rules.title: Suspicious GrpConv Execution
rules.description: Detects the suspicious execution of a utility to convert Windows 3.x .grp files or for persistence purposes by malicious software or actors

rules.title: Uncommon Svchost Command Line Parameter
rules.description:
Detects instances of svchost.exe running with an unusual or uncommon command line parameter by excluding known legitimate or common patterns.
This could point at a file masquerading as svchost, a process injection, or hollowing of a legitimate svchost instance.

rules.title: Rundll32 Registered COM Objects
rules.description: load malicious registered COM objects

rules.title: MMC20 Lateral Movement
rules.description: Detects MMC20.Application Lateral Movement; specifically looks for the spawning of the parent MMC.exe with a command line of "-Embedding" as a child of svchost.exe

rules.title: Uncommon  Assistive Technology Applications Execution Via AtBroker.EXE
rules.description: Detects the start of a non built-in assistive technology applications via "Atbroker.EXE".
falsepositives: Legitimate, non-default assistive technology applications execution

rules.title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Process Patterns
rules.description: Detects suspicious process patterns found in logs when CrackMapExec is used

rules.title: Malicious Base64 Encoded PowerShell Keywords in Command Lines
rules.description: Detects base64 encoded strings used in hidden malicious PowerShell command lines

rules.title: Suspicious Command Patterns In Scheduled Task Creation
rules.description: Detects scheduled task creation using "schtasks" that contain potentially suspicious or uncommon commands
falsepositives: Software installers that run from temporary folders and also install scheduled tasks are expected to generate some false positives

rules.title: Potential CobaltStrike Process Patterns
rules.description: Detects potential process patterns related to Cobalt Strike beacon activity
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: HackTool - Bloodhound/Sharphound Execution
rules.description: Detects command line parameters used by Bloodhound and Sharphound hack tools
falsepositives: Other programs that use these command line option and accepts an 'All' parameter

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary File Download Via Cmdl32.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of Cmdl32 with the "/vpn" and "/lan" flags.
Attackers can abuse this utility in order to download arbitrary files via a configuration file.
Inspect the location and the content of the file passed as an argument in order to determine if it is suspicious.

rules.title: PUA - 3Proxy Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of 3proxy, a tiny free proxy server

rules.title: Potential RDP Tunneling Via Plink
rules.description: Execution of plink to perform data exfiltration and tunneling

rules.title: Sdiagnhost Calling Suspicious Child Process
rules.description: Detects sdiagnhost.exe calling a suspicious child process (e.g. used in exploits for Follina / CVE-2022-30190)

rules.title: Renamed AutoIt Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of a renamed AutoIt2.exe or AutoIt3.exe.
AutoIt is a scripting language and automation tool for Windows systems. While primarily used for legitimate automation tasks, it can be misused in cyber attacks.
Attackers can leverage AutoIt to create and distribute malware, including keyloggers, spyware, and botnets. A renamed AutoIt executable is particularly suspicious.

rules.title: Perl Inline Command Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of perl using the "-e"/"-E" flags. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live perl code.

rules.title: PUA - CleanWipe Execution
rules.description: Detects the use of CleanWipe a tool usually used to delete Symantec antivirus.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative use (Should be investigated either way)

rules.title: Visual Studio Code Tunnel Shell Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of a shell (powershell, bash, wsl...) via Visual Studio Code tunnel. Attackers can abuse this functionality to establish a C2 channel and execute arbitrary commands on the system.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Visual Studio Code tunnel and running code from there

rules.title: Non Interactive PowerShell Process Spawned
rules.description: Detects non-interactive PowerShell activity by looking at the "powershell" process with a non-user GUI process such as "explorer.exe" as a parent.
