falsepositives: Likely. Many admin scripts and tools leverage PowerShell in their BAT or VB scripts which may trigger this rule often. It is best to add additional filters or use this to hunt for anomalies

rules.title: Potential PowerShell Console History Access Attempt via History File
rules.description:
Detects potential access attempts to the PowerShell console history directly via history file (ConsoleHost_history.txt).
This can give access to plaintext passwords used in PowerShell commands or used for general reconnaissance.
falsepositives: Legitimate access of the console history file is possible

rules.title: Suspicious Query of MachineGUID
rules.description: Use of reg to get MachineGuid information

rules.title: Forfiles.EXE Child Process Masquerading
rules.description: Detects the execution of "forfiles" from a non-default location, in order to potentially spawn a custom "cmd.exe" from the current working directory.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser
rules.description:
Detects manual execution of the "Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser" task via schtasks.
In order to trigger persistence stored in the "\AppCompatFlags\TelemetryController" registry key.

rules.title: Automated Collection Command Prompt
rules.description: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.

rules.title: Remote CHM File Download/Execution Via HH.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "hh.exe" to execute/download remotely hosted ".chm" files.

rules.title: Sensitive File Access Via Volume Shadow Copy Backup
rules.description: Detects a command that accesses the VolumeShadowCopy in order to extract sensitive files such as the Security or SAM registry hives or the AD database (ntds.dit)
authors: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: LOL-Binary Copied From System Directory
rules.description: Detects a suspicious copy operation that tries to copy a known LOLBIN from system (System32, SysWOW64, WinSxS) directories to another on disk in order to bypass detections based on locations.

rules.title: HackTool - Htran/NATBypass Execution
rules.description: Detects executable names or flags used by Htran or Htran-like tools (e.g. NATBypass)

rules.title: New DNS ServerLevelPluginDll Installed Via Dnscmd.EXE
rules.description: Detects the installation of a DNS plugin DLL via ServerLevelPluginDll parameter in registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DNS server (restart required)

rules.title: Webshell Tool Reconnaissance Activity
rules.description: Detects processes spawned from web servers (PHP, Tomcat, IIS, etc.) that perform reconnaissance looking for the existence of popular scripting tools (perl, python, wget) on the system via the help commands

rules.title: Script Event Consumer Spawning Process
rules.description: Detects a suspicious child process of Script Event Consumer (scrcons.exe).

rules.title: PUA - Nmap/Zenmap Execution
rules.description: Detects usage of namp/zenmap. Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation

rules.title: Suspicious RDP Redirect Using TSCON
rules.description: Detects a suspicious RDP session redirect using tscon.exe

rules.title: Potential Arbitrary DLL Load Using Winword
rules.description: Detects potential DLL sideloading using the Microsoft Office winword process via the '/l' flag.

rules.title: MsiExec Web Install
rules.description: Detects suspicious msiexec process starts with web addresses as parameter
falsepositives: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment

rules.title: Potential RDP Tunneling Via SSH
rules.description: Execution of ssh.exe to perform data exfiltration and tunneling through RDP

rules.title: HackTool - SharpImpersonation Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of the SharpImpersonation tool. Which can be used to manipulate tokens on a Windows computers remotely (PsExec/WmiExec) or interactively
authors: Sai Prashanth Pulisetti @pulisettis, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Scan Loop Network
rules.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for Lateral Movement from the current system

rules.title: Renamed Schtasks Execution
rules.description:
Detects the execution of renamed schtasks.exe binary, which is a legitimate Windows utility used for scheduling tasks.
One of the very common persistence techniques is schedule malicious tasks using schtasks.exe.
Since, it is heavily abused, it is also heavily monitored by security products. To evade detection, threat actors may rename the schtasks.exe binary to schedule their malicious tasks.

rules.title: PktMon.EXE Execution
rules.description: Detects execution of PktMon, a tool that captures network packets.

rules.title: Suspicious Provlaunch.EXE Child Process
rules.description: Detects suspicious child processes of "provlaunch.exe" which might indicate potential abuse to proxy execution.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Office Document Executed From Trusted Location
rules.description: Detects the execution of an Office application that points to a document that is located in a trusted location. Attackers often used this to avoid macro security and execute their malicious code.

rules.title: PUA - AdvancedRun Suspicious Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of AdvancedRun utility in the context of the TrustedInstaller, SYSTEM, Local Service or Network Service accounts

rules.title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag where the script is located in a potentially suspicious location.
falsepositives: False positives may occur if you execute the script from one of the paths mentioned in the rule. Apply additional filters that fits your org needs.

rules.title: Chopper Webshell Process Pattern
rules.description: Detects patterns found in process executions cause by China Chopper like tiny (ASPX) webshells

rules.title: Rar Usage with Password and Compression Level
rules.description: Detects the use of rar.exe, on the command line, to create an archive with password protection or with a specific compression level. This is pretty indicative of malicious actions.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Winrar command line version
Other command line tools, that use these flags

rules.title: Potential ReflectDebugger Content Execution Via WerFault.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "WerFault.exe" with the "-pr" commandline flag that is used to run files stored in the ReflectDebugger key which could be used to store the path to the malware in order to masquerade the execution flow

rules.title: Cloudflared Portable Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the "cloudflared" binary from a non standard location.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of Cloudflared portable versions

rules.title: Disabled IE Security Features
rules.description: Detects command lines that indicate unwanted modifications to registry keys that disable important Internet Explorer security features

rules.title: Suspicious Execution of Powershell with Base64
rules.description: Commandline to launch powershell with a base64 payload

rules.title: Execution of Powershell Script in Public Folder
rules.description: This rule detects execution of PowerShell scripts located in the "C:\Users\Public" folder

rules.title: SyncAppvPublishingServer Execute Arbitrary PowerShell Code
rules.description: Executes arbitrary PowerShell code using SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe.

rules.title: SafeBoot Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to prevent safeboot execution of security products

rules.title: HackTool - PCHunter Execution
rules.description: Detects suspicious use of PCHunter, a tool like Process Hacker to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level stuff

rules.title: Phishing Pattern ISO in Archive
rules.description: Detects cases in which an ISO files is opend within an archiver like 7Zip or Winrar, which is a sign of phishing as threat actors put small ISO files in archives as email attachments to bypass certain filters and protective measures (mark of web)
falsepositives: Legitimate cases in which archives contain ISO or IMG files and the user opens the archive and the image via clicking and not extraction

rules.title: Dumping of Sensitive Hives Via Reg.EXE
rules.description: Detects the usage of "reg.exe" in order to dump sensitive registry hives. This includes SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives.
authors: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Endgame, JHasenbusch, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, frack113
falsepositives: Dumping hives for legitimate purpouse i.e. backup or forensic investigation

rules.title: PowerShell Base64 Encoded FromBase64String Cmdlet
rules.description: Detects usage of a base64 encoded "FromBase64String" cmdlet in a process command line

rules.title: LSASS Process Reconnaissance Via Findstr.EXE
rules.description: Detects findstring commands that include the keyword lsass, which indicates recon actviity for the LSASS process PID

rules.title: HackTool - PurpleSharp Execution
rules.description: Detects the execution of the PurpleSharp adversary simulation tool

rules.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Name As GUID
rules.description: Detects creation of a scheduled task with a GUID like name
falsepositives: Legitimate software naming their tasks as GUIDs

rules.title: New Root Certificate Installed Via CertMgr.EXE
rules.description:
Detects execution of "certmgr" with the "add" flag in order to install a new certificate on the system.
Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.
falsepositives: Help Desk or IT may need to manually add a corporate Root CA on occasion. Need to test if GPO push doesn't trigger FP

rules.title: User Added to Remote Desktop Users Group
rules.description: Detects addition of users to the local Remote Desktop Users group via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".

rules.title: LSASS Dump Keyword In CommandLine
rules.description: Detects the presence of the keywords "lsass" and ".dmp" in the commandline, which could indicate a potential attempt to dump or create a dump of the lsass process.
authors: E.M. Anhaus, Tony Lambert, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Suspicious Copy From or To System Directory
rules.description:
Detects a suspicious copy operation that tries to copy a program from system (System32, SysWOW64, WinSxS) directories to another on disk.
Often used to move LOLBINs such as 'certutil' or 'desktopimgdownldr' to a different location with a different name in order to bypass detections based on locations.
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment (For example an admin scripts like https://www.itexperience.net/sccm-batch-files-and-32-bits-processes-on-64-bits-os/)
When cmd.exe and xcopy.exe are called directly
When the command contains the keywords but not in the correct order

rules.title: Potential Process Hollowing Activity
rules.description: Detects when a memory process image does not match the disk image, indicative of process hollowing.

rules.title: Terminal Server Client Connection History Cleared - Registry
rules.description: Detects the deletion of registry keys containing the MSTSC connection history

rules.title: Folder Removed From Exploit Guard ProtectedFolders List - Registry
rules.description: Detects the removal of folders from the "ProtectedFolders" list of of exploit guard. This could indicate an attacker trying to launch an encryption process or trying to manipulate data inside of the protected folder
falsepositives: Legitimate administrators removing applications (should always be investigated)

value.pattern: ^.*SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\ Defender\\Windows\ Defender\ Exploit\ Guard\\Controlled\ Folder\ Access\\ProtectedFolders.*$

rules.title: RunMRU Registry Key Deletion - Registry
rules.description:
Detects attempts to delete the RunMRU registry key, which stores the history of commands executed via the run dialog.
In the clickfix techniques, the phishing lures instruct users to open a run dialog through (Win + R) and execute malicious commands.
Adversaries may delete this key to cover their tracks after executing commands.

rules.title: Removal Of AMSI Provider Registry Keys
rules.description: Detects the deletion of AMSI provider registry key entries in HKLM\Software\Microsoft\AMSI. This technique could be used by an attacker in order to disable AMSI inspection.

rules.title: Removal Of Index Value to Hide Schedule Task - Registry
rules.description: Detects when the "index" value of a scheduled task is removed or deleted from the registry. Which effectively hides it from any tooling such as "schtasks /query"

rules.title: Windows Recall Feature Enabled - DisableAIDataAnalysis Value Deleted
rules.description:
Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation. Windows Recall can be enabled by deleting the existing "DisableAIDataAnalysis" registry value.
Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities.
This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.

rules.title: Removal of Potential COM Hijacking Registry Keys
rules.description:
Detects any deletion of entries in ".*\shell\open\command" registry keys.
These registry keys might have been used for COM hijacking activities by a threat actor or an attacker and the deletion could indicate steps to remove its tracks.
falsepositives: Legitimate software (un)installations are known to cause false positives. Please add them as a filter when encountered

rules.title: Removal Of SD Value to Hide Schedule Task - Registry
rules.description: Remove SD (Security Descriptor) value in \Schedule\TaskCache\Tree registry hive to hide schedule task. This technique is used by Tarrask malware

rules.title: Windows Credential Guard Related Registry Value Deleted - Registry
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable Windows Credential Guard by deleting registry values. Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may disable Credential Guard to gain access to sensitive credentials stored in the system, such as NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets, which can be used for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

rules.title: Shell Open Registry Keys Manipulation
rules.description:
Detects manipulation of shell open command registry keys such as "ms-settings" and "exefile",
which are commonly abused to achieve UAC bypass (e.g. via fodhelper.exe) or establish persistence
through file association hijacking.

rules.title: Wdigest CredGuard Registry Modification
rules.description:
Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of IsCredGuardEnabled from
HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to disable Cred Guard on a system.
This is usually used with UseLogonCredential to manipulate the caching credentials.

rules.title: Potential Qakbot Registry Activity
rules.description: Detects a registry key used by IceID in a campaign that distributes malicious OneNote files

rules.title: Registry Persistence Mechanisms in Recycle Bin
rules.description: Detects persistence registry keys for Recycle Bin

rules.title: Windows Registry Trust Record Modification
rules.description: Alerts on trust record modification within the registry, indicating usage of macros
falsepositives: This will alert on legitimate macro usage as well, additional tuning is required

rules.title: Office Application Startup - Office Test
rules.description: Detects the addition of office test registry that allows a user to specify an arbitrary DLL that will be executed every time an Office application is started

rules.title: Creation of a Local Hidden User Account by Registry
rules.description: Sysmon registry detection of a local hidden user account.

rules.title: New DLL Added to AppInit_DLLs Registry Key
rules.description: DLLs that are specified in the AppInit_DLLs value in the Registry key HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows are loaded by user32.dll into every process that loads user32.dll

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Via LSASS SilentProcessExit Technique
rules.description: Detects changes to the Registry in which a monitor program gets registered to dump the memory of the lsass.exe process

rules.title: Windows Defender Threat Severity Default Action Modified
rules.description:
Detects modifications or creations of Windows Defender's default threat action settings based on severity to 'allow' or take 'no action'.
This is a highly suspicious configuration change that effectively disables Defender's ability to automatically mitigate threats of a certain severity level,
allowing malicious software to run unimpeded. An attacker might use this technique to bypass defenses before executing payloads.
falsepositives: Legitimate administration via scripts or tools (e.g., SCCM, Intune, GPO enforcement). Correlate with administrative activity.
Software installations that legitimately modify Defender settings (less common for these specific keys).

rules.title: Esentutl Volume Shadow Copy Service Keys
rules.description: Detects the volume shadow copy service initialization and processing via esentutl. Registry keys such as HKLM\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\VSS\\Diag\\VolSnap\\Volume are captured.

rules.title: RedMimicry Winnti Playbook Registry Manipulation
rules.description: Detects actions caused by the RedMimicry Winnti playbook

rules.title: Suspicious Camera and Microphone Access
rules.description: Detects Processes accessing the camera and microphone from suspicious folder
falsepositives: Unlikely, there could be conferencing software running from a Temp folder accessing the devices

rules.title: Path To Screensaver Binary Modified
rules.description: Detects value modification of registry key containing path to binary used as screensaver.

rules.title: New DLL Added to AppCertDlls Registry Key
rules.description:
Dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) that are specified in the AppCertDLLs value in the Registry key can be abused to obtain persistence and privilege escalation
by causing a malicious DLL to be loaded and run in the context of separate processes on the computer.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Via Wsreset
rules.description: Unfixed method for UAC bypass from Windows 10. WSReset.exe file associated with the Windows Store. It will run a binary file contained in a low-privilege registry.

rules.title: Registry Tampering by Potentially Suspicious Processes
rules.description:
Detects suspicious registry modifications made by suspicious processes such as script engine processes such as WScript, or CScript etc.
These processes are rarely used for legitimate registry modifications, and their activity may indicate an attempt to modify the registry
without using standard tools like regedit.exe or reg.exe, potentially for evasion and persistence.
falsepositives: Some legitimate admin or install scripts may use these processes for registry modifications.

rules.title: Disable Security Events Logging Adding Reg Key MiniNt
rules.description: Detects the addition of a key 'MiniNt' to the registry. Upon a reboot, Windows Event Log service will stop writing events.

rules.title: Atbroker Registry Change
rules.description: Detects creation/modification of Assistive Technology applications and persistence with usage of 'at'
falsepositives: Creation of non-default, legitimate at usage

rules.title: Suspicious Run Key from Download
rules.description: Detects the suspicious RUN keys created by software located in Download or temporary Outlook/Internet Explorer directories
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poude (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Software installers downloaded and used by users

rules.title: New PortProxy Registry Entry Added
rules.description: Detects the modification of the PortProxy registry key which is used for port forwarding.
falsepositives: WSL2 network bridge PowerShell script used for WSL/Kubernetes/Docker (e.g. https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/4150#issuecomment-504209723)

rules.title: Windows Credential Editor Registry
rules.description: Detects the use of Windows Credential Editor (WCE)

rules.title: HybridConnectionManager Service Installation - Registry
rules.description: Detects the installation of the Azure Hybrid Connection Manager service to allow remote code execution from Azure function.

rules.title: DLL Load via LSASS
rules.description: Detects a method to load DLL via LSASS process using an undocumented Registry key

rules.title: CMSTP App Paths Registry Key Modification
rules.description:
Detects modifications to the CMSTP App Paths registry key. This may indicate abuse of
Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (CMSTP) for arbitrary code execution or UAC bypass.
falsepositives: Legitimate CMSTP use (unlikely in modern enterprise environments)

rules.title: WINEKEY Registry Modification
rules.description: Detects potential malicious modification of run keys by winekey or team9 backdoor

rules.title: Sticky Key Like Backdoor Usage - Registry
rules.description: Detects the usage and installation of a backdoor that uses an option to register a malicious debugger for built-in tools that are accessible in the login screen

falsepositives: Legitimate modification of the registry key by legitimate program

rules.title: NetNTLM Downgrade Attack - Registry
rules.description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), wagga, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Splunk STRT)
falsepositives: Services or tools that set the values to more restrictive values

rules.title: Security Support Provider (SSP) Added to LSA Configuration
rules.description: Detects the addition of a SSP to the registry. Upon a reboot or API call, SSP DLLs gain access to encrypted and plaintext passwords stored in Windows.

rules.title: Narrator's Feedback-Hub Persistence
rules.description: Detects abusing Windows 10 Narrator's Feedback-Hub

rules.title: Registry Entries For Azorult Malware
rules.description: Detects the presence of a registry key created during Azorult execution

rules.title: New RUN Key Pointing to Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detects suspicious new RUN key element pointing to an executable in a suspicious folder
authors: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Sander Wiebing, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
falsepositives: Software using weird folders for updates

rules.title: Disable Privacy Settings Experience in Registry
rules.description: Detects registry modifications that disable Privacy Settings Experience

rules.title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Using New NetworkProvider - REG
rules.description: Detects when an attacker tries to add a new network provider in order to dump clear text credentials, similar to how the NPPSpy tool does it
falsepositives: Other legitimate network providers used and not filtred in this rule

rules.title: DNS-over-HTTPS Enabled by Registry
rules.description:
Detects when a user enables DNS-over-HTTPS.
This can be used to hide internet activity or be used to hide the process of exfiltrating data.
With this enabled organization will lose visibility into data such as query type, response and originating IP that are used to determine bad actors.

rules.title: COM Hijack via Sdclt
rules.description: Detects changes to 'HKCU\Software\Classes\Folder\shell\open\command\DelegateExecute'

rules.title: Potential EventLog File Location Tampering
rules.description: Detects tampering with EventLog service "file" key. In order to change the default location of an Evtx file. This technique is used to tamper with log collection and alerting

rules.title: Potential WerFault ReflectDebugger Registry Value Abuse
rules.description: Detects potential WerFault "ReflectDebugger" registry value abuse for persistence.

rules.title: UAC Secure Desktop Prompt Disabled
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker tries to change User Account Control (UAC) elevation request destination via the "PromptOnSecureDesktop" value.
The "PromptOnSecureDesktop" setting specifically determines whether UAC prompts are displayed on the secure desktop. The secure desktop is a separate desktop environment that's isolated from other processes running on the system. It's designed to prevent malicious software from intercepting or tampering with UAC prompts.
When "PromptOnSecureDesktop" is set to 0, UAC prompts are displayed on the user's current desktop instead of the secure desktop. This reduces the level of security because it potentially exposes the prompts to manipulation by malicious software.

rules.title: MaxMpxCt Registry Value Changed
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "MaxMpxCt" registry value.
MaxMpxCt specifies the maximum outstanding network requests for the server per client, which is used when negotiating a Server Message Block (SMB) connection with a client. Note if the value is set beyond 125 older Windows 9x clients will fail to negotiate.
Ransomware threat actors and operators (specifically BlackCat) were seen increasing this value in order to handle a higher volume of traffic.

rules.description: Detects when attackers or tools disable Windows Defender functionalities via the Windows registry

When AMSI attempts to starts its COM component, it will query its registered CLSID and return a non-existent COM server. This causes a load failure and prevents any scanning methods from being accessed, ultimately rendering AMSI useless

Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.

rules.title: PUA - Sysinternal Tool Execution - Registry
rules.description: Detects the execution of a Sysinternals Tool via the creation of the "accepteula" registry key

rules.title: Add DisallowRun Execution to Registry

rules.title: NET NGenAssemblyUsageLog Registry Key Tamper
rules.description:
Detects changes to the NGenAssemblyUsageLog registry key.
.NET Usage Log output location can be controlled by setting the NGenAssemblyUsageLog CLR configuration knob in the Registry or by configuring an environment variable (as described in the next section).
By simplify specifying an arbitrary value (e.g. fake output location or junk data) for the expected value, a Usage Log file for the .NET execution context will not be created.

rules.title: Disable Windows Event Logging Via Registry
rules.description: Detects tampering with the "Enabled" registry key in order to disable Windows logging of a Windows event channel
falsepositives: Rare falsepositives may occur from legitimate administrators disabling specific event log for troubleshooting

rules.title: CrashControl CrashDump Disabled
rules.description: Detects disabling the CrashDump per registry (as used by HermeticWiper)

rules.title: Antivirus Filter Driver Disallowed On Dev Drive - Registry
rules.description: Detects activity that indicates a user disabling the ability for Antivirus mini filter to inspect a "Dev Drive".

rules.title: Lsass Full Dump Request Via DumpType Registry Settings
rules.description: Detects the setting of the "DumpType" registry value to "2" which stands for a "Full Dump". Technique such as LSASS Shtinkering requires this value to be "2" in order to dump LSASS.
falsepositives: Legitimate application that needs to do a full dump of their process

rules.title: Suspicious Keyboard Layout Load

falsepositives: Administrators or users that actually use the selected keyboard layouts (heavily depends on the organisation's user base)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via GlobalFlags

rules.title: Allow RDP Remote Assistance Feature
rules.description: Detect enable rdp feature to allow specific user to rdp connect on the targeted machine
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the feature (alerts should be investigated either way)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook LoadMacroProviderOnBoot Setting
rules.description: Detects the modification of Outlook setting "LoadMacroProviderOnBoot" which if enabled allows the automatic loading of any configured VBA project/module

rules.title: Disable Windows Security Center Notifications

rules.title: Lolbas OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe Proxy Download
rules.description:
Detects setting a custom URL for OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe to download a file from the Internet without executing any
anomalous executables with suspicious arguments. The downloaded file will be in C:\Users\redacted\AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive\StandaloneUpdaterreSignInSettingsConfig.json

rules.title: RDP Sensitive Settings Changed
rules.description:
Detects tampering of RDP Terminal Service/Server sensitive settings.
Such as allowing unauthorized users access to a system via the 'fAllowUnsolicited' or enabling RDP via 'fDenyTSConnections', etc.

Below is a list of registry keys/values that are monitored by this rule:

- Shadow: Used to enable Remote Desktop shadowing, which allows an administrator to view or control a user's session.
- DisableRemoteDesktopAntiAlias: Disables anti-aliasing for remote desktop sessions.
- DisableSecuritySettings: Disables certain security settings for Remote Desktop connections.
- fAllowUnsolicited: Allows unsolicited remote assistance offers.
- fAllowUnsolicitedFullControl: Allows unsolicited remote assistance offers with full control.
- InitialProgram: Specifies a program to run automatically when a user logs on to a remote computer.
- ServiceDll: Used in RDP hijacking techniques to specify a custom DLL to be loaded by the Terminal Services service.
- SecurityLayer: Specifies the security layer used for RDP connections.
authors: Samir Bousseaden, David ANDRE, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Nasreddine Bencherchali
falsepositives: Some of the keys mentioned here could be modified by an administrator while setting group policy (it should be investigated either way)

rules.title: ScreenSaver Registry Key Set
rules.description: Detects registry key established after masqueraded .scr file execution using Rundll32 through desk.cpl

rules.title: Suspicious Application Allowed Through Exploit Guard
rules.description: Detects applications being added to the "allowed applications" list of exploit guard in order to bypass controlled folder settings

rules.description: Monitor the creation of a new key under 'TaskCache' when a new scheduled task is registered by a process that is not svchost.exe, which is suspicious

rules.title: UAC Disabled
rules.description: Detects when an attacker tries to disable User Account Control (UAC) by setting the registry value "EnableLUA" to 0.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Today Page
rules.description:
Detects potential persistence activity via outlook today page.
An attacker can set a custom page to execute arbitrary code and link to it via the registry values "URL" and "UserDefinedUrl".
authors: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems), David Bertho (@dbertho) & Eirik Sveen (@0xSV1), Storebrand

rules.title: Sysmon Driver Altitude Change
rules.description:
Detects changes in Sysmon driver altitude value.
If the Sysmon driver is configured to load at an altitude of another registered service, it will fail to load at boot.
falsepositives: Legitimate driver altitude change to hide sysmon

rules.title: PowerShell as a Service in Registry
rules.description: Detects that a powershell code is written to the registry as a service.

rules.title: Enable Remote Connection Between Anonymous Computer - AllowAnonymousCallback
rules.description: Detects enabling of the "AllowAnonymousCallback" registry value, which allows a remote connection between computers that do not have a trust relationship.

rules.title: Potential PendingFileRenameOperations Tampering
rules.description: Detect changes to the "PendingFileRenameOperations" registry key from uncommon or suspicious images locations to stage currently used files for rename or deletion after reboot.
falsepositives: Installers and updaters may set currently in use files for rename or deletion after a reboot.

rules.title: ETW Logging Disabled For SCM
rules.description: Detects changes to the "TracingDisabled" key in order to disable ETW logging for services.exe (SCM)

rules.title: FileFix - Command Evidence in TypedPaths
rules.description: Detects commonly-used chained commands and strings in the most recent 'url' value of the 'TypedPaths' key, which could be indicative of a user being targeted by the FileFix technique.
authors: Alfie Champion (delivr.to), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

rules.title: Default RDP Port Changed to Non Standard Port
rules.description:
Detects changes to the default RDP port.
Remote desktop is a common feature in operating systems. It allows a user to log into a remote system using an interactive session with a graphical user interface.
Microsoft refers to its implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) as Remote Desktop Services (RDS).

rules.title: New BgInfo.EXE Custom DB Path Registry Configuration
rules.description: Detects setting of a new registry database value related to BgInfo configuration. Attackers can for example set this value to save the results of the commands executed by BgInfo in order to exfiltrate information.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of external DB to save the results

rules.title: Persistence Via New SIP Provider
rules.description: Detects when an attacker register a new SIP provider for persistence and defense evasion
falsepositives: Legitimate SIP being registered by the OS or different software.

rules.title: Displaying Hidden Files Feature Disabled
rules.description:
Detects modifications to the "Hidden" and "ShowSuperHidden" explorer registry values in order to disable showing of hidden files and system files.
This technique is abused by several malware families to hide their files from normal users.

rules.title: Registry Hide Function from User
rules.description: Detects registry modifications that hide internal tools or functions from the user (malware like Agent Tesla, Hermetic Wiper uses this technique)

rules.title: Hide Schedule Task Via Index Value Tamper
rules.description:
Detects when the "index" value of a scheduled task is modified from the registry
Which effectively hides it from any tooling such as "schtasks /query" (Read the referenced link for more information about the effects of this technique)

rules.title: UAC Bypass via Sdclt
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using registry key manipulation of sdclt.exe (e.g. UACMe 53)

rules.title: Registry Disable System Restore
rules.description: Detects the modification of the registry to disable a system restore on the computer

rules.title: Registry Modification to Hidden File Extension
rules.description: Hides the file extension through modification of the registry

rules.title: UAC Bypass Using Windows Media Player - Registry
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using Windows Media Player osksupport.dll (UACMe 32)

rules.title: New Application in AppCompat
rules.description: A General detection for a new application in AppCompat. This indicates an application executing for the first time on an endpoint.
falsepositives: This rule is to explore new applications on an endpoint. False positives depends on the organization.

rules.title: ServiceDll Hijack
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "ServiceDLL" value related to a service in the registry.
This is often used as a method of persistence.

rules.title: Potential CobaltStrike Service Installations - Registry
rules.description: Detects known malicious service installs that appear in cases in which a Cobalt Strike beacon elevates privileges or lateral movement.

rules.title: Enable Microsoft Dynamic Data Exchange
rules.description: Enable Dynamic Data Exchange protocol (DDE) in all supported editions of Microsoft Word or Excel.

rules.title: UAC Bypass Abusing Winsat Path Parsing - Registry
rules.description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using a path parsing issue in winsat.exe (UACMe 52)

rules.title: Bypass UAC Using Event Viewer
rules.description: Bypasses User Account Control using Event Viewer and a relevant Windows Registry modification

rules.title: Outlook EnableUnsafeClientMailRules Setting Enabled - Registry
rules.description: Detects an attacker trying to enable the outlook security setting "EnableUnsafeClientMailRules" which allows outlook to run applications or execute macros

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Shim Database In Uncommon Location
rules.description: Detects the installation of a new shim database where the file is located in a non-default location

rules.title: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution - REG
rules.description: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via App Paths Default Property
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "Default" property for keys located in the \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\ registry. Which might be used as a method of persistence
The entries found under App Paths are used primarily for the following purposes.
First, to map an application's executable file name to that file's fully qualified path.
Second, to prepend information to the PATH environment variable on a per-application, per-process basis.
falsepositives: Legitimate applications registering their binary from on of the suspicious locations mentioned above (tune it)

rules.title: Bypass UAC Using SilentCleanup Task
rules.description:
Detects the setting of the environement variable "windir" to a non default value.
Attackers often abuse this variable in order to trigger a UAC bypass via the "SilentCleanup" task.
The SilentCleanup task located in %windir%\system32\cleanmgr.exe is an auto-elevated task that can be abused to elevate any file with administrator privileges without prompting UAC.

rules.title: Windows Credential Guard Disabled - Registry
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable Windows Credential Guard by setting registry values to 0. Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets so that only privileged system software can access them.
Adversaries may disable Credential Guard to gain access to sensitive credentials stored in the system, such as NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets, which can be used for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

rules.title: Potential Registry Persistence Attempt Via Windows Telemetry
rules.description:
Detects potential persistence behavior using the windows telemetry registry key.
Windows telemetry makes use of the binary CompatTelRunner.exe to run a variety of commands and perform the actual telemetry collections.
This binary was created to be easily extensible, and to that end, it relies on the registry to instruct on which commands to run.
The problem is, it will run any arbitrary command without restriction of location or type.

rules.title: Windows Recall Feature Enabled - Registry
rules.description:
Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation. Windows Recall can be enabled by setting the value of "DisableAIDataAnalysis" to "0".
Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities.
This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.

rules.title: Custom File Open Handler Executes PowerShell
rules.description: Detects the abuse of custom file open handler, executing powershell

rules.title: COM Object Hijacking Via Modification Of Default System CLSID Default Value
rules.description: Detects potential COM object hijacking via modification of default system CLSID.

rules.title: Suspicious Space Characters in RunMRU Registry Path - ClickFix
rules.description: Detects the occurrence of numerous space characters in RunMRU registry paths, which may indicate execution via phishing lures using clickfix techniques to hide malicious commands in the Windows Run dialog box from naked eyes.

rules.title: UAC Bypass via Event Viewer
rules.description: Detects UAC bypass method using Windows event viewer

rules.title: Change Winevt Channel Access Permission Via Registry
rules.description: Detects tampering with the "ChannelAccess" registry key in order to change access to Windows event channel.

rules.title: Scripted Diagnostics Turn Off Check Enabled - Registry
rules.description: Detects enabling TurnOffCheck which can be used to bypass defense of MSDT Follina vulnerability

rules.title: Hypervisor Enforced Paging Translation Disabled
rules.description: Detects changes to the "DisableHypervisorEnforcedPagingTranslation" registry value. Where the it is set to "1" in order to disable the Hypervisor Enforced Paging Translation feature.

rules.title: Usage of Renamed Sysinternals Tools - RegistrySet
rules.description: Detects non-sysinternals tools setting the "accepteula" key which normally is set on sysinternals tool execution

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Via Registry
rules.description:
Detects registry value settings that would replace the user's desktop background.
This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
falsepositives: Administrative scripts that change the desktop background to a company logo or other image.

rules.title: Security Event Logging Disabled via MiniNt Registry Key - Registry Set
rules.description:
Detects the addition of the 'MiniNt' key to the registry. Upon a reboot, Windows Event Log service will stop writing events.
Windows Event Log is a service that collects and stores event logs from the operating system and applications. It is an important component of Windows security and auditing.
Adversary may want to disable this service to disable logging of security events which could be used to detect their activities.

rules.title: Windows Hypervisor Enforced Code Integrity Disabled
rules.description: Detects changes to the HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity registry key and the "Enabled" value being set to 0 in order to disable the Hypervisor Enforced Code Integrity feature. This allows an attacker to load unsigned and untrusted code to be run in the kernel
falsepositives: Legitimate system administration tasks that require disabling HVCI for troubleshooting purposes when certain drivers or applications are incompatible with it.

rules.title: Potential Ransomware Activity Using LegalNotice Message
rules.description: Detect changes to the "LegalNoticeCaption" or "LegalNoticeText" registry values where the message set contains keywords often used in ransomware ransom messages

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell In Registry Run Keys
rules.description: Detects potential PowerShell commands or code within registry run keys
falsepositives: Legitimate admin or third party scripts. Baseline according to your environment

rules.title: Suspicious Space Characters in TypedPaths Registry Path - FileFix
rules.description: Detects the occurrence of numerous space characters in TypedPaths registry paths, which may indicate execution via phishing lures using file-fix techniques to hide malicious commands.

rules.title: Disable PUA Protection on Windows Defender
rules.description: Detects disabling Windows Defender PUA protection

rules.title: ETW Logging Disabled For rpcrt4.dll
rules.description: Detects changes to the "ExtErrorInformation" key in order to disable ETW logging for rpcrt4.dll

rules.title: Office Macros Warning Disabled
rules.description: Detects registry changes to Microsoft Office "VBAWarning" to a value of "1" which enables the execution of all macros, whether signed or unsigned.

rules.title: Disable Tamper Protection on Windows Defender
rules.description: Detects disabling Windows Defender Tamper Protection

rules.title: Add Port Monitor Persistence in Registry
rules.description:
Adversaries may use port monitors to run an attacker supplied DLL during system boot for persistence or privilege escalation.
A port monitor can be set through the AddMonitor API call to set a DLL to be loaded at startup.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Excel Add-in - Registry
rules.description: Detect potential persistence via the creation of an excel add-in (XLL) file to make it run automatically when Excel is started.

rules.title: Periodic Backup For System Registry Hives Enabled
rules.description:
Detects the enabling of the "EnablePeriodicBackup" registry value. Once enabled, The OS will backup System registry hives on restarts to the "C:\Windows\System32\config\RegBack" folder. Windows creates a "RegIdleBackup" task to manage subsequent backups.
Registry backup was a default behavior on Windows and was disabled as of "Windows 10, version 1803".
falsepositives: Legitimate need for RegBack feature by administrators.

rules.title: Disable Microsoft Defender Firewall via Registry
rules.description: Adversaries may disable or modify system firewalls in order to bypass controls limiting network usage

rules.title: Potential Registry Persistence Attempt Via DbgManagedDebugger
rules.description: Detects the addition of the "Debugger" value to the "DbgManagedDebugger" key in order to achieve persistence. Which will get invoked when an application crashes
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the key to setup a debugger. Which is often the case on developers machines

rules.title: New BgInfo.EXE Custom VBScript Registry Configuration
rules.description: Detects setting of a new registry value related to BgInfo configuration, which can be abused to execute custom VBScript via "BgInfo.exe"

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Logon Scripts - Registry
rules.description: Detects creation of "UserInitMprLogonScript" registry value which can be used as a persistence method by malicious actors
falsepositives: Investigate the contents of the "UserInitMprLogonScript" value to determine of the added script is legitimate

rules.title: Potential COM Object Hijacking Via TreatAs Subkey - Registry
rules.description: Detects COM object hijacking via TreatAs subkey
falsepositives: Maybe some system utilities in rare cases use linking keys for backward compatibility

rules.title: Modify User Shell Folders Startup Value
rules.description:
Detect modification of the User Shell Folders registry values for Startup or Common Startup which could indicate persistence attempts.
Attackers may modify User Shell Folders registry keys to point to malicious executables or scripts that will be executed during startup.
This technique is often used to maintain persistence on a compromised system by ensuring that the malicious payload is executed automatically.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Visual Studio Tools for Office
rules.description: Detects persistence via Visual Studio Tools for Office (VSTO) add-ins in Office applications.

rules.title: DHCP Callout DLL Installation
rules.description: Detects the installation of a Callout DLL via CalloutDlls and CalloutEnabled parameter in Registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DHCP server (restart required)

rules.title: Suspicious Path In Keyboard Layout IME File Registry Value
rules.description:
Detects usage of Windows Input Method Editor (IME) keyboard layout feature, which allows an attacker to load a DLL into the process after sending the WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST message.
Before doing this, the client needs to register the DLL in a special registry key that is assumed to implement this keyboard layout. This registry key should store a value named "Ime File" with a DLL path.
IMEs are essential for languages that have more characters than can be represented on a standard keyboard, such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

rules.title: Classes Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description:
Detects modification of Windows Registry Classes keys used for persistence.
Adversaries modify these autostart extensibility points (ASEP) to execute malicious code when file types are opened or actions are performed.
Various legitimate software also uses these keys. Currently, this rule only filters out known legitimate software paths,
thus it is recommended to review and tune filters for your environment to reduce false positives before deploying to production.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: Change the Fax Dll
rules.description: Detect possible persistence using Fax DLL load when service restart

rules.title: Suspicious Shell Open Command Registry Modification
rules.description:
Detects modifications to shell open registry keys that point to suspicious locations typically used by malware for persistence.
Generally, modifications to the `*\shell\open\command` registry key can indicate an attempt to change the default action for opening files,
and various UAC bypass or persistence techniques involve modifying these keys to execute malicious scripts or binaries.
falsepositives: Legitimate software installations or updates that modify the shell open command registry keys to these locations.

rules.title: Tamper With Sophos AV Registry Keys
rules.description: Detects tamper attempts to sophos av functionality via registry key modification
falsepositives: Some FP may occur when the feature is disabled by the AV itself, you should always investigate if the action was legitimate

rules.title: Service Binary in Suspicious Folder
rules.description: Detect the creation of a service with a service binary located in a suspicious directory

rules.title: Macro Enabled In A Potentially Suspicious Document
rules.description: Detects registry changes to Office trust records where the path is located in a potentially suspicious location

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Event Viewer Events.asp
rules.description: Detects potential registry persistence technique using the Event Viewer "Events.asp" technique

rules.title: RDP Sensitive Settings Changed to Zero
rules.description:
Detects tampering of RDP Terminal Service/Server sensitive settings.
Such as allowing unauthorized users access to a system via the 'fAllowUnsolicited' or enabling RDP via 'fDenyTSConnections', etc.
authors: Samir Bousseaden, David ANDRE, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Nasreddine Bencherchali
falsepositives: Some of the keys mentioned here could be modified by an administrator while setting group policy (it should be investigated either way)

rules.title: Microsoft Office Protected View Disabled
rules.description: Detects changes to Microsoft Office protected view registry keys with which the attacker disables this feature.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Command Executed Via Run Dialog Box - Registry
rules.description:
Detects execution of commands via the run dialog box on Windows by checking values of the "RunMRU" registry key.
This technique was seen being abused by threat actors to deceive users into pasting and executing malicious commands, often disguised as CAPTCHA verification steps.

rules.title: Internet Explorer Autorun Keys Modification

authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)

Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: Windows Defender Exclusions Added - Registry

rules.title: AMSI Disabled via Registry Modification
rules.description:
Detects attempts to disable AMSI (Anti-Malware Scan Interface) by modifying the AmsiEnable registry value.
Anti-Malware Scan Interface (AMSI) is a security feature in Windows that allows applications and services to integrate with anti-malware products for enhanced protection against malicious content.
Adversaries may attempt to disable AMSI to evade detection by security software, allowing them to execute malicious scripts or code without being scanned.

rules.title: ClickOnce Trust Prompt Tampering
rules.description: Detects changes to the ClickOnce trust prompt registry key in order to enable an installation from different locations such as the Internet.

rules.title: Enabling COR Profiler Environment Variables
rules.description: Detects .NET Framework CLR and .NET Core CLR "cor_enable_profiling" and "cor_profiler" variables being set and configured.
authors: Jose Rodriguez (@Cyb3rPandaH), OTR (Open Threat Research), Jimmy Bayne (@bohops)

rules.title: Wow6432Node CurrentVersion Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: Directory Service Restore Mode(DSRM) Registry Value Tampering
rules.description:
Detects changes to "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" registry value.
During a Domain Controller (DC) promotion, administrators create a Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) local administrator account with a password that rarely changes. The DSRM account is an “Administrator” account that logs in with the DSRM mode when the server is booting up to restore AD backups or recover the server from a failure.
Attackers could abuse DSRM account to maintain their persistence and access to the organization's Active Directory.
If the "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" value is set to "0", the administrator account can only be used if the DC starts in DSRM.
If the "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" value is set to "1", the administrator account can only be used if the local AD DS service is stopped.
If the "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" value is set to "2", the administrator account can always be used.

rules.title: Running Chrome VPN Extensions via the Registry 2 VPN Extension
rules.description: Running Chrome VPN Extensions via the Registry install 2 vpn extension

rules.title: Registry Persistence via Explorer Run Key
rules.description: Detects a possible persistence mechanism using RUN key for Windows Explorer and pointing to a suspicious folder

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via AppCompat RegisterAppRestart Layer
rules.description:
Detects the setting of the REGISTERAPPRESTART compatibility layer on an application.
This compatibility layer allows an application to register for restart using the "RegisterApplicationRestart" API.
This can be potentially abused as a persistence mechanism.
falsepositives: Legitimate applications making use of this feature for compatibility reasons

rules.title: Uncommon Extension In Keyboard Layout IME File Registry Value
rules.description:
Detects usage of Windows Input Method Editor (IME) keyboard layout feature, which allows an attacker to load a DLL into the process after sending the WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST message.
Before doing this, the client needs to register the DLL in a special registry key that is assumed to implement this keyboard layout. This registry key should store a value named "Ime File" with a DLL path.
IMEs are essential for languages that have more characters than can be represented on a standard keyboard, such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
falsepositives: IMEs are essential for languages that have more characters than can be represented on a standard keyboard, such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.

rules.title: Windows Event Log Access Tampering Via Registry
rules.description: Detects changes to the Windows EventLog channel permission values. It focuses on changes to the Security Descriptor Definition Language (SDDL) string, as modifications to these values can restrict access to specific users or groups, potentially aiding in defense evasion by controlling who can view or modify a event log channel. Upon execution, the user shouldn't be able to access the event log channel via the event viewer or via utilities such as "Get-EventLog" or "wevtutil".

rules.title: Office Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description:
Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry. Adversaries may modify these keys to execute malicious code when Office files are opened.
There are various legitimate add-ins that also use these keys and this filter list might not be exhaustive.
Thus, it is recommended to review and tune filters for your environment to reduce false positives before deploying to production.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software or add-in installations and administrative configurations
Automatic registry modifications during legitimate software installations

rules.title: Winlogon Notify Key Logon Persistence
rules.description:
Adversaries may abuse features of Winlogon to execute DLLs and/or executables when a user logs in.
Winlogon.exe is a Windows component responsible for actions at logon/logoff as well as the secure attention sequence (SAS) triggered by Ctrl-Alt-Delete.

rules.title: Suspicious Shim Database Patching Activity
rules.description: Detects installation of new shim databases that try to patch sections of known processes for potential process injection or persistence.

rules.title: ETW Logging Disabled In .NET Processes - Sysmon Registry
rules.description: Potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.

rules.title: Disable Exploit Guard Network Protection on Windows Defender
rules.description: Detects disabling Windows Defender Exploit Guard Network Protection

rules.title: Registry Modification for OCI DLL Redirection
rules.description:
Detects registry modifications related to 'OracleOciLib' and 'OracleOciLibPath' under 'MSDTC' settings.
Threat actors may modify these registry keys to redirect the loading of 'oci.dll' to a malicious DLL, facilitating phantom DLL hijacking via the MSDTC service.

rules.title: Outlook Security Settings Updated - Registry
rules.description: Detects changes to the registry values related to outlook security settings

rules.title: Enable LM Hash Storage
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes.
By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.

rules.title: UAC Notification Disabled
rules.description:
Detects when an attacker tries to disable User Account Control (UAC) notification by tampering with the "UACDisableNotify" value.
UAC is a critical security feature in Windows that prevents unauthorized changes to the operating system. It prompts the user for permission or an administrator password before allowing actions that could affect the system's operation or change settings that affect other users.
When "UACDisableNotify" is set to 1, UAC prompts are suppressed.

rules.title: PUA - Sysinternals Tools Execution - Registry
rules.description: Detects the execution of some potentially unwanted tools such as PsExec, Procdump, etc. (part of the Sysinternals suite) via the creation of the "accepteula" registry key.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of SysInternals tools. Filter the legitimate paths used in your environment

rules.title: Disable Administrative Share Creation at Startup
rules.description: Administrative shares are hidden network shares created by Microsoft Windows NT operating systems that grant system administrators remote access to every disk volume on a network-connected system

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Netsh Helper DLL - Registry
rules.description: Detects changes to the Netsh registry key to add a new DLL value. This change might be an indication of a potential persistence attempt by adding a malicious Netsh helper
falsepositives: Legitimate helper added by different programs and the OS

authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: New BgInfo.EXE Custom WMI Query Registry Configuration
rules.description: Detects setting of a new registry value related to BgInfo configuration, which can be abused to execute custom WMI query via "BgInfo.exe"

rules.title: New Root or CA or AuthRoot Certificate to Store
rules.description: Detects the addition of new root, CA or AuthRoot certificates to the Windows registry

rules.title: Windows Vulnerable Driver Blocklist Disabled
rules.description:
Detects when the Windows Vulnerable Driver Blocklist is set to disabled. This setting is crucial for preventing the loading of known vulnerable drivers,
and its modification may indicate an attempt to bypass security controls. It is often targeted by threat actors to facilitate the installation of malicious or vulnerable drivers,
particularly in scenarios involving Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) bypass techniques.
This rule applies to systems that support the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist feature, including Windows 10 version 1903 and later, and Windows Server 2022 and later.
Note that this change will require a reboot to take effect, and this rule only detects the registry modification action.
falsepositives: Unlikely and should be investigated immediately.

rules.title: Wdigest Enable UseLogonCredential
rules.description: Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of UseLogonCredential from HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to enable clear-text credentials

rules.title: WinSock2 Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: RestrictedAdminMode Registry Value Tampering
rules.description:
Detects changes to the "DisableRestrictedAdmin" registry value in order to disable or enable RestrictedAdmin mode.
RestrictedAdmin mode prevents the transmission of reusable credentials to the remote system to which you connect using Remote Desktop.
This prevents your credentials from being harvested during the initial connection process if the remote server has been compromise

rules.title: Modification of IE Registry Settings
rules.description: Detects modification of the registry settings used for Internet Explorer and other Windows components that use these settings. An attacker can abuse this registry key to add a domain to the trusted sites Zone or insert JavaScript for persistence

rules.title: COM Hijacking via TreatAs

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Outlook Home Page
rules.description:
Detects potential persistence activity via outlook home page.
An attacker can set a home page to achieve code execution and persistence by editing the WebView registry keys.
authors: Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems), David Bertho (@dbertho) & Eirik Sveen (@0xSV1), Storebrand

rules.title: Potential Persistence Using DebugPath
rules.description: Detects potential persistence using Appx DebugPath

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Shim Database Modification
rules.description:
Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.
The Microsoft Windows Application Compatibility Infrastructure/Framework (Application Shim) was created to allow for backward compatibility of software as the operating system codebase changes over time
falsepositives: Legitimate custom SHIM installations will also trigger this rule

rules.title: Suspicious Printer Driver Empty Manufacturer
rules.description: Detects a suspicious printer driver installation with an empty Manufacturer value
falsepositives: Alerts on legitimate printer drivers that do not set any more details in the Manufacturer value

rules.title: Windows Defender Service Disabled - Registry
rules.description: Detects when an attacker or tool disables the  Windows Defender service (WinDefend) via the registry
authors: Ján Trenčanský, frack113, AlertIQ, Nasreddine Bencherchali

rules.title: Disable Internal Tools or Feature in Registry
rules.description: Detects registry modifications that change features of internal Windows tools (malware like Agent Tesla uses this technique)

rules.title: Outlook Macro Execution Without Warning Setting Enabled
rules.description: Detects the modification of Outlook security setting to allow unprompted execution of macros.

rules.title: Change User Account Associated with the FAX Service
rules.description: Detect change of the user account associated with the FAX service to avoid the escalation problem.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious ODBC Driver Registered
rules.description: Detects the registration of a new ODBC driver where the driver is located in a potentially suspicious location

rules.title: New DNS ServerLevelPluginDll Installed
rules.description: Detects the installation of a DNS plugin DLL via ServerLevelPluginDll parameter in registry, which can be used to execute code in context of the DNS server (restart required)

rules.title: Disable Windows Firewall by Registry
rules.description: Detect set EnableFirewall to 0 to disable the Windows firewall

rules.title: System Scripts Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: New Netsh Helper DLL Registered From A Suspicious Location
rules.description: Detects changes to the Netsh registry key to add a new DLL value that is located on a suspicious location. This change might be an indication of a potential persistence attempt by adding a malicious Netsh helper

rules.title: New TimeProviders Registered With Uncommon DLL Name
rules.description:
Detects processes setting a new DLL in DllName in under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\TimeProvider.
Adversaries may abuse time providers to execute DLLs when the system boots.
The Windows Time service (W32Time) enables time synchronization across and within domains.

rules.title: Suspicious Service Installed
rules.description:
Detects installation of NalDrv or PROCEXP152 services via registry-keys to non-system32 folders.
Both services are used in the tool Ghost-In-The-Logs (https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-The-Logs), which uses KDU (https://github.com/hfiref0x/KDU)
falsepositives: Other legimate tools using this service names and drivers. Note - clever attackers may easily bypass this detection by just renaming the services. Therefore just Medium-level and don't rely on it.

rules.title: Potential AutoLogger Sessions Tampering
rules.description:
Detects tampering with autologger trace sessions which is a technique used by attackers to disable logging.
The AutoLogger event tracing session records events up that occur early in the operating system boot process.
Applications and device drivers can use the AutoLogger session to capture traces before the user logs in, and also used by security solutions as telemetry source.
Adversaries may disable these sessions to evade detection and prevent security monitoring of early boot activities and system events.

rules.title: Suspicious Execution Of Renamed Sysinternals Tools - Registry
rules.description: Detects the creation of the "accepteula" key related to the Sysinternals tools being created from executables with the wrong name (e.g. a renamed Sysinternals tool)

rules.title: Common Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split), wagga (name)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: Potential ClickFix Execution Pattern - Registry
rules.description:
Detects potential ClickFix malware execution patterns by monitoring registry modifications in RunMRU keys containing HTTP/HTTPS links.
ClickFix is known to be distributed through phishing campaigns and uses techniques like clipboard hijacking and fake CAPTCHA pages.
Through the fakecaptcha pages, the adversary tricks users into opening the Run dialog box and pasting clipboard-hijacked content,
such as one-liners that execute remotely hosted malicious files or scripts.
falsepositives: Legitimate applications using RunMRU with HTTP links

rules.title: CurrentControlSet Autorun Keys Modification
rules.description: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
authors: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason

rules.title: Uncommon Microsoft Office Trusted Location Added
rules.description: Detects changes to registry keys related to "Trusted Location" of Microsoft Office where the path is set to something uncommon. Attackers might add additional trusted locations to avoid macro security restrictions.
falsepositives: Other unknown legitimate or custom paths need to be filtered to avoid false positives

rules.title: Winlogon AllowMultipleTSSessions Enable
rules.description:
Detects when the 'AllowMultipleTSSessions' value is enabled.
Which allows for multiple Remote Desktop connection sessions to be opened at once.
This is often used by attacker as a way to connect to an RDP session without disconnecting the other users
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the multi session functionality

rules.title: Hiding User Account Via SpecialAccounts Registry Key
rules.description: Detects modifications to the registry key "HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\Userlist" where the value is set to "0" in order to hide user account from being listed on the logon screen.

rules.title: Execution DLL of Choice Using WAB.EXE
rules.description: This rule detects that the path to the DLL written in the registry is different from the default one. Launched WAB.exe tries to load the DLL from Registry.

rules.title: Disabled Windows Defender Eventlog
rules.description: Detects the disabling of the Windows Defender eventlog as seen in relation to Lockbit 3.0 infections
falsepositives: Other Antivirus software installations could cause Windows to disable that eventlog (unknown)

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Custom Protocol Handler
rules.description: Detects potential persistence activity via the registering of a new custom protocole handlers. While legitimate applications register protocole handlers often times during installation. And attacker can abuse this by setting a custom handler to be used as a persistence mechanism.
falsepositives: Many legitimate applications can register a new custom protocol handler. Additional filters needs to applied according to your environment.

rules.title: Potential Persistence Via Scrobj.dll COM Hijacking
rules.description: Detect use of scrobj.dll as this DLL looks for the ScriptletURL key to get the location of the script to execute

rules.title: PowerShell Logging Disabled Via Registry Key Tampering
rules.description: Detects changes to the registry for the currently logged-in user. In order to disable PowerShell module logging, script block logging or transcription and script execution logging
